items.label: Born in Curitiba, Paraná, Brazil
items.detail: Nicolle Angélica Caliari was born Nov. 4, 1996 in Curitiba. She is 29 as of Oct. 21, 2026 and fights out of Florianópolis, Santa Catarina after relocating during her regional MMA career.
items.sourceLabel: UFC roster biography and Sherdog birthdate

items.label: Begins karate at her father's suggestion
items.detail: Caliari says her father enrolled her in karate for physical activity and self-defense. Initially reluctant, she grew to enjoy training after placing in youth competitions. The calendar range follows her Nov. 1996 birthday; the exact enrollment date is unknown.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete questionnaire and 2024 firsthand interview

items.label: Wins Brazilian, Paraná and world karate competitions
items.detail: Caliari's UFC questionnaire lists Brazilian and Paraná state karate championships and a karate world title, but not the event editions, age categories, exact dates or opponents. These are karate credentials, not professional MMA titles.

items.label: Switches from karate toward Muay Thai and later BJJ
items.detail: Seeking more full-contact competition, Caliari took up Muay Thai as a teenager and added Brazilian jiu-jitsu as she moved toward MMA. UFC lists a brown karate belt, Muay Thai ranks and a purple BJJ belt, without belt-award dates.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter questionnaire / Globo 2017 athlete interview

items.label: Studies law but later leaves during final year
items.detail: Caliari says she attended law school and quit in the final year when she had to choose between a legal career and professional fighting. The UFC questionnaire confirms the decision but does not date the withdrawal precisely.

items.label: WIN · Morgana de Cassia Silva · TKO (punches) · R1 time not officially recorded
items.detail: At Imortal FC 2: Kamikaze in Curitiba, Caliari defeated Morgana de Cassia Silva by tko (punches). The event lists round one, but no reliable stoppage clock is available. Her official professional MMA debut. The win made her 1-0; the stoppage clock is not reliably provided.

items.label: LOSS · Syuri Kondo · Unanimous decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At Pancrase 279 in Japan, Caliari lost to Syuri Kondo by unanimous decision. The fight went the scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Caliari traveled to Japan for her second pro fight; Kondo handed her first loss and brought her to 1-1.

items.label: WIN · Edna Oliveira Ajala · TKO (punches) · R2 4:56
items.detail: At Adventure Fighters Tournament 9, Caliari defeated Edna Oliveira Ajala by tko (punches). The finish came at 4:56 of round 2. Returned to winning and improved to 2-1.

items.label: WIN · Thuany Valentim Fernandes · KO (punches) · R1 4:05
items.detail: At Curitiba Top Fight 11: Girls' Night, Caliari defeated Thuany Valentim Fernandes by ko (punches). The finish came at 4:05 of round 1. A first-round KO in Curitiba, professional record 3-1.

items.label: Discusses Muay Thai, female representation and becoming a fighter
items.detail: A Globo Paraná feature discussed Caliari as a professional MMA athlete with a background in karate and Muay Thai. The source confirms her public involvement in women's combat sports in this period, not a specific championship outcome.
items.sourceLabel: Globo Paraná profile of Nicolle Caliari

items.label: WIN · Itzel Esquivel · TKO (punches) · R2 3:56
items.detail: At LFA 26 in Houston, Texas, Caliari defeated Itzel Esquivel by tko (punches). The finish came at 3:56 of round 2. First Legacy Fighting Alliance bout and third straight KO/TKO victory. She improved to 4-1.

items.label: Almost 23 months between completed MMA fights
items.detail: No completed professional MMA bout appears between her November 2017 LFA victory and October 2019 Invicta return. She later spoke more broadly about the challenge of finding sustainable progress in the sport; no specific diagnosed injury explains this entire interval.

items.label: LOSS · Kay Hansen · Submission (guillotine choke) · R3 1:14
items.detail: At Invicta FC 37 in Kansas City, Kansas, Caliari lost to Kay Hansen by submission (guillotine choke). The finish came at 1:14 of round 3. Caliari returned after 23 months and lost to Hansen. MMA Fighting and Sherdog record a guillotine choke; Tapology calls the same finish a neck crank from mount. The method is recorded as disputed across databases, with the official Invicta event report favoring guillotine.
items.sourceLabel: Original promotion report / corroborating fight record

items.label: Invicta names Hansen vs. Caliari Fight of the Night
items.detail: Invicta FC later released the complete Oct. 4, 2019 Hansen vs. Caliari fight as a Fight of the Night selection. That accolade is separate from the official loss by submission and is not a UFC bonus.
items.sourceLabel: Invicta official full-fight archive, published Apr. 2023

items.label: Two-year inactivity period after Invicta loss
items.detail: The records show no completed professional fight between the Oct. 4, 2019 Kay Hansen loss and Oct. 23, 2021 victory over Midian Fernandes Vicente. Archived 2021 bookings were canceled, but there is no verified single injury diagnosis or anti-doping suspension accounting for the whole period.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog professional bouts / Tapology scheduling archive

items.label: Nação Cyborg 8 booking with Vanessa Guimarães does not occur
items.detail: The planned Nação Cyborg 8 matchup with Vanessa Guimarães was canceled with the event. This is a booking, not another loss or a recordable professional bout.

items.label: Considers quitting MMA because the sport is not financially sustainable
items.detail: In a 2024 interview, Caliari recalled that by 2021 she had considered abandoning MMA after extensive work and little financial return. This was a career decision point she described in retrospect, not evidence of a medical or disciplinary absence.

items.label: Proposed Bruna Brasil and Mayara Thays matchups canceled
items.detail: Nação Cyborg 10 archives list canceled proposed matchups with both Bruna Brasil and Mayara Thays. Neither was fought on Oct. 21. The same card's two opponent listings must not be added as completed fights or counted as multiple withdrawals without evidence.

items.label: WIN · Midian Fernandes Vicente · TKO (punches) · R1 3:45
items.detail: At Face the Danger 23 in Brazil, Caliari defeated Midian Fernandes Vicente by tko (punches). The finish came at 3:45 of round 1. Caliari returned to competition, improving to 5-2 after roughly two years away.

items.label: Almost 22-month gap before returning in Fight Music Show
items.detail: The record contains no completed MMA bout between Oct. 23, 2021 and Aug. 26, 2023. In later interviews she discussed almost leaving the sport, limited financial return, and seeking a new coaching plan. It would be inaccurate to attribute the entire period to an unverified physical injury.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog bout history and 2024 profile interview

items.label: Angela Rosa bout does not take place
items.detail: A proposed MF promotion matchup with Angela Rosa appears among canceled regional bookings. No opponent replacement, health condition or fight result was confirmed by the archived match listing.

items.label: Coaches women's Muay Thai and helps manage a gym
items.detail: Caliari says she taught Muay Thai classes for women through 2022 and worked on the administrative/operational side of a gym in which she was a partner. The work accompanied her fighting career and explains the obligations she later left when relocating.

items.label: Moves from Curitiba to Florianópolis for Thai Brasil camp
items.detail: After seriously considering leaving MMA, Caliari accepted a plan from coach Márcio Malko and relocated from Curitiba to Florianópolis, joining Thai Brasil. Malko identified needed technical improvements and targeted a route to the UFC within about one year. She left her previous business routine and felt isolated away from family, according to her 2024 interview. No exact moving day is confirmed.

items.label: Focuses on aggressive finishes to improve UFC prospects
items.detail: Malko told Caliari that emphatic finishes, rather than merely winning decisions, would improve her chance of receiving a Contender Series opportunity. She completed an intensive camp program in Florianópolis. This explains the change in how she approached fight opportunities; it is not a separate MMA win.
items.sourceLabel: UmDois Esportes interview with fighter, Oct. 15, 2024

items.label: WIN · Carolina Jiménez · Submission (armbar) · R2 4:50
items.detail: At Fight Music Show 3 in Brazil, Caliari defeated Carolina Jiménez by submission (armbar). The finish came at 4:50 of round 2. Her first completed fight after moving in 2023. The win moved her to 6-2. Tapology gives 4:51, while Sherdog lists 4:50; the one-second discrepancy has not been conclusively resolved.

items.label: WIN · Daniella Antonelli · Submission (rear-naked choke) · R2 3:34
items.detail: At Fight Music Show: Fight Night 2, Caliari defeated Daniella Antonelli by submission (rear-naked choke). The finish came at 3:34 of round 2. A second consecutive round-two submission victory, taking her to 7-2. Some databases refer to this opponent as Daniella Oliveira or Daniella Oliveira Antonelli; Sherdog uses Daniella Antonelli.

items.label: Receives DWCS opportunity with roughly three months to prepare
items.detail: Caliari said in an October 2024 interview that her Sept. 10 Contender Series invitation arrived roughly three months in advance. She trained two to three sessions daily and worked on the mental side of preparation, while acknowledging pre-fight nerves. June is approximate, not a verified invitation day.

items.label: WIN · Corinne Laframboise · Submission (armbar) · R1 4:45
items.detail: At Dana White's Contender Series Season 8, Week 5, Caliari defeated Corinne Laframboise by submission (armbar). The finish came at 4:45 of round 1. Finished her Canadian opponent in the closing seconds of round one to reach 8-2. The DWCS win counts in the professional MMA record but precedes her official Octagon debut.

items.label: Earns UFC contract from Contender Series victory
items.detail: Dana White awarded Caliari a UFC contract after the first-round armbar over Corinne Laframboise. She reached the promotion on three straight submission wins following her 2023 relocation. Contract date tracks the broadcast, not an unspecified private signing day.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete career summary and 2024 firsthand interview

items.label: Discusses difficult move, loneliness and prior retirement thoughts
items.detail: In a lengthy Brazilian interview, Caliari described having nearly quit MMA, feeling isolated from her family after moving to Florianópolis, and becoming emotional during the uncertain road to UFC qualification. She explained that the training plan under Márcio Malko was what changed her direction. These are self-reported personal experiences, not diagnoses inferred from the fight record.

items.label: LOSS · Ernesta Kareckaitė · Split decision · R3 5:00
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2 in Las Vegas, Caliari lost to Ernesta Kareckaitė by split decision. The fight went the scheduled 3 rounds; 5:00 is the final bell. Official UFC debut at flyweight, ending her submission winning streak. Sherdog, fight-by-fight databases and contemporaneous UFC media report a SPLIT decision, despite one UFC fighter-summary line incorrectly saying unanimous.

items.label: Disputes judging and discusses difficulties making strawweight
items.detail: Caliari said she thought she won rounds one and three against Kareckaitė, and questioned why two apparent fence grabs drew no point deduction. In the same interview, she explained she had previously struggled to reach 115 pounds while maintaining adequate energy, which was why she chose flyweight. These are her post-fight claims, not official overturned results.

items.label: LOSS · Carli Judice · TKO (knee to body and punches) · R3 1:30
items.detail: At UFC 318 in New Orleans, Caliari lost to Carli Judice by tko (knee to body and punches). The finish came at 1:30 of round 3. Judice landed a damaging knee to the liver/body and follow-up punches for the stoppage. Caliari fell to 8-4 overall and 0-2 in regular UFC fights.

items.label: Rebuilds body composition to make strawweight
items.detail: After two UFC flyweight losses, Caliari and her support team spent about six months preparing to move back to 115 pounds. In her May 14 interview she said the program reduced strength-training loads, altered protein intake and focused on reducing muscle mass under professional supervision. No exact program start day is documented.

items.label: Undergoes breast implant removal to facilitate 115-pound cut
items.detail: Caliari told Ag. Fight she had breast implants removed because the added weight complicated her move from 125 to 115 pounds. The procedure occurred before the May 14, 2026 interview; the exact surgery date and postoperative details are not public. This was an intentional career/body-composition decision, not a reported fight injury.
items.sourceLabel: Ag. Fight firsthand interview on implant removal, May 14

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled March 28 fight with Carol Foro
items.detail: Ag. Fight reported the replacement by Stephanie Luciano on Jan. 29, well before the March 28 Seattle event. UFC's Mar. 25 recap later stated Caliari had been injured and withdrawn. No precise body part, medical diagnosis, surgery or rehabilitation timetable is established; the bout was never contested. The Jan. 29 announcement corrects timelines that date the withdrawal itself to March.
items.sourceLabel: Ag. Fight Jan. 29 replacement report / UFC Mar. 25 injury description

items.label: Explains 115-pound switch and implant-removal decision publicly
items.detail: Ahead of the Shauna Bannon fight, Caliari explained the roughly six-month program and said she believed the smaller opponents at strawweight would allow her to compete with greater strength and less physical disadvantage. These are her expectations rather than evidence of a performance outcome.

items.label: Successfully weighs 115.5 pounds for first UFC strawweight fight
items.detail: Caliari officially weighed 115.5 lb for Shauna Bannon at UFC Vegas 117, within the 116-pound non-title strawweight allowance. Bannon also weighed 115.5 lb. This confirms a successful weigh-in at the NEW class, not an October UFC 333 weigh-in.

items.label: WIN · Shauna Bannon · Submission (arm-triangle choke) · R3 3:08
items.detail: At UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa (UFC Vegas 117), Caliari defeated Shauna Bannon by submission (arm-triangle choke). The finish came at 3:08 of round 3. First UFC victory and first UFC bout at strawweight, improving to 9-4 overall and 1-2 UFC. It was her fourth pro submission and her ninth consecutive stoppage win in nine career victories, with five other wins by KO/TKO.

items.label: Credits Ronda Rousey for influencing her judo throws
items.detail: After beating Bannon, Caliari described using the harai goshi-style hip/leg sweep she had admired watching Ronda Rousey's UFC run. She secured takedowns before eventually finishing Bannon with a third-round arm triangle (katagatame). This is a technical influence she acknowledged, not evidence Rousey was her personal coach.

items.label: Maintains Thai Brasil Floripa affiliation
items.detail: UFC and Sherdog list Thai Brasil Floripa, with Márcio Malko as a key coach. Caliari's 2023 move to Florianópolis is documented; no verified permanent 2026 return to Curitiba or new training team has been reported.
items.sourceLabel: UFC current athlete profile and Sherdog team listing

items.label: Lucindo vs. Caliari scheduled for UFC 333
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported the all-Brazilian Oct. 24 strawweight contest in Abu Dhabi on Oct. 1, citing sources close to matchmaking. Caliari enters 9-4 (1-2 UFC) off the May arm-triangle win and Lucindo enters 18-6 (5-2 UFC).

items.label: UFC Brazil confirms 29-year-old strawweight on Abu Dhabi card
items.detail: UFC's Brazilian fighter overview lists Caliari as born in Curitiba, 29 years old, a 9-4 professional record, and newly established at 115 pounds following her win over Bannon. This confirms her roster division and scheduled opponent, not the Oct. 24 result.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Brazil Oct. 17 UFC 333 fighters overview

items.label: UFC preview confirms Lucindo matchup as opening bout
items.detail: The UFC's official fight-by-fight preview describes Caliari vs Iasmin Lucindo as the opening fight at UFC 333, an all-Brazilian women's strawweight pairing. The entire early preliminary segment begins at 10 a.m. Eastern / 9 a.m. Central / 6 p.m. Abu Dhabi local time; no independently fixed individual walkout time is published.

items.label: Enters UFC 333 with nine finishes and first strawweight win
items.detail: Caliari enters Abu Dhabi with 9 wins from 13 professional fights, five KO/TKOs and four submissions, all victories inside the distance. Her most recent fight was May 16 at strawweight, so no October injury status, successful UFC 333 weigh-in or fight result is independently verified yet.

items.label: UFC 333 · women's strawweight vs. Iasmin Lucindo
items.detail: Nicolle Caliari (9-4 overall, 1-2 UFC) is scheduled against Iasmin Lucindo (18-6 overall, 5-2 UFC) at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on Saturday, Oct. 24. The UFC advertises it as the opening bout; early prelims begin at 10 a.m. ET / 9 a.m. CT / 6 p.m. UAE local. This is a segment start, not a confirmed personal cage-walk clock. No result is recorded as of Oct. 21.

audit.scope: Full 13-bout professional chronology 9-4 with all dated matches, methods, rounds and verified clocks (2015 debut finish time unavailable), 5 KO/TKO and 4 submission wins, conflicting 2019 Hansen guillotine vs neck crank classification, 2023 Carolina Jimenez one-second clock difference, three documented near-two-year inactive spans not assigned fabricated injury diagnoses; karate age nine, youth titles without unverified medal dates, Muay Thai age 15 and BJJ credentials, unfinished law degree, women's Muay Thai teaching and gym administration through 2022, 2021 near-retirement, exact 2023 Curitiba-to-Florianopolis Thai Brasil relocation under Marcio Malko and Fight Music Show rebound, Sept 2024 DWCS armbar and UFC signing; Jan 2025 UFC debut split-decision loss to Ernesta Kareckaite (UFC Q&A typo says unanimous), post-fight scoring reaction, Jul 2025 Judice TKO; six-month body-composition restructuring and reported implant removal before May 14 2026; Jan 29 cancellation of March 28 Carol Foro fight with generic UFC injury statement but no diagnosis; May 15 2026 compliant 115.5-lb official weigh-in for first strawweight bout; May 16 first UFC victory Shauna Bannon R3 3:08, Ronda Rousey inspired harai goshi and May 18 interview; Oct 1 UFC 333 booking, Oct 17/19 UFC event confirmation, Oct 24 scheduled Lucindo fight without pre-emptive weigh-in/outcome. Team remains Thai Brasil Floripa, no verified doping suspension or permanent new coach.

items.label: WIN · João Paulo Rodrigues de Souza

items.label: WIN · Eduardo Felipe

items.label: WIN · João Luiz Nogueira
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision at Jungle Fight 25; moved to 4–0.

items.label: WIN · Iliarde Santos
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision at Jungle Fight 29; moved to 5–0.

items.label: DRAW · Felipe Froes
items.detail: Fought to a majority draw over three rounds at Shooto Brazil 36, the only draw on his professional record.

items.label: WIN · Mauro Chaulet
items.detail: Submitted Chaulet by rear-naked choke at 2:53 of round two at Jungle Fight 50.

items.label: WIN · Nilson Pereira

items.label: WIN · Ismael Bonfim · interim Jungle Fight featherweight title

items.label: WIN · Tom Niinimäki · UFC debut
items.detail: Submitted Niinimäki via rear-naked choke at 3:30 of round two in his first UFC appearance.

items.label: WIN · Zubaira Tukhugov
items.detail: Took a split decision at UFC 198, keeping his undefeated professional record intact.

items.label: WIN · Jeremy Stephens
items.detail: Won a split decision against Stephens at UFC on FOX 24 in a high-profile featherweight matchup.

items.label: LOSS · Brian Ortega
items.detail: Suffered his first professional defeat when Ortega caught a guillotine choke at 2:59 of round three at UFC 214. This finish time is confirmed by Sherdog and the event report, despite the UFC athlete bio listing 3:29.

items.label: WIN · Calvin Kattar
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision over Kattar at UFC 223.

items.label: WIN · Cub Swanson
items.detail: Submitted Swanson by rear-naked choke at 4:15 of round one at UFC 227.

items.label: LOSS · José Aldo
items.detail: Lost by TKO (punches) at 0:44 of round two in Fortaleza, Brazil.

items.label: LOSS · Chan Sung Jung
items.detail: Lost by TKO (punches) after 58 seconds of round one in a UFC featherweight main event against 'The Korean Zombie'.

items.label: WIN · Damir Hadžović · lightweight run begins
items.detail: Moved from featherweight to lightweight and finished Hadžović by rear-naked choke just 44 seconds into round one.

items.label: LOSS · Rafael Fiziev
items.detail: Knocked out with punches at 4:05 of round one at UFC 256.

items.label: WIN · Jai Herbert
items.detail: Used takedowns and top control to set up a rear-naked choke at 4:34 of round two. UFC event results and Sherdog report 4:34; the UFC athlete bio lists 4:36.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Hernandez
items.detail: Submitted Hernandez by rear-naked choke at 1:23 of round two at UFC 271.

items.label: LOSS · Rafael dos Anjos · short-notice five-round fight
items.detail: Stepped into a five-round bout on short notice at UFC 272 and lost by unanimous decision.

items.label: WIN · Brad Riddell
items.detail: Submitted Riddell by rear-naked choke at 3:20 of round one at UFC 281.

items.label: WIN · Drew Dober
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision, relying heavily on takedowns and top control.

items.label: WIN · Jalin Turner · UFC 300
items.detail: Recovered from a difficult first round and finished Turner with elbows and punches at 4:11 of round two at UFC 300.

items.label: WIN · Benoît Saint Denis · Paris main event
items.detail: Won by doctor stoppage at the end of round two of their Paris main event, having inflicted extensive damage with ground strikes.

items.label: UFC 311 bout changed · next-day lightweight title opportunity
items.detail: The UFC announced that Moicano would replace injured Arman Tsarukyan against Islam Makhachev for the UFC lightweight championship the next day. Moicano had originally been booked against Beneil Dariush on that card.

items.label: LOSS · Islam Makhachev · UFC title challenge
items.detail: Challenged Makhachev for the UFC lightweight title at UFC 311 on one day's notice after Arman Tsarukyan withdrew. Submitted by brabo/D'Arce choke at 4:05 of round one.

items.label: LOSS · Beneil Dariush
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision at UFC 317, his second consecutive defeat.

items.label: WIN · Chris Duncan
items.detail: Returned with a second-round submission at 3:14 in the main event. UFC records a rear-naked choke, while Sherdog describes a face crank.

items.label: Brian Ortega bout cancelled; Moicano–Nolan headliner announced
items.detail: Moicano had been booked to face Brian Ortega at UFC 331. The UFC removed the bout following Ortega's injury and announced Nolan as Moicano's October 31 main-event opponent.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Tom Nolan
items.detail: Booked opposite Australian lightweight Tom Nolan in the October 31 main event; result not yet known.

Tom Nolan.name: Tom Nolan
Tom Nolan.subtitle: Career chronology · 12 professional bouts and 8 documented amateur bouts

items.label: Begins martial arts training
items.detail: Began martial arts training at age 14 to learn self-defense and improve his wrestling for rugby league. His UFC biography also identifies his later Muay Thai black rank.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Scott MacGregor · first recorded MMA bout
items.detail: Opened his documented amateur MMA career with a three-round decision at Eternal MMA 22. Sherdog calls it a split decision; several other bout databases report a unanimous decision, so the winning result is clear but the judging classification differs.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog amateur history; other results databases differ on decision type

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Ryan Bishop
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision at Eternal MMA 24. The contemporary Australian event report and Tapology agree on unanimous, while Sherdog lists split.
items.sourceLabel: Contemporary Fight News Australia event report

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Ruuben Suits
items.detail: Defeated Suits by unanimous decision at XFC 30 after three three-minute rounds.

items.label: AMATEUR NO CONTEST · Pati (Ropati) Lemai
items.detail: An accidental eye poke ended Nolan's Eternal MMA 26 fight with Lemai in the first round, producing a no contest; some sources list the opponent as Ropati Lemai.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Joshua Francois · wins XFC featherweight title
items.detail: Stopped Francois by first-round TKO at 3:00 at XFC 32 to win the XFC amateur featherweight championship. This fight is missing from Sherdog's amateur ledger, but contemporary results document it and help reconcile his UFC-reported 6–1, 1 NC amateur record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Brandon Stowers · XFC title defense
items.detail: Successfully defended the XFC amateur featherweight championship at XFC 34, submitting Stowers with a rear-naked choke at 1:34 of round two. Contemporary results list Nolan as the defending champion.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Aaren McConnell · loses XFC featherweight title
items.detail: Lost the XFC amateur featherweight championship to McConnell by TKO (strikes) at 0:45 of round three at XFC 36. This was Nolan's only recorded amateur defeat.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Mitch Bayliss · spinning-back-kick TKO
items.detail: Finished Bayliss with a spinning back kick at 0:20 of round three at Eternal MMA 42. Contemporary Australian reporting identifies the stoppage as a TKO; Sherdog also places it in round three at 0:20. Some later records incorrectly list round one at 1:41.
items.sourceLabel: Fight News Australia · Eternal MMA 42 results (2019)

items.label: Amateur career concludes · 6–1, 1 NC; two XFC championships
items.detail: Nolan completed his documented amateur run at 6–1 with one no contest across eight bouts. His official UFC profile credits him as a two-time amateur XFC champion; his 2017 Francois title win, 2018 Stowers defense and 2018 McConnell title loss are separately documented above. Sherdog omits the Francois victory.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete profile; contemporary XFC event results

items.label: WIN · Sam Flint · professional debut
items.detail: Turned professional with a three-round unanimous-decision victory over Flint at XFC 46: State of Origin.

items.label: Earns Brazilian jiu-jitsu brown belt
items.detail: Nolan says he earned his BJJ brown belt in 2021. UFC also lists him as holding a Muay Thai black rank, while he continued training with Team Compton Training Centre.

items.label: WIN · Trevor Sinclair
items.detail: Defeated Sinclair by unanimous decision after three rounds at Eternal MMA 63 on the Gold Coast.

items.label: WIN · Niam Stephen
items.detail: Stopped Stephen with punches at 3:54 of round one at Eternal MMA 67, his first recorded professional finish.

items.label: WIN · Adam Cook
items.detail: Stopped Cook with punches and a knee at 3:58 of round two at Eternal MMA 72, improving to 4–0 as a professional.

items.label: WIN · Aidan Aguilera
items.detail: Finished Aguilera with a knee and follow-up punches at 2:22 of round one at Eternal MMA 74. Entered Contender Series with a 5–0 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Bogdan Grad · Contender Series contract
items.detail: Knocked out Grad with a left hand at 1:23 of the first round on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 7, Week 1. Nolan entered 6–0 as a professional and earned a UFC contract after the finish.

items.label: LOSS · Nikolas Motta · UFC debut
items.detail: Was stopped with punches at 1:03 of round one in his Octagon debut at UFC Fight Night: Ankalaev vs. Walker 2, his first professional defeat.

items.label: WIN · Victor Martinez
items.detail: Bounced back from the Motta loss with a first-round TKO, landing a knee to the body and follow-up punches at 3:50 against Martinez.

items.label: WIN · Alex Reyes
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision against Reyes at UFC 305 in Perth, extending his UFC winning run to two.

items.label: WIN · Viacheslav Borshchev
items.detail: Beat the experienced kickboxer by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC 312 in Sydney, moving to three straight UFC victories.

items.label: Charlie Campbell replaces injured Evan Elder for UFC Perth
items.detail: Nolan's originally booked opponent, Evan Elder, withdrew with a leg injury in early September. Charlie Campbell stepped in for the September 27 Perth fight.

items.label: WIN · Charlie Campbell · first pro submission and UFC bonus
items.detail: After being knocked down early, Nolan rallied and submitted Campbell by rear-naked choke at 4:08 of round one in Perth. It was his first professional submission victory and earned him a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus, extending his UFC win streak to four.

items.label: WIN · Farès Ziam · fifth consecutive UFC victory
items.detail: Defeated Ziam by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Muhammad vs. Bonfim in Las Vegas. All three judges scored it 29–28 for Nolan, extending his UFC winning streak to five ahead of his first main-event booking.

items.label: Booked for first UFC main event against Moicano
items.detail: After Brian Ortega withdrew injured from a UFC 331 fight with Renato Moicano, the UFC announced Nolan as Moicano's October 31 main-event opponent. Nolan entered the booking on five straight UFC wins.

items.label: First UFC main event · scheduled vs. Renato Moicano
items.detail: Scheduled for his first UFC main event, a five-round lightweight bout against Renato Moicano at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. No result has occurred or been recorded as of October 26, 2026.

Randy Brown.subtitle: Career chronology · 28 professional fights and 6 amateur results

items.label: Begins boxing as a teenager
items.detail: Brown says he began boxing as a teenager in 2005, several years before starting mixed martial arts.

items.label: Transitions from boxing to MMA
items.detail: Brown says he discovered mixed martial arts around age 19 after several years of boxing. The UFC credits him with four amateur MMA championships across local promotions.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Stephond Ewins · first documented bout
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision at Locked in the Cage 11, the earliest amateur bout listed in Sherdog's record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Joseph Tortorella
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision at Ring of Combat Amateur 14.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Chris Edmund
items.detail: Submitted Edmund with a guillotine choke at 1:41 of round three at Ring of Combat Amateur 15.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Eric Fleming
items.detail: Earned a first-round guillotine choke submission at 2:27 at Dead Serious MMA 7.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Nicholas Willey
items.detail: Lost a unanimous decision over three rounds at Xtreme Caged Combat / Xtreme Fight Events.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · James Rendeiro · finishes amateur career 4–2
items.detail: Defeated Rendeiro by unanimous decision at Xtreme Caged Combat: Unrivaled. His six recorded amateur bouts finished at 4–2, consistent with the UFC's reported amateur record.
items.sourceLabel: UFC athlete profile; Sherdog amateur results

items.label: WIN · Steve Tyrrell · professional debut
items.detail: Made his professional debut at Ring of Combat 48 in Atlantic City and submitted Tyrrell by armbar at 1:53 of round one. It was the first of six consecutive Ring of Combat victories.

items.label: WIN · Leonard Simpson
items.detail: Stopped Simpson by TKO (punches) at 0:52 of round two at Ring of Combat 49, moving to 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Mike Winters · wins Ring of Combat welterweight title
items.detail: Stopped Winters by TKO (punches) at 1:11 of round two at Ring of Combat 50, winning the vacant welterweight championship in just his third professional fight.

items.label: WIN · Rocky Edwards · first Ring of Combat title defense
items.detail: Defended the Ring of Combat welterweight belt with a TKO (punches) at 4:25 of round two at Ring of Combat 51.

items.label: WIN · Ben Brewer · catchweight bout
items.detail: Submitted Brewer by guillotine choke at 0:31 of round two at Ring of Combat 52. The fight took place at a 178-pound catchweight rather than as a welterweight title defense.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Brown's Ring of Combat fight ledger

items.label: WIN · Robert Plotkin · second title defense and UFC opportunity
items.detail: Knocked out Plotkin with a knee at 4:23 of round one at Ring of Combat 53, successfully defending his welterweight title for the second time. Dana White saw the fight while filming Lookin' for a Fight; Brown subsequently joined the UFC at 6–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC fighter feature; Sherdog bout record

items.label: WIN · Matt Dwyer · UFC debut
items.detail: Made his UFC debut at UFC on FOX 18 in Newark, beating Dwyer by unanimous decision. The win extended his unbeaten professional start to 7–0.

items.label: LOSS · Michael Graves · first professional defeat
items.detail: Graves submitted Brown by rear-naked choke at 2:31 of round two at UFC on FOX 19, ending his 7–0 professional start.

items.label: WIN · Erick Montaño · guillotine finish
items.detail: Submitted Montaño with a guillotine choke at 0:18 of round three at UFC Fight Night: Poirier vs. Johnson in Hidalgo, Texas.

items.label: WIN · Brian Camozzi · second-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Camozzi with a knee and follow-up punches at 1:25 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Lewis vs. Abdurakhimov.

items.label: LOSS · Belal Muhammad
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to Muhammad at UFC 208 in Brooklyn.

items.label: WIN · Mickey Gall · Madison Square Garden
items.detail: Defeated Gall by unanimous decision at UFC 217 in New York. The win returned Brown to the win column and showed his experience against a heavily publicized prospect.

items.label: LOSS · Niko Price · unusual ground-position knockout
items.detail: Price knocked Brown out at 1:09 of round two at UFC Boise, using hammerfists from bottom position while trapping Brown's head with his foot. The finish became a memorable UFC highlight.

items.label: WIN · Bryan Barberena · third-round stoppage
items.detail: Returned after nearly a year away and stopped Barberena by TKO (punches) at 2:54 of round three at UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. The Korean Zombie.

items.label: WIN · Warlley Alves · triangle choke and performance bonus
items.detail: After Alves took him down, Brown locked a triangle choke from his back at 1:22 of round two in São Paulo. The submission earned Brown a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · UFC São Paulo bonus report

items.label: LOSS · Vicente Luque · late second-round knockout
items.detail: Luque stopped Brown with a knee and punches at 4:56 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Brunson vs. Shahbazyan.

items.label: WIN · Alex Oliveira · first-round submission
items.detail: Submitted Oliveira by rear-naked choke at 2:50 of round one at UFC 261 in Jacksonville, beginning a four-fight winning streak.

items.label: WIN · Jared Gooden
items.detail: Beat Gooden by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Rodriguez, his second consecutive victory.

items.label: WIN · Khaos Williams · split decision
items.detail: Edged Williams by split decision over three rounds at UFC 274, extending Brown's winning streak to three.

items.label: WIN · Francisco Trinaldo · fourth consecutive victory
items.detail: Defeated Trinaldo by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Yan. It was Brown's fourth straight UFC victory, his longest UFC winning streak.

items.label: LOSS · Jack Della Maddalena · UFC 284
items.detail: Della Maddalena submitted Brown via rear-naked choke at 2:13 of round one at UFC 284 in Perth, ending Brown's four-fight winning streak.

items.label: WIN · Wellington Turman
items.detail: Beat Turman by unanimous decision at UFC on ABC: Emmett vs. Topuria in Jacksonville.

items.label: WIN · Muslim Salikhov · knockout and $50,000 bonus
items.detail: Knocked Salikhov out with punches at 3:17 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Dolidze vs. Imavov. The finish earned Brown a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: WIN · Elizeu Zaleski dos Santos · UFC 302
items.detail: Outpointed Zaleski dos Santos by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC 302 in Newark, stretching his latest winning streak to three.

items.label: LOSS · Bryan Battle · split decision
items.detail: Lost a closely contested split decision against Battle at UFC 310 in Las Vegas.

items.label: WIN · Nicolas Dalby · knockout and Fight of the Night
items.detail: After both men were hurt, Brown knocked out Dalby with a right hook at 1:39 of round two at UFC Kansas City, becoming the first opponent to stop the Danish veteran. They each earned a $50,000 Fight of the Night bonus.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · UFC Kansas City bonuses

items.label: LOSS · Gabriel Bonfim · first UFC main event
items.detail: Headlined UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brown in Las Vegas. Bonfim caught him with a knee and stopped him at 1:40 of round two.

items.label: LOSS · Kevin Holland · UFC 327
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to Holland at UFC 327, leaving Brown on a two-fight losing streak heading into his next booking.

items.label: Jacobe Smith replaces Carlos Leal in October 31 co-main event
items.detail: Carlos Leal withdrew injured from his scheduled fight with Brown. Unbeaten Jacobe Smith, fresh off his October 3 win over Bruce Whitehead, accepted the October 31 co-main event on short notice. The bout was reported October 21 and appears on the UFC's official event lineup.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Jacobe Smith
items.detail: Booked to face undefeated Jacobe Smith (13–0) in the co-main event at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Brown enters at 20–8 overall and 14–8 in the UFC, having lost his previous two fights. As of October 26, the matchup has not taken place.

Jacobe Smith.name: Jacobe Smith
Jacobe Smith.subtitle: Career chronology · 13 professional bouts and collegiate wrestling milestones

items.label: Wins Oklahoma high-school wrestling championship
items.detail: Won the Oklahoma Class 6A high-school wrestling state title at 160 pounds while competing for Muskogee. Muskogee Athletics and Northeastern Oklahoma A&M list the championship in 2014; his UFC and Oklahoma State biographies say 2013, a discrepancy in the published histories.

items.label: First NJCAA national wrestling championship
items.detail: Won the 174-pound NJCAA national championship for Northeastern Oklahoma A&M, beating Colby's Jared Johnson 6–2 in the final. Went 5–0 at the tournament and finished the season 36–4.

items.label: Second NJCAA national wrestling championship
items.detail: Repeated as the 174-pound NJCAA national champion, defeating Ellsworth's Jordan Gundrum 14–5 in the final. Went 76–6 across his two junior-college seasons before joining Oklahoma State.

items.label: Oklahoma State wrestling · undefeated redshirt season
items.detail: Transferred to Oklahoma State and went 15–0 at 174 pounds while competing in open tournaments during his redshirt season. Won all four tournaments he entered; ten of his wins came by fall.

items.label: NCAA Division I wrestling All-American
items.detail: Placed eighth nationally at 174 pounds to earn NCAA Division I All-American honors for Oklahoma State. He finished the 2017–18 season 22–8 and placed third at the Big 12 championship.

items.label: Wins Big 12 wrestling championship at 174 pounds
items.detail: Defeated Northern Iowa's Taylor Lujan 6–4 in the 174-pound final to win the Big 12 title for Oklahoma State. He went 28–5 during the 2018–19 season. His school bio calls it a second consecutive Big 12 title, but its own 2018 recap lists him third; only the 2019 individual title is independently established here.

items.label: WIN · Roderick Stewart · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Began his professional MMA career with a first-round TKO (punches) at 1:34 at Xtreme Fight Night 374. He moved into MMA after his collegiate wrestling career.

items.label: WIN · Will Florentino · 23-second TKO
items.detail: Stopped Florentino by TKO (punches) at 0:23 of round one at Xtreme Fight Night 378, improving to 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Zac Kelley · 42-second TKO
items.detail: Stopped Kelley with punches at 0:42 of round one at Xtreme Fight Night 381. His first three professional fights all ended by first-round TKO.

items.label: WIN · Tommie Britton · Fury FC debut
items.detail: Stopped Britton by TKO (punches) at 3:06 of round one at Fury FC 72, improving to 4–0.

items.label: WIN · Leivon Lewis · first decision victory
items.detail: Defeated Lewis by unanimous decision after three rounds at Fury FC 74, the first time his professional career reached the scorecards.

items.label: WIN · Austin Jones · second decision victory
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision over Jones at Fury FC 81, moving to 6–0. This remains his most recent decision win entering October 31, 2026.

items.label: WIN · Brian Grinnell · returns to finishing opponents
items.detail: Knocked out Grinnell with a punch at 1:01 of round one at Fury FC 83. This began a run of seven consecutive finishes through October 3, 2026.

items.label: WIN · Jared McLoughlin · first-round knockout
items.detail: Knocked out McLoughlin with punches in the first round at Fury FC 86. Tapology and the UFC list the stoppage at 0:18; Sherdog lists 0:21, so databases disagree on the exact time.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · original Fury FC 86 bout record

items.label: WIN · Christien Savoie · earns UFC contract on Contender Series
items.detail: Stopped Savoie with ground-and-pound elbows at 2:55 of round two on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 8, Week 8. Entered the bout 8–0; the ninth professional victory secured a UFC contract.

items.label: WIN · Preston Parsons · UFC debut
items.detail: Knocked Parsons out with punches at 1:13 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2, improving to 10–0 as a professional.

items.label: WIN · Niko Price · first professional submission
items.detail: Took Price down, controlled him on the ground and secured a rear-naked choke at 4:03 of round two at UFC 317. It was Smith's first recorded professional submission finish.

items.label: WIN · Josiah Harrell · knockout and Performance of the Night
items.detail: After being taken down early, reversed position and knocked Harrell out with ground strikes at 3:01 of round one in Houston. The finish earned a Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: Takes short-notice UFC 332 bout against Bruce Whitehead
items.detail: Accepted an October 3 fight with promotional newcomer Bruce Whitehead on about nine days' notice, setting up a quick return after his February win over Josiah Harrell.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Mania report via Yahoo Sports · September 24, 2026

items.label: WIN · Bruce Whitehead · fourth consecutive UFC stoppage
items.detail: Knocked out Whitehead with punches at 1:32 of round one at UFC 332 in Salt Lake City. The victory put him at 13–0 overall and 4–0 in the UFC, with seven straight finishes since September 2023.

items.label: Accepts Randy Brown co-main event on short notice
items.detail: Agreed to replace injured Carlos Leal against veteran Randy Brown at the October 31 UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas. Reports broke October 20–21; the booking was made roughly 12 days before fight night and 17–18 days after his Whitehead knockout.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Randy Brown
items.detail: Scheduled to meet Brown (20–8) in the welterweight co-main event at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Smith enters unbeaten at 13–0 (4–0 UFC). No fight result is available as of October 26, 2026.

Yana Santos.name: Yana Santos
Yana Santos.subtitle: Career chronology · 26 professional bouts, including one no contest

items.label: Begins martial-arts training
items.detail: Santos says she began martial arts at four and later won Russian national championships in Thai boxing and taekwondo. Exact title dates are not independently established.

items.label: WIN · Magdalena Jarecka · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Made her professional debut as Yana Kunitskaya in Poland at the K-1 World Grand Prix, finishing Jarecka by TKO (punches) at 1:38 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Vladena Yavorskaya · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted Yavorskaya by rear-naked choke at 3:20 of the first round at Bushido FC: Legends. This is her only recorded professional submission victory.

items.label: LOSS · Maria Hougaard Djursaa · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision at Fight Gala 14 in Denmark.

items.label: WIN · Kamila Balanda · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Balanda with punches at 4:26 of round one at Bushido Lithuania: Hero's Lithuania 2010.

items.label: WIN · Cindy Dandois · 34-second finish
items.detail: Stopped future UFC fighter Cindy Dandois by TKO (punches) just 34 seconds into round one at M-1 Challenge 22.

items.label: WIN · Arune Lauzeckaite · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Lauzeckaite with punches at 1:34 of round one at Bushido Lithuania: Hero's Lithuania 2011.

items.label: WIN · Ekaterina Saraykina · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Saraykina with punches at 1:05 of round one at Verdict Fighting Championship 1.

items.label: WIN · Anna Melikhova · two-round decision
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision after two five-minute rounds at Lion's Fights 1.

items.label: WIN · Sylwia Kusiak · corner stoppage
items.detail: Won by TKO when Kusiak's corner stopped the fight at 0:50 of round one at Baltic Arena, ending her first active stretch at 8–1.

items.label: Nearly four years away from professional MMA
items.detail: Did not compete between June 2012 and March 2016. She later discussed the limited opportunities available to women at the time and raising her first child during this period. The interruption should not be labeled an injury layoff without evidence.

items.label: LOSS · Zaira Dishekova · returns to MMA
items.detail: Returned to competition at ACB 32 in Moscow but lost by armbar at 3:38 of round one, her first fight after the extended hiatus.

items.label: WIN · Wu Yanan · second-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Wu Yanan (listed in some records as Yanan Wu) by TKO (punches) at 0:32 of round two at Fightspirit Championship 6.

items.label: NO CONTEST · Tonya Evinger · Invicta FC 20
items.detail: Initially announced as the winner by first-round armbar, but the Missouri Office of Athletics overturned the result on December 1, 2016 because a referee instruction interfered with Evinger's legal defense. The official ruling is a no contest, and Evinger retained her Invicta bantamweight belt.

items.label: LOSS · Tonya Evinger · Invicta FC 22 rematch
items.detail: Lost the bantamweight title rematch to Evinger by rear-naked choke at 4:32 of round two.

items.label: WIN · Raquel Pa'aluhi · vacant Invicta bantamweight championship
items.detail: Defeated Raquel Pa'aluhi (also recorded under Raquel Canuto) by unanimous decision over five rounds at Invicta FC 25, winning the vacant bantamweight title. This is separate from the 2016 Tonya Evinger armbar result that was overturned to a no contest.

items.label: LOSS · Cris Cyborg · UFC debut and title challenge
items.detail: Made her UFC debut on short notice in a featherweight title challenge at UFC 222. She scored an early takedown but was stopped by Cyborg's punches at 3:25 of round one.

items.label: WIN · Lina Länsberg
items.detail: Won by unanimous decision at UFC 229.

items.label: WIN · Marion Reneau
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision at bantamweight.

items.label: LOSS · Aspen Ladd
items.detail: Stopped by ground strikes in round three.

items.label: WIN · Julija Stoliarenko
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision.

items.label: WIN · Ketlen Vieira
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over Vieira.

items.label: LOSS · Irene Aldana
items.detail: Stopped by strikes late in round one at UFC 264.

items.label: Gives birth to second child, daughter Alise
items.detail: Santos welcomed her second child in April 2022 with husband Thiago Santos. She had not fought since July 2021 and returned to UFC competition in March 2023, balancing training with motherhood.

items.label: LOSS · Holly Holm
items.detail: Lost by unanimous decision.

items.label: LOSS · Karol Rosa
items.detail: Lost by split decision.

items.label: Chelsea Chandler misses weight by five pounds
items.detail: Chelsea Chandler weighed 141 pounds, five above the non-title bantamweight allowance of 136; Santos made weight. Their scheduled 135-pound fight proceeded at a catchweight after Chandler's miss.

items.label: WIN · Chelsea Chandler
items.detail: Defeated Chandler by unanimous decision at UFC on ESPN 61, snapping a three-fight losing streak. Santos made the bantamweight limit but Chandler weighed five pounds over; the bout proceeded at catchweight.

items.label: WIN · Miesha Tate
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over the former UFC champion.

items.label: Macy Chiasson misses weight before UFC 320
items.detail: Chiasson came in at 137.5 pounds, 1.5 pounds above the non-title bantamweight allowance. Santos made weight and the fight proceeded; it was Santos' second consecutive bout against an opponent who missed weight.

items.label: WIN · Macy Chiasson
items.detail: Defeated Chiasson by unanimous decision at UFC 320 for a third consecutive victory. Chiasson had weighed 137.5 pounds, above the bantamweight non-title limit, while Santos made weight. All seven of Santos' UFC victories have come by decision.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Luana Santos
items.detail: Booked against Luana Santos in a bantamweight matchup.

Luana Santos.name: Luana Santos
Luana Santos.subtitle: Career chronology · 13 professional bouts and 3 amateur results

items.label: Begins judo training
items.detail: Started judo at eight, encouraged by her father, and practiced through her teenage years. She later won Brazilian, Pan-American and European judo titles; specific dates and categories are not established in her UFC biography.

items.label: Transitions from judo toward MMA at 011 MMA Team
items.detail: Inspired by Ronda Rousey, Santos became interested in MMA while watching a UFC card at a friend's home around 2017. A family connection introduced her to Hélio Moyano at 011 MMA Team in São Paulo, where she began MMA training.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Karine Cristine · first recorded MMA bout
items.detail: Opened her documented amateur career by unanimous decision over Karine Cristine at SFT 11, completing three rounds.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Ana Merlin · second-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Ana Merlin by TKO (punches) at 0:45 of round two at SFT 15.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Angela Rosa · concludes 3–0 amateur record
items.detail: Defeated Angela Rosa by unanimous decision at SFT 21, completing her three-bout amateur MMA record undefeated.

items.label: WIN · Marjorie Barragan · professional debut
items.detail: Submitted Barragan by scarf-hold armlock (kesa-gatame variation) at 3:19 of round one at SFT 27, her first recorded professional MMA bout.

items.label: WIN · Djulia Ariana · first professional decision
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision against Djulia Ariana at SFT 32, improving to 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Beatriz Ferreira · third-round keylock
items.detail: Submitted Beatriz Ferreira with a keylock at 0:26 of round three at SFT 34, leaving the Standout Fighting Tournament promotion undefeated at 3–0.

items.label: LOSS · Jena Bishop · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost by split decision over three rounds against veteran grappler Jena Bishop at LFA 135. The loss interrupted her 3–0 professional start and remains one of her two professional defeats.

items.label: WIN · Waleska Sousa · rebounds at LFA 146
items.detail: Earned a three-round unanimous decision over Waleska Sousa at LFA 146, returning to the win column.

items.label: WIN · Bartira Rodrigues · technical guillotine submission
items.detail: Finished Rodrigues by technical submission (guillotine choke) at 3:05 of round one at LFA 154. She entered the UFC on the back of this win, 5–1 as a professional.

items.label: Signs UFC contract ahead of August debut
items.detail: Joined the UFC with a 5–1 professional record after wins over Waleska Sousa and Bartira Rodrigues. The UFC biography describes the signing as 'exactly 24 months' after her professional debut, but the documented fight dates from July 15, 2021 to August 12, 2023 span about 25 months; the exact contract-signing day is not confirmed.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · fighter questionnaire; Sherdog bout dates

items.label: WIN · Juliana Miller · UFC debut and first pro TKO
items.detail: Stopped The Ultimate Fighter winner Juliana Miller by TKO (punches) at 3:41 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Luque vs. dos Anjos. It was the first knockout/TKO victory of Santos' professional MMA career.

items.label: WIN · Stephanie Egger · short-notice weight cut
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision over Egger at UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Gutiérrez. Santos later said it was her toughest fight to date because of a short camp, losing considerable weight in about 20 days, and an unexpected health problem.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official result and fighter Q&A

items.label: WIN · Mariya Agapova · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted Agapova by rear-naked choke at 3:27 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Namajunas vs. Cortez, securing her third consecutive UFC victory.

items.label: LOSS · Casey O'Neill · UFC 305
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to O'Neill in Perth at UFC 305. This remains her only UFC defeat through October 26, 2026.

items.label: WIN · Tainara Lisboa · americana at 4:59
items.detail: Submitted Lisboa with an americana/keylock at 4:59 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Burns vs. Morales, finishing just before the round ended. Both fighters are scheduled separately on the October 31, 2026 card.

items.label: WIN · Melissa Croden · second straight victory
items.detail: Defeated Melissa Croden by unanimous decision at UFC on ESPN: Royval vs. Kape. The judges scored it 29–28, 29–28 and 30–27, extending Santos' win streak to two.

items.label: WIN · Karol Rosa · unanimous 30–27 sweep
items.detail: Defeated established bantamweight contender Karol Rosa over three rounds at UFC Fight Night: Kape vs. Horiguchi 2. All three judges scored the fight 30–27 for Santos, extending her UFC winning streak to three.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Yana Santos
items.detail: Set to face former Invicta bantamweight champion Yana Santos at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Luana enters 11–2 professionally and 6–1 inside the UFC, carrying three consecutive wins. No October 31 result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Ode' Osbourne.name: Ode' Osbourne
Ode' Osbourne.subtitle: Career chronology · 24 professional bouts and 3 documented amateur results

items.label: Born in Jamaica and later moves to the United States
items.detail: Born in Kingston, Jamaica, and moved to the United States as a child, according to UFC interviews. Exact childhood move date varies or is not firmly sourced.

items.label: College wrestling brings Osbourne to Wisconsin
items.detail: Moved to Wisconsin in 2011 to wrestle under college coach Benjamin Tones. Tones also coached at an MMA gym and introduced Osbourne to head coach Reese Shaner during the wrestling offseason. UFC identifies Osbourne as a first-year collegiate national qualifier.

items.label: Wins amateur championship; begins MMA competition
items.detail: The UFC lists an XFO amateur title among Osbourne's accomplishments. Three amateur bouts in 2013 are indexed by Sherdog; the championship's exact fight date and opponent are not firmly established, so no unsourced title fight is identified here.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jesse Fisher · unanimous decision
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision over Fisher at RFA 8: Pettis vs. Pegg, one of three amateur bouts documented by Sherdog.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Alex Brockway · 19-second stoppage
items.detail: Stopped Brockway by TKO (punches) at 0:19 of round one at APFC 12.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jonathan Morrison · unanimous decision
items.detail: Defeated Morrison by unanimous decision after three three-minute rounds at NAFC: Unrivaled, bringing his three documented amateur bouts to 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Brent Lee · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Opened his professional MMA career by submitting Brent Lee with a rear-naked choke at 1:10 of round two at NAFC: Explosion in Waukesha, Wisconsin.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: NO CONTEST · Murjan Flowers · Pure FC 1
items.detail: His second professional bout ended in a round-two no contest at Pure FC 1. MMA Official attributes the stoppage to an accidental eye poke; Sherdog verifies the no-contest ruling but does not give a cause or reliable elapsed stoppage time.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Official · bout mechanism; Sherdog · no-contest ruling

items.label: WIN · Doug Milbrath · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Milbrath with punches at 1:37 of the first round at NAFC: Battledome, raising his professional record to 2–0 with one no contest.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · David Rhoads · stoppage from punches
items.detail: Earned a first-round TKO (submission to punches) over Rhoads at 4:36 at NAFC: Super Brawl 3.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: LOSS · Antonio Sanchez · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost a unanimous decision over three rounds at RFA 39: Barcelos vs. Moffett. It was Osbourne's first recorded professional defeat after a 3–0 start.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Cory Galloway · split decision
items.detail: Won a three-round split decision at Pure FC 5, moving to 4–1 with one no contest.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: LOSS · Jose Calvo · 24-second kneebar
items.detail: Submitted by Jose Calvo (also listed as Jose Luis Calvo) with a kneebar just 0:24 into round one at United Combat League: Havoc in Hammond 4.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Seigenald Aurtan Daley Jr. · first meeting
items.detail: Submitted Daley with a triangle choke at 1:44 of the opening round at Pure FC 9.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Seigenald Aurtan Daley Jr. · rematch
items.detail: Stopped Daley by TKO (punches) at 2:16 of round one at Pure FC 10, recording two consecutive wins against the same opponent.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Kelly Offield · triangle choke
items.detail: Submitted Offield by triangle choke at 4:07 of round one at HD MMA 15, his third consecutive professional win.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · complete professional MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Armando Villarreal · Contender Series UFC contract
items.detail: Submitted Villarreal by armbar at 4:39 of round one on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 3, Week 4. Entered the UFC with an 8–2 professional record and one no contest.

items.label: LOSS · Brian Kelleher · UFC debut
items.detail: Kelleher submitted Osbourne with a guillotine choke at 2:49 of round one at UFC 246. This was Osbourne's first official UFC event bout; his 2019 Contender Series appearance is counted as a professional fight, not a UFC Octagon result.

items.label: WIN · Jerome Rivera · 26-second knockout
items.detail: Knocked Rivera out with punches only 26 seconds into round one at UFC Fight Night: Overeem vs. Volkov, recording his first official UFC victory.

items.label: LOSS · Manel Kape · flying-knee knockout
items.detail: Kape knocked him out with a flying knee and follow-up punches at 4:44 of round one at UFC 265.

items.label: WIN · C.J. Vergara · UFC 268
items.detail: Beat Vergara by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC 268 in New York.

items.label: WIN · Zarrukh Adashev · knockout and first UFC bonus
items.detail: Knocked out Adashev with a counter right hook and follow-up punches at 1:01 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Volkov vs. Rozenstruik. The finish earned a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus, Osbourne's first UFC bonus.

items.label: LOSS · Tyson Nam · first-round knockout
items.detail: Nam knocked Osbourne out with punches at 2:59 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Vera vs. Cruz.

items.label: WIN · Charles Johnson · split decision
items.detail: Won a three-round split decision over Johnson at UFC Fight Night: Muniz vs. Allen. Judges scored it 29–28, 29–28 for Osbourne and 29–28 for Johnson.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · UFC fight result and judges' scores

items.label: LOSS · Asu Almabayev · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Almabayev submitted Osbourne by rear-naked choke at 3:11 of round two at UFC on ESPN: Sandhagen vs. Font.

items.label: LOSS · Jafel Filho · first-round submission
items.detail: Filho submitted Osbourne with a rear-naked choke at 4:27 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Tuivasa vs. Tybura, his second consecutive submission loss.

items.label: LOSS · Ronaldo Rodriguez · UFC 306
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to Rodriguez at UFC 306 at the Sphere in Las Vegas. This was Osbourne's third consecutive defeat.

items.label: WIN · Luis Gurule · snaps skid; Performance of the Night
items.detail: Stopped previously unbeaten UFC newcomer Gurule with a counter left hand and follow-up punches at 1:54 of round two at UFC Vegas 105. The win ended a three-fight skid and earned a second $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: LOSS · Steve Erceg · bantamweight co-main event
items.detail: Moved up to bantamweight for a co-main-event fight with former flyweight title challenger Steve Erceg at UFC on ESPN: Dolidze vs. Hernandez. Lost by unanimous decision after three rounds.

items.label: NO CONTEST · Alibi Idiris · decision overturned after drug-test finding
items.detail: Idiris initially won a unanimous decision at UFC Houston, but the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation changed the result to a no contest after Idiris tested positive for hydrochlorothiazide, a prohibited diuretic. CSAD announced Idiris' 12-month suspension in March. Some UFC fighter pages still show the original decision loss; the commission-amended no contest is used here.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · March 31, 2026 suspension and commission ruling

items.label: Withdraws injured from original Cody Durden booking
items.detail: Was booked to face Cody Durden at UFC 329 on July 11, but withdrew after suffering an injury following an eight-week training camp. Alessandro Costa replaced him against Durden. No specific medical diagnosis is reliably established.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · July 2, 2026 injury and replacement report

items.label: Rebooked against Cody Durden for October 31
items.detail: Osbourne and Durden were rebooked for an October 31 flyweight fight, after the July matchup fell through because of Osbourne's injury. The rebooking was reported in September.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Cody Durden
items.detail: Booked against Cody Durden on the main card at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Enters with a professional record of 13–9 and two no contests; his official UFC record is 5–7 with one no contest. No result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Cody Durden.name: Cody Durden
Cody Durden.subtitle: Career chronology · 30 professional MMA bouts, 6 documented amateur MMA bouts

items.label: Wins two Georgia high-school wrestling state championships
items.detail: Durden says he won two Georgia state wrestling championships in 2009 and received three scholarship offers, but began working after school to support his child. These are his self-reported wrestling accomplishments, not professional MMA titles.

items.label: Begins MMA training in Atlanta
items.detail: Started training for MMA in Atlanta after a background in competitive wrestling. Durden says he worked in construction before becoming a full-time fighter.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Francisco Quijada · amateur debut
items.detail: Lost his first documented amateur MMA fight at NFC 64 to a rear-naked choke at 2:09 of round three. He went on to win his next five amateur fights.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Deego Bautista
items.detail: Submitted Bautista via guillotine choke at 2:06 of the first round at NFC 65.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Max Thomas
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision against Thomas at NFC 66.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Anthony Canzano
items.detail: Defeated Canzano by unanimous decision after three rounds at NFC 68.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jamark Cooper
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision over Cooper at NFC 77. This is the only amateur bout displayed in Sherdog's shorter amateur ledger, but other databases document five additional fights.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · amateur history; Tapology · additional bouts

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Michael Torres · completes 5–1 amateur run
items.detail: Beat Torres by unanimous decision at NFC 81. His six named amateur MMA bouts total five wins and one loss, consistent with the 5–1 amateur record he reports to the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · amateur MMA history; UFC athlete Q&A

items.label: WIN · Marcus Levester · professional debut
items.detail: Turned professional at NFC 83, stopping Levester by TKO (punches) at 1:30 of round one in Atlanta.

items.label: WIN · Damarcus Holmes
items.detail: Submitted Holmes by rear-naked choke at 1:01 of the first round at NFC 85 in Kennesaw, Georgia.

items.label: WIN · Devante Sewell
items.detail: Earned a three-round unanimous decision over Sewell at NFC 88 in Atlanta, improving to 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Dave Morgan · 39-second guillotine choke
items.detail: Caught Morgan in a guillotine choke at 0:39 of round one at NFC 92, extending his unbeaten professional start to 4–0.

items.label: LOSS · Jared Scoggins · NFC flyweight championship
items.detail: Lost by unanimous decision after three rounds against Jared Scoggins at NFC 97 in a bout listed for the NFC flyweight championship. It was Durden's first professional defeat.

items.label: LOSS · Ryan Hollis · second consecutive defeat
items.detail: Submitted by rear-naked choke at 3:39 of round two at 864 Fighting Championship 3.

items.label: WIN · Todd Monroe · first meeting
items.detail: Stopped Monroe by TKO (punches) at 3:15 of round one at 864 Fighting Championship 5, ending a two-fight losing streak.

items.label: WIN · Todd Monroe · wins rematch by armbar
items.detail: Met Monroe again at 864 Fighting Championship 9 and submitted him with an armbar at 4:56 of round three.

items.label: Competes in professional boxing
items.detail: Boxing records document wins over Matt Murphy (August 11, 2018), Isidro Guzman (March 9, 2019), Justin Parker and James DeHerrera (both April 27, 2019). These were professional boxing bouts, not MMA victories, and are kept separate from his 18–11–1 MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Dylan Schulte · 30-second slam TKO
items.detail: Stopped Schulte via slam TKO at 0:30 of round one at Sparta Combat League: Army vs. Marines 10 in Loveland, Colorado. The MMA bout is one distinct professional result alongside other boxing/kickboxing activity connected with the event.

items.label: Wins King of Sparta eight-man flyweight tournament
items.detail: Durden credits himself with winning the King of Sparta eight-man flyweight tournament in Colorado during 2019, accepting the opportunity on two days' notice with Justin Gaethje in his corner. He describes boxing, kickboxing and MMA rounds in a single night and a $10,000 prize. These mixed-rules contests are not all additional professional MMA fights; his UFC interviews differ on the exact month.

items.label: WIN · Jeremy Rogers · armbar
items.detail: Submitted Rogers by armbar at 0:59 of round one at Valor Fighting Challenge 59.

items.label: WIN · Dre Miley · Valor bantamweight championship
items.detail: Stopped Miley with punches at 4:37 of round two at Valor Fighting Challenge 66 to win the vacant Valor bantamweight title, his eighth professional win.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Valor 66 confirmed championship main event

items.label: WIN · Varon Webb · NFC headliner
items.detail: Submitted Webb via rear-naked choke at 3:17 of the opening round in the NFC 124 main event, improving to 10–2.

items.label: WIN · John Sweeney · final regional bout before UFC
items.detail: Stopped John Sweeney with punches at 1:20 of round one at NFC 125. Entered the UFC two weeks later riding a seven-fight professional winning streak and an 11–2 record.

items.label: DRAW · Chris Gutierrez · UFC debut on short notice
items.detail: Fought Chris Gutierrez to a three-round unanimous draw at UFC Fight Night: Brunson vs. Shahbazyan after accepting a bout up a weight class only two weeks after his NFC victory. The official result was a draw, not a win or a loss.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fight history and fighter Q&A

items.label: LOSS · Jimmy Flick · flying triangle submission
items.detail: Flick submitted Durden via flying triangle choke at 3:18 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Thompson vs. Neal, a notable highlight-reel grappling finish.

items.label: WIN · Aoriqileng · first UFC victory
items.detail: Defeated Aoriqileng (also indexed as Qileng Aori) by three-round unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Vieira vs. Tate. This was Durden's first victory in the Octagon.

items.label: LOSS · Muhammad Mokaev · 58-second guillotine
items.detail: Mokaev submitted Durden with a guillotine choke at 0:58 of round one at UFC London, Durden's fastest recorded UFC defeat.

items.label: WIN · JP Buys · first UFC knockout
items.detail: Stopped Buys with punches at 1:08 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Tsarukyan vs. Gamrot, the beginning of four straight victories.

items.label: WIN · Carlos Mota
items.detail: Outpointed Mota by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC Fight Night: Kattar vs. Allen, improving to two straight victories.

items.label: WIN · Charles Johnson · third straight UFC win
items.detail: Used takedowns and extended control time to defeat Charles Johnson by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Simón. This UFC victory was absent from the earlier timeline.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fight history; Sherdog record

items.label: WIN · Jake Hadley · four-fight UFC winning streak
items.detail: Beat Hadley by unanimous decision at UFC Nashville, moving to four consecutive wins—the longest streak of his UFC career.

items.label: LOSS · Tagir Ulanbekov · face-crank submission
items.detail: Submitted by Ulanbekov with a face crank at 4:25 of round two at UFC 296, ending his four-fight winning streak. Some generalized reports call it a rear-naked choke; Sherdog records face crank.

items.label: LOSS · Bruno Silva · second-round TKO
items.detail: Silva stopped Durden by TKO (punches) at 2:58 of round two at UFC on ESPN: Lemos vs. Jandiroba.

items.label: WIN · Matt Schnell · submission and Performance of the Night
items.detail: Accepted the matchup on four days' notice and submitted Schnell at 0:29 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Burns vs. Brady, earning a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus. UFC classifies the hold as anaconda choke; Sherdog and Tapology call it ninja choke. The difference in classification is acknowledged rather than presented as two finishes.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official result; Sherdog/Tapology alternative technique

items.label: LOSS · Joshua Van · UFC 310
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision against Joshua Van at UFC 310 in Las Vegas.

items.label: LOSS · José Ochoa · second-round knockout
items.detail: Ochoa knocked Durden out with punches at 0:11 of round two at UFC on ESPN: Usman vs. Buckley in Atlanta.

items.label: LOSS · Allan Nascimento · 130-pound catchweight
items.detail: Durden replaced Rafael Estevam and fought Nascimento at a negotiated 130-pound catchweight at UFC Fight Night: Garcia vs. Onama. Nascimento submitted him by anaconda choke at 3:13 of round two.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official result; catchweight confirmed by bout history

items.label: LOSS · Nyamjargal Tumendemberel · UFC 326
items.detail: Dropped a three-round unanimous decision against Tumendemberel at UFC 326, his fourth consecutive defeat.

items.label: WIN · Jafel Filho · short notice, bantamweight upset
items.detail: Stepped in for Lucas Rocha on approximately six days' notice and upset heavily favored Jafel Filho by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Sterling vs. Zalal. The bout took place at bantamweight (135 pounds), not flyweight, and snapped a four-fight losing streak.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · UFC April 25 bout report, weight and result

items.label: Ode' Osbourne withdraws; Alessandro Costa replaces him
items.detail: Durden had been booked against Osbourne for UFC 329 on July 11, but Osbourne withdrew injured. Alessandro Costa accepted the replacement fight, announced July 1–2.

items.label: LOSS · Alessandro Costa · UFC 329
items.detail: Costa submitted Durden by rear-naked choke at 2:19 of round two at UFC 329 in Las Vegas, bringing Durden's professional record to 18–11–1.

items.label: Original matchup against Ode' Osbourne rebooked
items.detail: UFC's October 26 fight-by-fight preview confirms Durden and Osbourne are paired again for an October 31 flyweight bout. The exact signing date is not established here.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Ode' Osbourne
items.detail: Scheduled to face Ode' Osbourne in a flyweight bout at Meta APEX, Las Vegas. Durden enters at 18–11–1 overall and 7–9–1 UFC. The matchup has not occurred as of October 26, 2026.

Zachary Reese.name: Zachary Reese
Zachary Reese.subtitle: Career chronology · 15 professional bouts and 5 documented amateur fights

items.label: Inspired by UFC and Strikeforce
items.detail: Reese says he became interested in MMA through UFC and Strikeforce broadcasts in high school, including Anderson Silva and BJ Penn fights. He later earned a BJJ brown belt.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Steven Gainville · first indexed fight
items.detail: Stopped Gainville by TKO (punches) at 2:54 of round one at Kickass Productions; earliest amateur result listed in Sherdog.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Kevin Holland · unanimous decision
items.detail: Lost a unanimous decision over three three-minute rounds to future UFC fighter Kevin Holland at Cowboys Extreme Cagefighting. Both were competing as amateurs.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · John Wageman · guillotine
items.detail: Submitted Wageman by guillotine choke 30 seconds into round one at Texas Clash Bash 9. The reason for the gap since his 2012 amateur fights is not established.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Coby Bradford · triangle choke
items.detail: Submitted Bradford by triangle choke at 1:20 of round one at Peak Fighting 5.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Parker Didier · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted Didier via rear-naked choke at 2:20 of round two at Peak Fighting 8. Five named amateur fights are documented, four wins and one loss.

items.label: Peak middleweight title and oilfield employment
items.detail: UFC credits Reese with a Peak middleweight championship, but the title fight's date and opponent are not established. Reese described working as an oilfield well tester, sometimes for 90-hour weeks, while preparing for his MMA career.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: WIN · Fred Zamora · professional debut
items.detail: Stopped Zamora by TKO (punches) at 1:32 of round one at Peak Fighting 10, his first professional bout.

items.label: WIN · Malik Jahmaze · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Jahmaze by TKO (punches) at 4:13 of round one at Peak Fighting 15. FightMatrix calls the same opponent Malik Tambe; this is one fight, not two.

items.label: WIN · Shahriar Zolfaghari · Fury FC 71
items.detail: Stopped Zolfaghari with elbows and punches at 0:50 of round one to improve to 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Aaron Phillips · 35-second technical submission
items.detail: Finished TUF alumnus Phillips by technical submission (guillotine choke) at 0:35 of round one at Fury FC 74.

items.label: WIN · Tommie Britton · 52-second TKO
items.detail: Stopped Britton with punches at 0:52 of round one at Fury FC 76. Reese's first five professional wins were first-round finishes.

items.label: WIN · Eli Aronov · Contender Series contract
items.detail: Submitted Aronov by armbar at 1:14 of round one on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 7, Week 3, earning a UFC contract at 6–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: LOSS · Cody Brundage · UFC debut
items.detail: Suffered his first professional defeat when Brundage slammed him and followed with punches, scoring a first-round knockout at 1:49.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: WIN · Julian Marquez · first UFC victory
items.detail: Stopped Marquez 20 seconds into round one with a body kick and follow-up punches, his first UFC win.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: WIN · José Daniel Medina · unanimous decision
items.detail: Defeated Medina by unanimous decision at UFC on ESPN 62, winning 30–27 on all three judges' scorecards. First professional win by decision.

items.label: LOSS · Azamat Bekoev · UFC 311
items.detail: Lost by first-round knockout (punches) at 3:04 to Bekoev at UFC 311, his second professional knockout defeat.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: WIN · Duško Todorović · decision
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over Todorović at UFC on ESPN 68, his second professional decision victory.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official athlete profile and results

items.label: NO CONTEST · Sedriques Dumas · accidental groin kick
items.detail: A Reese kick accidentally struck Dumas in the groin. Dumas could not continue and referee Mike Beltran stopped the fight at 0:51 of round one. Official result: no contest, not a loss or disqualification.

items.label: Replaces injured Robert Valentin on two days' notice
items.detail: Reese accepted a fight with Jackson McVey on two days' notice after Robert Valentin's injury withdrawal. The UFC changed it to a 195-pound catchweight.

items.label: WIN · Jackson McVey · choke and $50,000 bonus
items.detail: Survived a difficult opening round and submitted McVey via rear-naked choke at 1:38 of round two. Earned a $50,000 Performance of the Night bonus in the 195-pound catchweight fight.

items.label: LOSS · Michel Pereira · split decision
