items.detail: Lost a three-round split decision in Houston. Two judges scored it 29–28 Pereira and one 29–28 Reese. His first professional defeat by decision.

items.label: LOSS · Ryan Gandra · first-round TKO
items.detail: Gandra dropped Reese with a left hand and followed with punches, winning by TKO at 1:15 of round one at UFC 329. Gandra—not Reese—was the opponent and winner.

items.label: Mickey Gall matchup reported for October 31
items.detail: MMA Junkie reported Reese's middleweight matchup with Mickey Gall. Gall had been booked to fight Sedriques Dumas in September but withdrew without medical clearance.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Mickey Gall
items.detail: Scheduled for a three-round middleweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Reese enters 10–4 with one no contest overall, 4–4 with one no contest in the UFC. No result yet as of October 26, 2026.

Mickey Gall.name: Mickey Gall
Mickey Gall.subtitle: Career chronology · 14 professional bouts and 3 documented amateur results

items.label: Begins boxing, jiu-jitsu and MMA training
items.detail: Gall says he started boxing at 13, Brazilian jiu-jitsu at 16 and MMA at 19. He later earned a Gracie jiu-jitsu black belt under David Adiv and attended Rutgers University, where he studied communications. The black-belt promotion date is not confirmed.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and martial arts credentials

items.label: Gracie New Jersey and grappling competition
items.detail: Trained with Gracie New Jersey and in the broader Miller Brothers MMA network. UFC credits him with titles at NAGA and Grapplers Quest as well as a Dead Serious MMA middleweight title, but dates of those accomplishments are not established.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Woodmy Jean · MMA debut
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision against Woodmy Jean at CFFC 32. This is the first of three indexed amateur MMA victories.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Joseph Morrison · armbar
items.detail: Submitted Joseph Morrison with an armbar at 1:50 of round two at WCC 11, according to the longer MMA fight ledger. Sherdog's public listing omits this bout, but UFC confirms that Gall's 3–0 amateur run included one armbar and one rear-naked choke.
items.sourceLabel: Combat Edge amateur fight ledger; UFC official career Q&A

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Marvin Nino · ends 3–0 amateur run
items.detail: Submitted Marvin Nino by rear-naked choke at 1:48 of round three at Dead Serious MMA 15, completing a documented 3–0 amateur record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · amateur fight record; UFC amateur summary

items.label: WIN · Ron Templeton · professional debut
items.detail: Made his professional MMA debut in Philadelphia at Dead Serious MMA 17, submitting Ron Templeton via rear-naked choke at 2:53 of round one. UFC president Dana White attended to film the first episode of Dana White: Lookin' for a Fight.

items.label: Calls out CM Punk in front of Dana White
items.detail: After the Templeton win, Gall publicly challenged newly signed former WWE star CM Punk during the Lookin' for a Fight taping. White offered Gall a UFC opportunity while he had just a single professional fight.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · January 2016 interview about the callout

items.label: UFC agrees to CM Punk bout if Gall beats Mike Jackson
items.detail: White set up a fight against fellow novice Mike Jackson with the condition that Gall would be given CM Punk's UFC debut if he won; Jackson would not receive the same opportunity if he won.

items.label: WIN · Mike Jackson · 45-second UFC debut submission
items.detail: Dropped Jackson with a right hand, took his back and finished with a rear-naked choke at 0:45 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Hendricks vs. Thompson. Earned the promised booking against CM Punk.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · February 2016 UFC debut report

items.label: WIN · CM Punk (Phil Brooks) · UFC 203
items.detail: Welcomed CM Punk to professional MMA at UFC 203 in Cleveland and submitted him with a rear-naked choke at 2:14 of round one. Gall improved to 3–0 professionally.

items.label: WIN · Sage Northcutt · 4–0 professional start
items.detail: Submitted Northcutt via rear-naked choke at 1:40 of round two at UFC on FOX: VanZant vs. Waterson. Gall's first four professional wins were all by rear-naked choke.

items.label: LOSS · Randy Brown · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to Randy Brown at UFC 217 in Madison Square Garden, ending his unbeaten 4–0 start. Brown is also on the October 31, 2026 card.

items.label: WIN · George Sullivan · first-round submission
items.detail: Submitted Sullivan via rear-naked choke at 1:09 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Gaethje vs. Vick in Lincoln, Nebraska.

items.label: LOSS · Diego Sanchez · first career stoppage defeat
items.detail: Sanchez stopped Gall by TKO (punches and ground strikes) at 4:13 of round two at UFC 235. It was Gall's first defeat by stoppage. He subsequently revealed he had collapsed during the weight cut and later required hospital treatment.

items.label: Hospitalized with rhabdomyolysis and kidney complications
items.detail: Gall said he became ill and dehydrated around the Sanchez fight, passed out during the weight cut, and spent eight days hospitalized afterward. He reported being diagnosed with rhabdomyolysis and experiencing kidney failure. These are details of his own medical account, not a claim that he was medically cleared to compete despite a known diagnosis.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · March 2019 interview and medical account

items.label: WIN · Salim Touahri · first decision victory
items.detail: Beat Touahri by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC on ESPN: Covington vs. Lawler in Newark, New Jersey. This remains Gall's only professional win by decision as of October 2026.

items.label: Serious back pain develops during fight preparations
items.detail: Gall says a back injury began around preparations for a proposed Carlos Condit fight in late 2019 and grew worse over several years. Despite pain severe enough to limit sitting and training, he continued competing before eventually having surgery in December 2023.

items.label: LOSS · Mike Perry · UFC on ESPN 12
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision to Perry at UFC on ESPN: Poirier vs. Hooker in Las Vegas. Gall later said he had been managing significant back pain during training for this fight.

items.label: WIN · Jordan Williams · sixth rear-naked choke win
items.detail: Submitted Williams via rear-naked choke at 2:57 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Sandhagen vs. Dillashaw. It was Gall's sixth recorded professional submission win; all six were rear-naked chokes.

items.label: LOSS · Alex Morono · unanimous decision
items.detail: Lost to Morono by unanimous decision over three rounds at UFC on ESPN: Font vs. Aldo. This started a four-fight losing streak that continued through November 2024.

items.label: LOSS · Mike Malott · UFC 273
items.detail: Malott stopped Gall with punches at 3:41 of the opening round at UFC 273 in Jacksonville, Florida. It was Gall's second successive defeat and left his UFC record 6–5.

items.label: UFC contract expires; temporarily off roster
items.detail: MMA Fighting reported that Gall had completed his UFC contract and was no longer under contract in September 2022, while remaining eligible to re-sign. This was not reported as a permanent ban or disciplinary suspension.

items.label: Undergoes back surgery after lengthy layoff
items.detail: Gall underwent back surgery shortly before Christmas 2023 after years of severe pain, limited movement, and a competition hiatus dating to April 2022. He later described roughly six weeks of very restricted activity and rehabilitation before returning to training. The UFC account does not identify a verified procedure name.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · May 2024 interview about surgery and recovery

items.label: Returns to Kill Cliff FC training after recovery
items.detail: Gall said his teammates at Kill Cliff FC in Florida welcomed him back during rehabilitation, and he returned to the gym after medical clearance to train. The UFC's current profile still lists Gracie New Jersey; the sources establish training at both gyms, not a precisely dated permanent switch.

items.label: LOSS · Bassil Hafez · return after 26-month layoff
items.detail: Returned to the UFC at UFC 302 in Newark after more than two years away due to surgery and recovery. Lost a unanimous decision to Hafez over three rounds.

items.label: LOSS · Ramiz Brahimaj · first-round knockout
items.detail: Brahimaj knocked Gall out with a right hand at 2:55 of round one at UFC 309 in Madison Square Garden. The defeat extended Gall's UFC losing streak to four.

items.label: Medical-clearance issue cancels scheduled Dumas bout
items.detail: UFC removed Gall from its September 26 middleweight fight with Sedriques Dumas after a fight-week medical issue made him ineligible. Gall said an issue had come back on the medical tests; neither Gall nor the UFC disclosed a specific diagnosis. Luis Hernandez replaced him, and the substitute matchup moved to light heavyweight.

items.label: Medically cleared and rebooked against Zachary Reese
items.detail: MMA Junkie and Heavy reported that Gall received medical clearance and agreed to face Zachary Reese at middleweight October 31. It would be his first completed professional middleweight bout; the canceled September 26 booking against Dumas was also scheduled for the division.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Zachary Reese
items.detail: Booked against Zachary Reese (10–4) at middleweight at Meta APEX, Las Vegas. Gall enters with a 7–7 professional record (6–7 UFC), a four-fight losing streak, and no fights since November 2024. This remains upcoming as of October 26, 2026.

Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani.name: Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani
Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani.subtitle: Career chronology · 13 professional bouts and 7 documented amateur results

items.label: Begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu training with his father
items.detail: Lebosnoyani began Brazilian jiu-jitsu at age three under his father and longtime coach Nono Lebosnoyani, a black belt who trained under Hélio Gracie and coached Royce Gracie. He began competing in BJJ tournaments at five and won age-group titles at IBJJF, NAGA and Gracie Nationals events.

items.label: Wrestles for Mira Costa High School
items.detail: Wrestled all four years at Mira Costa High School in Manhattan Beach, California. His father remained his primary jiu-jitsu coach, and he also trained with Brian Ortega. School reporting from March 2017 describes his participation in the California high-school wrestling championship and professional grappling tournaments.
items.sourceLabel: Mira Costa La Vista · March 2017 firsthand interview; LFA biography

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Andrew Morello · first amateur MMA fight
items.detail: Submitted Morello at 1:12 of round one at Fighters First MMA in San Bernardino. A contemporaneous story from his high-school newspaper identifies the finishing hold as a Peruvian necktie; MMA result databases record it more generally as a submission. It was his amateur MMA debut while still a senior in high school.
items.sourceLabel: Mira Costa La Vista · March 21, 2017 contemporaneous fight report

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Elijah Larkin · second-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Larkin with punches at 0:42 of round two at Spar Star Promotions, moving to 2–0 as an amateur.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Garland Guay · first-round TKO
items.detail: Stopped Guay by TKO (punches) at 1:29 of round one at Fight Club OC: Rumble on the Water.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Anthony Marsh · 22-second guillotine
items.detail: Submitted Marsh by guillotine choke in 0:22 of round one at Celtic Gladiator 13. Some databases use the shortened opponent name Anthony Mars.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Vaughn Tomas Liulama · rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted Vaughn Tomas Liulama at 0:32 of round one at King of the Cage: Never Quit. Other fight registries list him as Vaughn Thomas.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Djavan Coleman · first-round submission
items.detail: Finished Coleman with a submission at 0:43 of round one at Spar Star Promotions. Available fight ledgers do not establish the exact choke or joint lock.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Isaiah Culpepper · Bellator 192
items.detail: Finished Culpepper with an armbar at 2:11 of round three on the Bellator 192 card in Inglewood, California. This was an amateur bout on a major promotional card, not a professional Bellator victory. He ended the seven documented amateur fights undefeated at 7–0.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Official Registry / Combat Registry · amateur record

items.label: WIN · Eugene Cacho · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Made his professional debut at LFA 54, submitting Cacho with a triangle choke at 3:14 of round two. UFC featherweight contender Brian Ortega was in his corner.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional MMA results; LFA career feature

items.label: WIN · Skyler Hicks · first professional knockout
items.detail: Stopped Hicks by TKO (punches) at 2:10 of round one at LFA 69, beginning his professional career 2–0.

items.label: Competes in Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds welterweight tournament
items.detail: Submitted Andrew McInnes by guillotine choke in the opening round of the Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds tournament before losing to eventual champion Kody Steele by rear-naked choke. These were grappling matches under combat jiu-jitsu rules and do not count toward his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: Combat Press · August 2019 CJJ Worlds tournament results

items.label: LOSS · Spike Carlyle · first professional defeat
items.detail: Carlyle knocked Lebosnoyani out with punches at 1:50 of round one at Lights Out Xtreme Fighting 4. It was his first professional MMA defeat after a 2–0 start.

items.label: Approximately 17 months between completed MMA fights
items.detail: Fight records show no completed professional MMA bouts between the Carlyle loss and his April 2021 return. No verified cause for the full absence is established here; his August 2019 combat jiu-jitsu matches predate the gap.

items.label: WIN · Richardson Santos · first-round guillotine
items.detail: Submitted Santos by guillotine choke at 1:14 of round one at LFA 105, returning to winning ways after his November 2019 loss. Some registries shorten the opponent's name to Richard Santos.

items.label: WIN · Devon Brock · first-round triangle
items.detail: Submitted Brock via triangle choke at 2:49 of round one at Lights Out Xtreme Fighting 6, improving to 4–1 professionally.

items.label: WIN · Caleb Hall · scarf-hold armlock
items.detail: Finished Hall with a scarf-hold armlock at 1:21 of round one at LFA 137, his third straight regional MMA victory.

items.label: LFA announces lightweight championship main event
items.detail: The promotion announced Lebosnoyani would fight three-time All-American wrestler JaCobi Jones for its vacant 155-pound title at LFA 158. LFA described him as a BJJ black belt entering at 5–1.

items.label: LOSS · JaCobi Jones · vacant LFA lightweight title
items.detail: Lost to Jones by TKO (punches and elbows) at 2:18 of round two in the LFA 158 main event in Chandler, Arizona. Jones won the vacant LFA lightweight championship. The defeat left Lebosnoyani 5–2 before his subsequent welterweight move.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · LFA 158 official bout result; LFA title announcement

items.label: Moves from lightweight to welterweight
items.detail: Moved from the 155-pound lightweight division to 170-pound welterweight after the JaCobi Jones loss. His next six completed professional fights through July 18, 2026 were all victories; the UFC explicitly describes him as 6–0 since changing divisions.

items.label: WIN · Adam Wamsley · first welterweight victory
items.detail: Knocked out Wamsley with punches at 3:46 of round one at LFA 178, his first completed bout after moving to welterweight.

items.label: WIN · Victor Kuiks · first professional decision
items.detail: Beat Kuiks by unanimous decision over three rounds at LFA 184, earning his first professional MMA victory on the judges' scorecards.

items.label: Announced for LFA 206 welterweight main event
items.detail: LFA officially booked Lebosnoyani against former lightweight champion Kegan Gennrich in a non-title welterweight main event. Both athletes had previously challenged for or held LFA lightweight gold. The booking was not for a welterweight title.

items.label: WIN · Kegan Gennrich · triangle choke in LFA main event
items.detail: Submitted Gennrich by triangle choke at 4:00 of round one at LFA 206 in Prior Lake, Minnesota. His third consecutive welterweight victory came over a former LFA lightweight champion, but it was a non-title fight.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · official LFA 206 bout result; LFA preview

items.label: WIN · Jack Congdon · Contender Series contract
items.detail: Dropped Congdon with a head kick followed by a right hand, winning by KO at 1:08 of round one on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 9, Week 4. The main-event stoppage secured his UFC contract and improved his professional record to 9–2.

items.label: WIN · Phil Rowe · UFC debut via split decision
items.detail: Beat Rowe by split decision in Houston: two judges scored 29–28 for Lebosnoyani while the third had it 29–28 for Rowe. He landed 66 significant strikes, secured three takedowns and held 5:17 of control time in his UFC debut.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Decisions · February 2026 official judges' scorecards

items.label: WIN · Seokhyeon Ko · unanimous 29–28 decision
items.detail: Defeated Ko by unanimous decision in Oklahoma City. All three judges scored the bout 29–28 despite Ko's 66–52 edge in significant strikes; Lebosnoyani landed three takedowns and made two submission attempts. This improved his UFC record to 2–0 and extended his welterweight winning streak to six.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Farman Hasanov
items.detail: Booked against undefeated Azerbaijani prospect Farman Hasanov at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Lebosnoyani enters 11–2 professionally and 2–0 in the UFC, with six straight wins since moving to welterweight. No October 31 bout result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Farman Hasanov.name: Farman Hasanov
Farman Hasanov.subtitle: Career chronology · 6 UFC-recognized professional wins (1 contested classification), 2 documented GAMMA amateur bouts

items.label: Competes in freestyle wrestling for Azerbaijan
items.detail: Hasanov's foundation is freestyle wrestling. The UFC lists him as a Master of Sport in the discipline and says he worked as a wrestler before MMA. No independently verified dates for individual freestyle medals, team selections or national championships are established here.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fighter background and Q&A

items.label: Begins mixed martial arts training
items.detail: Says he took up MMA in 2021 following a lengthy freestyle wrestling background. The year is his own account in the UFC athlete questionnaire, not a date derived from an unverified gym registry.

items.label: WIN · Emil Salimov · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Made his professional debut at ASED Fighting Championship: Selection 2 in Azerbaijan and stopped Emil Salimov with punches at 0:47 of round one. Sherdog, FightMatrix, and Tapology agree on the date and result.

items.label: WIN · Ibragim Sariev · Iron Fist / Olimpia bout
items.detail: Defeated Sariev at Iron Fist Fighting Championship vs. Olimpia in Baku. UFC and FightMatrix include this result in his 6–0 professional record. Tapology calls it a pro MMA win by first-round retirement at 5:00; Sherdog lists it separately as a pro exhibition, TKO (punches) in round two at 1:55. Those classifications, round and time conflict and are not presented as settled.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · bout classification; Sherdog · pro-exhibition result; UFC · overall record

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Yunus Emre Şahbaz · GAMMA European tournament
items.detail: Stopped Turkey's Yunus Emre Şahbaz by TKO (punches) at 2:06 of round two in the GAMMA European MMA Championships at 83.9 kg in Tbilisi, Georgia. This is classified by Tapology as amateur competition despite Hasanov already having fought professional bouts that summer.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · GAMMA European amateur MMA results

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Luka Bregvadze · European championship final
items.detail: Lost to Georgia's Luka Bregvadze by TKO (head kick) at 0:11 of round two in the tournament championship match at approximately 83.9 kg. This was an amateur-format GAMMA bout, not a defeat on his UFC-recognized professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · GAMMA amateur championship fight ledger

items.label: Earns silver at European amateur MMA championships
items.detail: Won silver for Azerbaijan in the 83/83.9 kg category at the GAMMA European MMA Championships held in Tbilisi. A September 29, 2022 Azerbaijani news report names Hasanov as silver medalist; the UFC also recognizes the 2022 amateur European medal. The available databases document two tournament fights here, not a complete lifetime amateur ledger.
items.sourceLabel: SIA Azerbaijan · September 29, 2022 championship medal report

items.label: Moves to the United States and trains at Stout PGH
items.detail: Moved to the U.S. in 2023 and initially trained at Stout PGH in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The UFC confirms this gym as his first American training base. No exact month of relocation is established.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · fighter profile and American training history

items.label: GRAPPLING WIN · Chase Boyde · Stout Fights
items.detail: Beat Chase Boyde in a professional grappling superfight at Stout Fights: BJJ Super Fights in Pittsburgh, contested around 180 pounds. This was a grappling match, not a professional MMA win, and it does not increase his 6–0 MMA record.

items.label: WIN · Luke Roberts · LFA debut at 165-pound catchweight
items.detail: Defeated Roberts by unanimous decision, 30–27 on all three cards, at LFA 177 in Niagara Falls, New York. LFA confirms the bout was a 165-pound catchweight, not a 170-pound welterweight contest.

items.label: Planned fight against Dan Gura does not take place
items.detail: An LFA 202 booking against Dan Gura appears as canceled in Tapology's bout archives. The reason is not reliably documented, so no withdrawal cause or result is assigned.

items.label: Changes training base to American Top Team
items.detail: Moved from Stout PGH to American Top Team in Florida in 2025, according to the UFC's 2026 athlete profile. The official current affiliation is ATT; Sherdog continues to display Renzo Gracie Academy, so the two listings are not treated as proof of a separate recent transfer.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fighter background and camp listing

items.label: WIN · Marc-Ari William Lewis · LFA 211 TKO
items.detail: Stopped Lewis with punches at 3:28 of round two on the LFA 211 preliminary card in Salamanca, New York. LFA's official results shorten the opponent's name to Will Lewis; Sherdog lists Marc-Ari William Lewis. They are the same fight.

items.label: WIN · Abdurakhmon Fazilov · doctor stoppage
items.detail: Defeated Fazilov (also spelled Fozilov) by first-round doctor-stoppage TKO with only two seconds remaining in the round, at 4:58, on the LFA 223 preliminary card in Niagara Falls. Finished his LFA run 3–0.

items.label: Booked for UFC debut against Eric Nolan in Baku
items.detail: Reports confirmed Hasanov would make his UFC debut against Eric Nolan at the UFC's June 27 event in Baku. The fight was announced with Hasanov unbeaten and three consecutive LFA victories.
items.sourceLabel: RotoWire · May 11, 2026 UFC debut booking report

items.label: WIN · Eric Nolan · unanimous decision in UFC debut
items.detail: Made his UFC debut in front of a home crowd in Baku and defeated Eric Nolan by unanimous decision, 30–27 on all three judges' cards. Completed 17 of 27 takedown attempts, with 11:12 control time and 21 significant strikes landed across the three rounds. The dominant wrestling performance moved his UFC record to 1–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Baku official bout statistics via EdgeUp; UFC official result

items.label: Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani matchup reported for October 31
items.detail: RotoWire reported the planned welterweight matchup against fellow UFC newcomer Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani for October 31 in Las Vegas. Both entered with undefeated UFC records (Hasanov 1–0, Lebosnoyani 2–0).

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Jean-Paul Lebosnoyani
items.detail: Scheduled to meet Lebosnoyani (11–2, 2–0 UFC) in a welterweight fight at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. The UFC lists Hasanov as 6–0 overall and 1–0 in the Octagon; Sherdog separately categorizes the 2022 Sariev victory as a professional exhibition and therefore lists five regular professional wins. No October 31 result exists as of October 26, 2026.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official October 31 card and fighter record

Francis Marshall.name: Francis Marshall
Francis Marshall.subtitle: Career chronology · 13 professional fights and 5 documented amateur victories

items.label: Begins MMA training with a goal of reaching the UFC
items.detail: Marshall says he began training around age 14 or 15 with the explicit goal of making fighting his career and eventually competing in the UFC. His UFC profile describes him as a Brazilian jiu-jitsu purple belt and identifies the rear-naked choke and jab as his preferred techniques.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Chris Gholi · knockout
items.detail: Recorded an amateur knockout of Chris Gholi by punch at 0:34 of round three at Dead Serious MMA 29. Sherdog and Tapology both document this fight.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Bryant Pabon · majority decision
items.detail: Defeated Bryant Pabon by majority decision over three three-minute rounds at Dead Serious MMA 30.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Chauncey Randolph · north-south choke
items.detail: Submitted Randolph with a north-south choke at 2:52 of round one at a Primal Fight Promotions event held at a 160-pound catchweight. This amateur result is present on Tapology but absent from Sherdog's shorter four-fight amateur listing.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Nakia Brown · Bayou FC lightweight title bout
items.detail: Submitted Brown via rear-naked choke at 2:33 of round two at Bayou FC 38 (Fightville 4). Tapology lists this as a lightweight championship fight, though the source does not establish whether the belt was vacant. UFC credits Marshall as a Bayou FC amateur lightweight champion.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Bayou FC 38 bout; UFC · amateur title

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Damon Vincent · Bayou FC 40 title bout
items.detail: Stopped Vincent by TKO (punches) at 2:24 of round one at Bayou FC 40. Tapology identifies the bout as a lightweight championship contest and Marshall as the interim champion entering; the distinction between interim and undisputed status is preserved.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Bayou FC 40 amateur title record

items.label: WIN · Keith Forant · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Made his professional debut at Maverick MMA 15, submitting Forant by rear-naked choke at 4:57 of round three. It began a six-fight unbeaten regional/Contender Series professional run.

items.label: Maverick MMA 16 bout with Thad Frick canceled
items.detail: Marshall was scheduled to meet Thad Frick at Maverick MMA 16, but the event was canceled during COVID-19 restrictions. It does not count as a professional bout, and no uninterrupted injury or suspension is inferred from the gap.

items.label: WIN · Jude McNicol · first-round rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted McNicol with a rear-naked choke at 3:38 of round one at Gulf Coast MMA 9, returning to professional competition after the canceled 2020 card.

items.label: WIN · Mike Taylor · first-round submission
items.detail: Submitted Taylor by rear-naked choke at 3:10 of round one at Gulf Coast MMA 10, improving to 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Rey Trujillo · first professional decision
items.detail: Defeated Trujillo by unanimous decision over three rounds at Gulf Coast MMA 11; his first completed professional fight decided by judges rather than a finish.

items.label: WIN · Mike Lawrence · Ring of Combat 75
items.detail: Submitted Lawrence by rear-naked choke at 3:26 of round three at Ring of Combat 75, the fifth win of his unbeaten professional start.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Ring of Combat bout record

items.label: WIN · Connor Matthews · unanimous decision on DWCS
items.detail: Outpointed Matthews by unanimous decision on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 6 Week 2, earning a UFC contract. The scorecards were 30–27, 30–27 and 30–26. He joined the UFC undefeated professionally at 6–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Dana White's Contender Series 2022 result

items.label: WIN · Marcelo Rojo · UFC debut knockout
items.detail: Won his Octagon debut at UFC Orlando with a right hand in the clinch and a finishing hammerfist at 1:14 of round two, handing Rojo a knockout defeat and extending his professional start to 7–0.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · UFC Orlando knockout report

items.label: LOSS · William Gomis · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost a competitive three-round split decision to William Gomis at UFC Fight Night: Pavlovich vs. Blaydes. Two judges scored it 29–28 for Gomis and one 29–28 for Marshall. Gomis' range management frustrated him early; Marshall rallied with grappling attacks in the third.

items.label: LOSS · Isaac Dulgarian · first-round TKO
items.detail: Dulgarian stopped Marshall with punches and elbows at 4:48 of round one at UFC on ESPN: Luque vs. dos Anjos, giving Marshall consecutive defeats.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · UFC on ESPN 51 official result

items.label: Joins American Top Team in South Florida
items.detail: Relocated his principal training camp from New Jersey to American Top Team in South Florida. Marshall described his August 24, 2024 outing as his first fight with ATT in his corner; the precise initial date of relocation is not established.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · March 2025 account of the move

items.label: Replaces Danny Silva against Dennis Buzukja
items.detail: Accepted the Buzukja bout four days before UFC Vegas 96 after Danny Silva withdrew injured. The UFC officially moved the matchup from featherweight to lightweight for the replacement booking.

items.label: WIN · Dennis Buzukja · short-notice split decision
items.detail: Defeated Buzukja via split decision in the 155-pound lightweight bout at UFC on ESPN 62, snapping a two-fight losing streak. Official UFC scorecards were 30–27 and 29–28 for Marshall, 29–28 for Buzukja. The matchup was not contested at the original featherweight limit.

items.label: LOSS · Mairon Santos · controversial split decision
items.detail: Lost to The Ultimate Fighter 32 champion Mairon Santos at UFC 313. One judge gave Marshall all three rounds (30–27), but the other two scored the contest 29–28 for Santos. The 27–30, 29–28, 29–28 cards made it a disputed close decision, not a unanimous loss.

items.label: Leaves Jersey City firefighting job to train full-time
items.detail: Marshall said after his February 2026 victory that he had left his job as a firefighter in Jersey City, New Jersey, moved to Florida and devoted himself full-time to training at American Top Team. The exact date he left the department is not verified.

items.label: WIN · Erik Silva · first-round rear-naked choke
items.detail: Submitted Silva by rear-naked choke at 2:29 of round one at UFC Mexico City, putting him back in the win column after the close Santos decision. This was his first UFC submission victory.

items.label: WIN · Lucas Brennan · unanimous 30–27 sweep
items.detail: Defeated Brennan by unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Sterling vs. Zalal in Las Vegas, winning 30–27 on all three judges' cards. UFC statistics credit Marshall with 6:36 of control time and a 33–9 significant-strike advantage. He entered his next booking on a two-fight winning streak.

items.label: Dakota Hope replaces injured Gaston Bolaños
items.detail: Gaston Bolaños withdrew from his scheduled October 31 fight with Marshall after sustaining an eyebrow laceration during training. MMA Junkie and Heavy reported on October 8 that Dakota Hope had accepted the replacement assignment, not October 23 as previously recorded.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Dakota Hope
items.detail: Booked for a featherweight bout against Dakota Hope (11–2) at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Marshall enters 10–3 professionally (4–3 UFC) and has won two straight fights. No result is recorded as of October 26, 2026.

Dakota Hope.name: Dakota Hope
Dakota Hope.subtitle: Career chronology · 13 professional fights and 3 documented amateur wins

items.label: College wrestling and transition to MMA
items.detail: Wrestled for one year at NCAA Division II New Mexico Highlands University before pursuing an MMA career. The UFC records an undefeated 3–0 amateur MMA career but does not give exact dates for his college enrollment.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Josh Rosen · amateur MMA debut
items.detail: Defeated Josh Rosen by unanimous decision over three three-minute rounds at Valor FL: Brazos Throwdown 4 at featherweight. This bout is in Tapology's longer amateur ledger but is missing from Sherdog's public two-fight amateur list.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Valor FL: Brazos Throwdown 4 event results

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Don Doyle · split decision
items.detail: Earned a three-round split decision over Don Doyle at American Kombat Alliance: Rite of Passage 4. His second documented amateur win.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Justice Torres · five-round decision
items.detail: Beat Justice Torres by unanimous decision over five three-minute rounds at Garcia Promotions: Cage Combat 32, finishing the three documented amateur fights 3–0.

items.label: Develops international fight experience
items.detail: Hope says international teams began sponsoring his fighting career around age 20. He later fought in China and the Philippines, describing the experience of traveling abroad as a central part of his education outside formal college.

items.label: WIN · Jhonmar Sopranes · professional MMA debut in Philippines
items.detail: Debuted professionally at Aspera FC Asia 2, stopping Sopranes by TKO (punches) at 0:55 of round one in the Philippines.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Aspera FC Asia 2 official result

items.label: WIN · Ailiyaer Didaer · 30-second stoppage in China
items.detail: Stopped Didaer by TKO (punches) only 0:30 into round one at Wu Lin Feng W.A.R.S. 32 in China, improving to 2–0.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Wu Lin Feng W.A.R.S. 32 result

items.label: WIN · Shaoxiang Wang · first decision victory
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision against Shaoxiang Wang at Yunfeng Showdown / Global Kung Fu Masters in China. This was the first professional bout in which Hope went to the scorecards.

items.label: WIN · Akenbieke Ayijiake · fourth consecutive victory
items.detail: Beat Akenbieke Ayijiake (also indexed as Ayijiake Akenbieke) by unanimous decision over three rounds at WLF W.A.R.S. 40 in China. This brought his record to 4–0, after one bout in the Philippines and three in China; a fourth documented China appearance followed in November 2024.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · international fight background; Sherdog chronological results

items.label: Professional competition pause between international and domestic bouts
items.detail: Fight records show no completed professional MMA bouts from November 15, 2019 to January 30, 2021. No reliable source establishes a single specific injury or other cause for the whole gap.

items.label: WIN · Colton Hamm · wins vacant Peak featherweight championship
items.detail: Stopped Hamm with punches 0:15 into round one in the Peak Fighting 7 main event in Texarkana, Arkansas, capturing the vacant Peak Fighting featherweight championship. The UFC calls this his first professional title.

items.label: WIN · Patrick Connors · first Peak title defense
items.detail: Submitted Connors by rear-naked choke at 3:25 of round five at Peak Fighting 10, successfully defending his featherweight championship. This is his only recorded professional submission victory and is one of the latest-round submission finishes on his record.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Peak Fighting 10 title result; Sherdog fight ledger

items.label: LOSS · David Bosnick · first professional defeat in separate title challenge
items.detail: Challenged for the American Kombat Alliance featherweight title at AKA: Rite of Passage 19, losing to Bosnick by unanimous decision after five rounds. This was a separate promotion's championship, not a loss of his Peak Fighting belt.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · AKA 19 title bout; Sherdog result

items.label: WIN · Milko Tucto · second Peak featherweight title defense
items.detail: Defeated Tucto by unanimous decision over five rounds in the Peak Fighting Texas co-main event in San Angelo, successfully defending the Peak featherweight championship. It was his second title defense after the Connors fight.

items.label: More than two years without a recorded professional MMA bout
items.detail: There are no completed professional fights between the October 2022 Tucto decision and November 2024 Yongqiang Liu stoppage in the indexed record. A particular injury or contractual reason for this inactivity is not established.

items.label: WIN · Yongqiang Liu · first-round elbow stoppage in China
items.detail: Returned to MMA in China at JCK Fight Night 94 and finished Yongqiang Liu by TKO (elbows) at 1:37 of round one. It was his fifth documented knockout/TKO-related professional victory counting the later 2026 Gomez bout.

items.label: WIN · Jeremy Henry · LFA 210
items.detail: Defeated Henry by unanimous decision over three rounds at LFA 210: Lawrence vs. Reyes, after a return to regular competition in the United States. The fight was at featherweight.

items.label: WIN · Damion Nelson · Fury FC Challenger Series main event
items.detail: Defeated Nelson by unanimous decision in the Fury Challenger Series 15 featherweight main event in Houston. Tapology lists a five-round fight; Sherdog lists a three-round decision. The official completed round count has not been independently reconciled.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · official event listing; Sherdog · competing round count

items.label: Trains at 4oz Fight Club with Daniel Pineda and Joshua Van
items.detail: UFC lists 4oz Fight Club as his gym, Daniel Pineda as his Brazilian jiu-jitsu instructor (purple belt), and UFC fighters Joshua Van and Alden Coria as training partners. Hope has spoken warmly about Van's assistance and influence. The date Hope first joined 4oz Fight Club is not verified.

items.label: WIN · Mauricio Gomez · knockout at Fury FC 116
items.detail: Stopped Gomez with punches at 1:59 of round one at Fury FC 116 in Houston. The Texas commission records this as a TKO; Sherdog labels it KO (punches). Both agree on the result and finish time. The win extended his run to five consecutive victories.
items.sourceLabel: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation · February 20 results; Sherdog

items.label: LOSS · Kai Kamaka III · split decision in UFC debut
items.detail: Made his UFC debut in a 155-pound lightweight bout against Kamaka III at UFC Fight Night: Moicano vs. Duncan. Won the first round on every judge's card and scored the fight's only knockdown, but Kamaka took a split decision (29–28, 29–28, 28–29). Hope landed 106 significant strikes to Kamaka's 105. Hope entered 11–1 and exited 11–2.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · April 2026 official judges' scorecards and bout statistics

items.label: Replaces Gaston Bolaños against Francis Marshall
items.detail: Agreed to step in against Marshall at featherweight after Bolaños suffered an eyebrow laceration in training and withdrew. Marcel Dorff reported the replacement on October 8; the original timeline's October 23 date was incorrect. Hope had previously fought at lightweight in his UFC debut.
items.sourceLabel: Heavy · Marcel Dorff, October 8, 2026 replacement report

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Francis Marshall
items.detail: Booked to face Francis Marshall (10–3, 4–3 UFC) in a featherweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Hope enters 11–2 professionally and 0–1 in the UFC, seeking his first Octagon win. No result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Rodrigo Sezinando.name: Rodrigo Sezinando
Rodrigo Sezinando.subtitle: Career chronology · 10 documented professional bouts, 2 TUF exhibitions and regional titles

items.label: Begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu
items.detail: Started jiu-jitsu to lose weight and developed an interest in competing. He eventually earned a BJJ black belt and won multiple Brazilian jiu-jitsu tournaments.

items.label: Early life and work before professional MMA
items.detail: Raised by a single mother in a Brazilian favela. Worked in sales and as an Uber driver before establishing his fighting career.

items.label: WIN · Matheus Felipe · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Submitted Felipe with a triangle choke at 1:33 of round one at Shooto Brazil 102.

items.label: WIN · Marcos Vinicius
items.detail: Won by punches at 2:54 of round one at Shooto Brazil.

items.label: WIN · Renan Martins Gonçalves
items.detail: Went the full three rounds and won a unanimous decision at Favela Kombat 37.

items.label: WIN · Allan da Silva Pena
items.detail: Finished Pena with a rear-naked choke at 2:51 of round one at Favela Kombat 39.

items.label: LOSS · Willker Lemos
items.detail: Suffered his first professional loss by three-round unanimous decision at Shooto Brazil 112.

items.label: WIN · Saeid Mirzaei
items.detail: Rebounded with a knockout by punches and a knee at 3:21 of round two at Battlefield Fight League 76.

items.label: WIN · Scottie Stockman · BFL championship
items.detail: Won the vacant Battlefield Fight League 165-pound championship with a first-round rear-naked choke at 3:04. BFL's published results confirm the exact finish.

items.label: WIN · Dario Sinagoga · BFL title defense
items.detail: Defended his Battlefield Fight League 165-pound championship by TKO (punches). BFL's own published results record 2:08 of round one, whereas Sherdog records 2:03 of round two; the round and time are disputed between sources.
items.sourceLabel: Battlefield Fight League · official BFL80 results; Sherdog · conflicting result

items.label: Cancelled · Navid Zanganeh · BFL title matchup
items.detail: The scheduled lightweight title bout with Navid Zanganeh at BFL 81 was cancelled after Sezinando did not appear for the official weigh-in. No professional fight result was recorded.
items.sourceLabel: Battlefield Fight League · BFL 81 official card

items.label: WIN · Jonathan Ramsay · Samourai MMA championship
items.detail: Stopped Ramsay with punches at 3:06 of round one at Samourai MMA 12. Lists the Samourai super-welterweight world championship among his professional titles.
items.sourceLabel: UFC biography and Sherdog fight record

items.label: WIN · Diego Bianchini · The Ultimate Fighter 33 quarterfinal
items.detail: Won a two-round unanimous decision representing Team Cormier. This was an exhibition bout and is not counted among his professional results.

items.label: WIN · Jeff Creighton · The Ultimate Fighter 33 semifinal
items.detail: Won a three-round split decision to advance to the welterweight final. Sezinando described it as his toughest fight due to the short turnaround, weight cut and pressure. The bout was an exhibition.

items.label: LOSS · Daniil Donchenko · TUF 33 welterweight final
items.detail: Lost by first-round TKO (punches) at 4:27 at Noche UFC. Unlike the earlier TUF tournament appearances, the televised final counts toward his professional and UFC records.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · vs. Theodor Berggren
items.detail: Scheduled to meet Berggren at UFC Fight Night on October 31. UFC displays 9–2 with four knockouts, two submissions and three decisions; Sherdog documents eight wins and two losses (four knockouts, three submissions and one decision). There is no verified additional named bout. The disagreement in both total wins and method breakdown remains unresolved.

Theodor Berggren.name: Theodor Berggren
Theodor Berggren.subtitle: Career chronology · 12 professional fights, 3 documented amateur bouts and UFC debut

items.label: Begins mixed martial arts training in Sweden
items.detail: Says his mother encouraged him to try MMA after a difficult childhood. He began training in 2017 and eventually joined Renyi.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Khalid Kerchiyev
items.detail: Won a three-round split decision at Fight Club Rush 5, his earliest fight in Sherdog's documented amateur ledger.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · John Odelkvist
items.detail: Submitted Odelkvist with a rear-naked choke in round three at Excellence Fighting Championship 2. Sherdog omits the official finishing time, while another MMA record database lists 0:53 of round three.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Rahmads Stromanis
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision at Fight Club Rush 6. Sherdog documents a 2–1 amateur MMA record; another database omits this defeat.

items.label: WIN · Tobias Wallberg · professional debut
items.detail: Knocked out Wallberg in 1:36 of round one at Fight Club Rush 10.

items.label: WIN · Ebrima Faal
items.detail: Submitted Faal with a first-round rear-naked choke at Fight Club Rush 11. Precise finishing time is not established by Sherdog.

items.label: LOSS · Christian Stigenberg · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision at Fight Club Rush 12.

items.label: Extended gap in professional competition
items.detail: No completed professional MMA bouts are documented between May 2022 and December 2023. A definitive reason for the gap is not independently established.

items.label: WIN · Markus Mäki-Ventelä · return to competition
items.detail: Returned at Battle of Botnia 8 and submitted Mäki-Ventelä with a first-round rear-naked choke.

items.label: WIN · Giorgi Kankava · Battle of Botnia 9 main event
items.detail: Scored a first-round knockout with a punch after the originally scheduled opponent, Dorin Paladi, withdrew. Reliable records do not establish an exact finish time.

items.label: WIN · Kristjan Tõniste
items.detail: Finished Tõniste by rear-naked choke at 2:35 of round one at Fight Club Rush 20.

items.label: WIN · Moein Ahmadi · Fight Club Rush 21 headliner
items.detail: Finished Ahmadi by first-round TKO (punches) at 1:36 in the main event. Extended his winning streak to four.

items.label: LOSS · Justin Burlinson · Cage Warriors 181
items.detail: Lost by arm-triangle choke at 2:44 of round three in Newcastle, ending his four-fight winning streak.

items.label: LOSS · Leonardo Damiani · Fight Club Rush 23
items.detail: Lost a unanimous decision after three rounds in the co-main event, his second straight professional defeat.

items.label: Cancelled Cage Warriors 190 bout · Manuel Del Valle
items.detail: A scheduled Cage Warriors 190 meeting with Manuel Del Valle was cancelled following Berggren's withdrawal; no fight result was recorded.

items.label: WIN · Daniele Battaglia · Cage Warriors 195
items.detail: Stopped Battaglia by TKO (punches) at 4:44 of round two in Rome. Khadim Dia had been the original opponent but withdrew through injury; Battaglia was the replacement.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog fight result; Tapology cancellation record

items.label: WIN · Abdulatip Samedov · Fight Club Rush 27 main event
items.detail: Stopped Samedov by third-round TKO (punches) at 2:20 in Sweden. Berggren singled out this fight against a Dagestani wrestler as a pivotal test of his toughness.

items.label: Short-notice UFC signing · replaces Andreas Gustafsson
items.detail: Received the UFC opportunity on short notice after fellow Swede Andreas Gustafsson withdrew from his scheduled bout with Daniil Donchenko due to medical issues. Berggren entered the UFC at 8–3.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Theodor Berggren Answered the Call, June 25, 2026

items.label: LOSS · Daniil Donchenko · UFC debut in Baku
items.detail: Lost via TKO after a head kick and follow-up punches at 1:35 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Fiziev vs. Torres. His professional record moved to 8–4 and UFC record to 0–1.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · vs. Rodrigo Sezinando
items.detail: Scheduled to face Rodrigo Sezinando in Las Vegas. Both men are coming off losses to Daniil Donchenko. No result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Julian Erosa.name: Julian Erosa
Julian Erosa.subtitle: Career chronology · 44 documented pro bouts (31–13 in Sherdog/Tapology), 4 TUF exhibitions, UFC-listed 31–14

items.label: AMATEUR CAREER · 10–0 reported by UFC
items.detail: Erosa reports an undefeated 10–0 amateur combat-sports record in his UFC questionnaire; complete opponent names and individual bout dates are not independently documented and have not been invented.

items.label: WIN · Angel Diaz
items.detail: Defeated Angel Diaz by KO (punches) at 2:16 of round 1 at CageSport 12.

items.label: WIN · Omar Avelar
items.detail: Defeated Omar Avelar by submission (armbar) at 2:32 of round 2 at CageSport 13.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Mulvihill
items.detail: Defeated Ryan Mulvihill by submission (brabo choke) at 1:23 of round 2 at CageSport 14.

items.label: WIN · John Martinez
items.detail: Defeated John Martinez by TKO (punches) at 3:24 of round 3 at Lords of the Cage.

items.label: WIN · Ernesto Toscano
items.detail: Defeated Ernesto Toscano by unanimous decision after 3 rounds at CageSport 16.

items.label: WIN · Matt Coble
items.detail: Defeated Matt Coble by submission (rear-naked choke) at 3:31 of round 3 at CageSport 17.

items.label: WIN · Jerome Jones
items.detail: Defeated Jerome Jones by submission (armbar) at 4:30 of round 2 at CageSport 18.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Mulvihill · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Ryan Mulvihill by submission (armbar) at 1:48 of round 4 at CageSport 19. Won CageSport featherweight championship, having entered this fight 7–0. A contemporary promoter release describes a guillotine finish at 1:43, conflicting with Sherdog's armbar at 1:48; both agree he won by fourth-round submission.
items.sourceLabel: Halquist Productions · contemporary event account (finish disputed)

items.label: WIN · Jason Gybels
items.detail: Defeated Jason Gybels by KO (punch) at 4:36 of round 1 at CageSport 21.

items.label: LOSS · Drew Brokenshire · career milestone
items.detail: Lost to Drew Brokenshire by unanimous decision after 5 rounds at CageSport 22. Lost his CageSport featherweight championship in his first title defense, a five-round unanimous decision; this was his first professional loss.

items.label: WIN · Jason Gybels
items.detail: Defeated Jason Gybels by submission (triangle choke) at 3:49 of round 2 at CageSport 24.

items.label: LOSS · Lee Morrison
items.detail: Lost to Lee Morrison by unanimous decision after 3 rounds at CageSport 25.

items.label: WIN · Mike Joy
items.detail: Defeated Mike Joy by TKO (punches) at 2:28 of round 2 at CageSport 29.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Mulvihill
items.detail: Defeated Ryan Mulvihill by submission (triangle choke) at 4:19 of round 2 at KOTC: Seek and Destroy.

items.label: WIN · Harrison Bevens · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Harrison Bevens by KO (knee) at 2:10 of round 2 at CageSport 33 / SFL America 2. Captured the vacant CageSport lightweight championship with a knee knockout; event co-promoted as SFL America 2.

items.label: WIN · Drew Brokenshire · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Drew Brokenshire by submission (brabo choke) at 4:35 of round 3 at CageSport 34 / SFL America 3. Reclaimed the CageSport featherweight championship by submitting the man who had taken the belt from him in December 2012. His win also appears under SFL America 3.

items.label: The Ultimate Fighter 22 · Team Urijah Faber
items.detail: Selected for Team Faber in the United States-versus-Europe season coached by Urijah Faber and Conor McGregor; his three exhibition wins and semifinal loss are recorded separately from professional MMA results.

items.label: TUF 22 EXHIBITION WIN · Jason Soares
items.detail: Defeated Soares by majority decision in the two-round entry bout. This was an exhibition and does not count toward his official professional MMA record.

items.label: TUF 22 EXHIBITION WIN · Mehdi Baghdad
items.detail: Won by majority decision over two rounds in the tournament's opening round. Exhibition only.

items.label: TUF 22 EXHIBITION WIN · Abner Lloveras
items.detail: Won a split decision after three rounds to reach the semifinals; was the final surviving Team Faber fighter. Exhibition only.

items.label: TUF 22 EXHIBITION LOSS · Artem Lobov
items.detail: Knocked out by Lobov at 1:00 of round one in the semifinals. Exhibition only; this does not increase his professional loss count.

items.label: WIN · Marcin Wrzosek · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Marcin Wrzosek by split decision after 3 rounds at The Ultimate Fighter 22 Finale. UFC debut following a run to the TUF 22 semifinals; defeated fellow cast member Wrzosek at lightweight.

items.label: LOSS · Teruto Ishihara
items.detail: Lost to Teruto Ishihara by KO (punches) at 0:34 of round 2 at UFC 196. After this loss, Erosa was released by the UFC for the first time.

items.label: WIN · Daniel Swain
items.detail: Defeated Daniel Swain by TKO (doctor stoppage) at 5:00 of round 2 at KOTC: Battle Zone.

items.label: WIN · Austin Springer · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Austin Springer by TKO (punches) at 3:15 of round 2 at Prime Fighting 8. Won the Prime Fighting featherweight championship at Prime Fighting 8.

items.label: LOSS · Paddy Pimblett · career milestone
items.detail: Lost to Paddy Pimblett by unanimous decision after 5 rounds at Cage Warriors: Unplugged. Challenged defending Cage Warriors featherweight champion Paddy Pimblett in London; lost the five-round title fight by unanimous decision (49–46, 48–47, 48–47).
items.sourceLabel: Combat Press · Cage Warriors Unplugged results

items.label: WIN · Justin Harrington · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Justin Harrington by submission (triangle choke) at 2:23 of round 1 at CageSport 44. Won the CageSport lightweight championship against Justin Harrington.

items.label: WIN · Justin Harrington · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Justin Harrington by KO (knees and punches) at 4:09 of round 1 at CageSport 45. Defended the CageSport lightweight championship in an immediate rematch with Harrington.

items.label: LOSS · Bobby McIntyre · career milestone
items.detail: Lost to Bobby McIntyre by TKO (punches) at 3:58 of round 1 at CageSport 46. Lost the CageSport lightweight championship to McIntyre. Tapology reports the same first-round TKO at 3:28, whereas Sherdog has 3:58. The stoppage time is therefore disputed.

items.label: WIN · Erick Sanchez
items.detail: Defeated Erick Sanchez by TKO (punches) at 4:32 of round 3 at Global Knockout 11. Tapology lists this stoppage in round two at 4:36 while Sherdog lists round three at 4:32. Both sources agree Erosa won by TKO, but the round and time conflict.

items.label: WIN · Bryan Nuro · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Bryan Nuro by unanimous decision after 5 rounds at CageSport 48. Won a five-round title bout for the CageSport lightweight championship; Tapology's pre-fight title status is marked as unknown/possibly vacant, so the title's vacancy is not asserted.

items.label: WIN · Jamall Emmers · career milestone
items.detail: Defeated Jamall Emmers by KO (head kick and punches) at 1:10 of round 2 at Dana White's Contender Series S2 W3. Earned a UFC contract for a second stint by stopping Emmers in the second round of Dana White's Contender Series.

items.label: LOSS · Devonte Smith
items.detail: Lost to Devonte Smith by KO (punches) at 0:46 of round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Korean Zombie vs. Rodriguez.

items.label: LOSS · Grant Dawson
items.detail: Lost to Grant Dawson by unanimous decision after 3 rounds at UFC Fight Night: Lewis vs. dos Santos.

items.label: LOSS · Julio Arce · career milestone
items.detail: Lost to Julio Arce by KO (head kick) at 1:49 of round 3 at UFC Fight Night: dos Anjos vs. Lee. Third successive UFC defeat following his Contender Series signing; he was released by the promotion again afterward.

items.label: WIN · A.J. Bryant
items.detail: Defeated A.J. Bryant by submission (bulldog choke) at 4:43 of round 1 at CageSport 60. Scored a first-round bulldog choke on the regional circuit before his next short-notice UFC return.

items.label: Third opportunity after two UFC releases
items.detail: After his first UFC release in 2016 and second after three losses in 2018–19, Erosa unexpectedly returned on three days' notice in 2020. He later described the Woodson win as the most meaningful of his career.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Julian Erosa Changed His Life Forever

items.label: WIN · Sean Woodson
items.detail: Defeated Sean Woodson by submission (d'arce choke) at 2:44 of round 3 at UFC on ESPN: Poirier vs. Hooker. Accepted on approximately three days' notice and rallied for a third-round D'Arce submission after being behind in the fight. His third UFC stint followed two previous releases.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Julian Erosa Changed His Life Forever (2020)

items.label: WIN · Nate Landwehr
items.detail: Defeated Nate Landwehr by TKO (flying knee) at 0:56 of round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Blaydes vs. Lewis. Won by flying knee in under a minute.

items.label: LOSS · Seung Woo Choi
items.detail: Lost to Seung Woo Choi by KO (punches) at 1:37 of round 1 at UFC on ESPN: Korean Zombie vs. Ige.

items.label: WIN · Charles Jourdain
items.detail: Defeated Charles Jourdain by submission (d'arce choke) at 2:56 of round 3 at UFC Fight Night: Brunson vs. Till. Submitted Jourdain with a D'Arce (brabo) choke in round three.

items.label: WIN · Steven Peterson
items.detail: Defeated Steven Peterson by split decision after 3 rounds at UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Strickland.

items.label: WIN · Hakeem Dawodu
items.detail: Defeated Hakeem Dawodu by unanimous decision after 3 rounds at UFC 279. Earned his third consecutive victory and completed a three-fight winning streak against Jourdain, Peterson and Dawodu.

items.label: LOSS · Alex Caceres
items.detail: Lost to Alex Caceres by TKO (head kick and punches) at 3:04 of round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Cannonier vs. Strickland.

items.label: LOSS · Fernando Padilla
items.detail: Lost to Fernando Padilla by TKO (punches) at 1:41 of round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Simon.

items.label: WIN · Ricardo Ramos
items.detail: Defeated Ricardo Ramos by submission (guillotine choke) at 2:15 of round 1 at UFC on ESPN: Ribas vs. Namajunas.

items.label: WIN · Christian Rodriguez
items.detail: Defeated Christian Rodriguez by submission (guillotine choke) at 4:49 of round 1 at UFC on ESPN: Namajunas vs. Cortez. Second straight first-round guillotine victory, following his win against Ricardo Ramos.

items.label: WIN · Darren Elkins
items.detail: Defeated Darren Elkins by TKO (elbow and punches) at 4:15 of round 1 at UFC 314. Completed a three-fight win streak, all by finish, against Ramos, Rodriguez and Elkins.

items.label: LOSS · Melquizael Costa
items.detail: Lost to Melquizael Costa by unanimous decision after 3 rounds at UFC Fight Night: Burns vs. Morales.

items.label: LOSS · Lerryan Douglas
items.detail: Lost to Lerryan Douglas by KO (punches) at 3:33 of round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Adesanya vs. Pyfer. Lost in Seattle; his second consecutive UFC defeat entering the October 31 scheduled matchup.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. JeongYeong Lee
items.detail: Booked to face JeongYeong Lee at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas. UFC currently lists 31–14 overall; Sherdog and Tapology document 31–13 across 44 named professional bouts. UFC record is 9–9. The additional UFC-listed professional loss cannot be matched to a verified bout in those ledgers; no extra fight has been invented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Oct. 31 event; Sherdog · full fight record

JeongYeong Lee.name: JeongYeong Lee
JeongYeong Lee.subtitle: Career chronology · 14 professional fights, 2 documented amateur bouts and Road FC / Road to UFC titles

items.label: Begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu training
items.detail: Started training in BJJ at age 15 because he enjoyed feeling himself get stronger. Went on to earn a jiu-jitsu black belt; he lists the armbar as his favorite submission technique.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Seong Won Jo · first documented MMA bout
items.detail: Defeated Seong Won Jo (also rendered Sung Won Jo) by unanimous decision over two four-minute rounds at Road FC: Into League 11.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jong Tae Hong · first amateur finish
items.detail: Submitted Hong with an armbar at 1:40 of round one at Road FC: Into League 13. These two wins comprise Sherdog's documented 2–0 amateur record.

items.label: WIN · Se Yoon Kwon · professional debut
items.detail: Made his professional MMA debut at Road FC 14, submitting Kwon by armbar at 3:21 of round two.

items.label: Long gap before second documented professional fight
items.detail: No completed professional MMA bouts appear in Sherdog's indexed record between his February 2014 debut and September 2016 return. No single cause for the gap has been independently established.

items.label: WIN · Kyung Yui Cho · 18-second armbar
items.detail: Secured an armbar just 18 seconds into round one at Road FC 33. The UFC cites this as one of his four quickest finishes.

items.label: WIN · Ho Joon Kim · first professional decision
items.detail: Won a two-round split decision at Road FC 35, moving to 3–0.

items.label: LOSS · Se Yeong Kim · first professional defeat
items.detail: Lost to Se Yeong Kim by unanimous decision after two rounds at Road FC 39, dropping to 3–1.

items.label: WIN · Marcio Cesar · Road FC 43
items.detail: Defeated Marcio Cesar by second-round TKO due to a doctor stoppage at 1:44 of the round, beginning his climb back toward Road FC's featherweight title.

items.label: WIN · Se Yeong Kim · avenges first loss
items.detail: Stopped Se Yeong Kim with punches at 3:30 of round one in their Road FC 46 rematch, avenging the unanimous-decision loss from June 2017. The bout was billed as a featherweight contenders match.

items.label: WIN · Mu Gyeom Choi · claims Road FC featherweight championship
items.detail: Defeated reigning champion Mu Gyeom Choi by unanimous decision over three rounds in the main event of Road FC 50 in Daejeon, South Korea. Lee became the promotion's youngest featherweight titleholder, a distinction confirmed by his UFC biography.

items.label: WIN · Hae Jin Park · 10-second Road FC title defense
items.detail: Knocked out Hae Jin Park with a punch only 10 seconds into the first round of their Road FC 55 featherweight championship fight. It was the sole successful defense in Lee's recorded Road FC title reign.

items.label: Nearly three years between professional MMA bouts
items.detail: No completed pro MMA fights are documented after Road FC 55 in September 2019 until his Road to UFC tournament opener in June 2022. The fight-history gap is verifiable, but its full cause is not; it should not automatically be attributed to military service or an injury.

items.label: Road FC featherweight championship reign ends
items.detail: Road FC later awarded its vacant featherweight belt in September 2021. Championship histories describe Lee as having been stripped due to inactivity, but there is no verified contemporaneous announcement date in this timeline.

items.label: WIN · Xie Bin · Road to UFC quarterfinal
items.detail: Submitted Xie Bin with an armbar 36 seconds into round one in Singapore, advancing in the inaugural Road to UFC featherweight tournament.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Road to UFC tournament record

items.label: WIN · Lu Kai · Road to UFC semifinal
items.detail: Knocked out Lu Kai with punches at 0:42 of round one in Abu Dhabi. His two Road to UFC knockout/submission wins took a combined 78 seconds.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Road to UFC tournament record

items.label: WIN · Yi Zha · Road to UFC Season 1 featherweight final
items.detail: Won the inaugural Road to UFC featherweight tournament by split decision against Yi Zha (also listed as Zha Yi) in Las Vegas. Official scorecards were 29–28, 29–28 and 27–30. His two earlier tournament wins were part of his professional record, though some UFC statistics exclude them from regular Octagon totals. The event is also indexed as February 5 in UFC's UTC-oriented display.

items.label: Torn ACL interrupts UFC progress
items.detail: Suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament during a training camp after winning Road to UFC. He needed time to rehabilitate before returning to the Octagon in February 2024.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · JeongYeong Lee Has Superstardom On His Mind (Feb. 2024)

items.label: Trains internationally and prepares for first fight after ACL recovery
items.detail: His UFC athlete profile lists Fight Ready as his training gym; Road FC's historical roster lists Ssen Gym in South Korea. The date of any permanent gym change is not independently established.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete profile; Road FC historical team listing

items.label: WIN · Blake Bilder · first bout after ACL rehabilitation
items.detail: Returned after nearly a year out and won a clear three-round unanimous decision over Blake Bilder at UFC Fight Night: Dolidze vs. Imavov. All three judges scored it 30–27.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · fighter fight history and event result

items.label: LOSS · Hyder Amil · first UFC stoppage defeat
items.detail: Was stopped by Amil's punches at 1:05 of the opening round at UFC on ESPN: Lemos vs. Jandiroba. It was Lee's first career defeat by strikes.

items.label: LOSS · Daniel Santos · UFC 315
items.detail: Lost by unanimous decision to Daniel Santos in Montreal. All three judges scored the fight 30–27 for Santos, giving Lee consecutive losses for the first time in his professional career.

items.label: Accepts short-notice UFC 326 matchup against Gaston Bolaños
items.detail: Agreed to replace the injured Joo Sang Yoo against Gaston Bolaños at UFC 326 on March 7, seeking to rebound from two straight losses.

items.label: Gaston Bolaños fight cancelled over weight-management issues
items.detail: The March 7 featherweight bout was cancelled the day before UFC 326 because of weight-management problems on Lee's side. Bolaños weighed in at 145.5 pounds; Lee did not appear at the official weigh-in. This was not a completed fight and did not change his 11–3 record.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · booked vs. Julian Erosa
items.detail: Scheduled to face veteran Julian Erosa in a featherweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Enters with an 11–3 professional record and a 2–2 record in four UFC main-card/preliminary-card bouts, excluding the first two Road to UFC qualifying rounds. His March 2026 Bolaños bout was cancelled. No fight result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Nick Klein.name: Nick Klein
Nick Klein.subtitle: Career chronology · 9 professional bouts, 8 amateur bouts and Caged Aggression title

items.label: Wrestles at Random Lake High School in Wisconsin
items.detail: Joined the high-school wrestling team as a junior and reached the Wisconsin state championship final in his senior year (2014). He credits the sport and his coach John Hatfield with developing his work ethic.

items.label: Develops his MMA game at Pura Vida BJJ & MMA
items.detail: Trains at Pura Vida BJJ & MMA in Wisconsin; his UFC profile lists freestyle as his fighting style and purple belt as his BJJ rank. The date he first joined Pura Vida is not independently confirmed.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Sean Wallace · MMA debut
items.detail: Started his recorded amateur MMA career with a first-round TKO (punches) at 1:30 at King of the Cage: Stone Cold.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Austin Drabick
items.detail: Scored a TKO (punches) at 3:37 of round one at Victory FC: Fight Night Coco Key 2.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Rob Van Wormer
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision at Pure FC 9, his first documented amateur bout to reach the judges.

items.label: Cancelled amateur booking · Nate Aleo
items.detail: A scheduled bout with Nate Aleo at Pure FC 11 was cancelled. No reason or official result is established in the available record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Manatua Lemaire · LFA 56
items.detail: Submitted Lemaire by rear-naked choke at 2:39 of round one at LFA 56, improving to 4–0 as an amateur.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Kevin Surber · Pure FC 12
items.detail: Won by first-round TKO (injury) at 1:21.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Justin Stuart · 26-second knockout
items.detail: Knocked out Stuart with punches at 0:26 of round one at A-Town Throwdown 15, moving to 6–0.

items.label: AMATEUR LOSS · Nyle Bartling · first MMA defeat
items.detail: Lost by first-round TKO (punches) at 3:18 of round one at DCS 52: Spring Brawl. This was his only documented amateur loss.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Phillip Ahrens · Caged Aggression middleweight championship
items.detail: Captured the Caged Aggression amateur middleweight championship with a heel-hook submission at 2:52 of round five at Caged Aggression 25. Finished his documented amateur run 7–1.

items.label: Cancelled amateur booking · Rodney Nash
items.detail: Was listed against Rodney Nash at 3 River Throwdown 16, but the bout was cancelled. No completed result exists.

items.label: Transitions from amateur to professional MMA
items.detail: There are no completed MMA bouts in the documented record between his August 2019 amateur title win and June 2021 professional debut. No single explanation for the gap has been verified.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · amateur and professional fight chronologies

items.label: WIN · Dan Almario · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Won by TKO due to injury at 0:29 of round one at Pure FC 19. This fight was contracted at heavyweight, rather than his eventual UFC middleweight division.

items.label: WIN · Kacey Joe Sanders · 17-second stoppage
items.detail: Stopped Sanders by TKO (punches) just 17 seconds into round one at Pure FC 21. Klein competed around 208 pounds for this heavyweight booking.

items.label: WIN · Tristan Overvig · LFA 131
items.detail: Went three rounds and won a unanimous decision over Overvig at LFA 131. The bout was at light heavyweight; he weighed in at 202 pounds. This remains his only professional decision victory.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog result; Tapology division and weigh-in

items.label: LOSS · Dorjan Dokaj · first professional defeat
items.detail: Suffered his first professional loss at BTC 16 in Canada, where Dokaj stopped him with punches and ground-and-pound at 1:54 of round three.

items.label: Cancelled booking · Ben Ross
items.detail: A planned middleweight bout with Ben Ross at 3 River Throwdown 19 was cancelled. It is not included in his professional record.

items.label: WIN · Collin Huckbody · Ignite Fights main event
items.detail: Returned against Huckbody, a former Contender Series competitor, at Ignite Fights: No Mercy 11. Won via rear-naked choke at 4:51 of round three. Klein later called it his toughest fight because of the emotional circumstances surrounding the event.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A; Sherdog bout ledger

items.label: WIN · Cory Simpson · MCC 69 main event
items.detail: Submitted Simpson by rear-naked choke just 57 seconds into round one at MCC 69: Thanksgiving Throwdown. The matchup was held at a 195-pound catchweight.

items.label: Cancelled regional booking · Preston LaGrange
items.detail: Had been scheduled to face Preston LaGrange at Caged Aggression 38. The matchup was cancelled when Klein instead accepted a Contender Series opportunity on short notice.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Nick Klein Is Getting Everything He Hoped

items.label: Replaces injured teammate Wes Schultz on Contender Series
items.detail: His Pura Vida teammate Wes Schultz injured a rib in sparring, opening a place opposite Heraldo Souza on the October 15 Contender Series finale. Klein took the fight on eight days' notice while continuing to work construction.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · February 2025 profile and firsthand interview

items.label: WIN · Heraldo Souza · DWCS contract-winning finish
items.detail: Submitted Souza with a rear-naked choke at 0:37 of round one in the season-eight Contender Series finale, earning a UFC contract. The win took his professional record to 6–1.

items.label: LOSS · Mansur Abdul-Malik · UFC debut
items.detail: Faced undefeated Mansur Abdul-Malik at UFC Fight Night: Cejudo vs. Song in Seattle and lost by TKO (knee and punches) at 3:24 of round two. He entered with a 6–1 professional record.

items.label: LOSS · Andrey Pulyaev · second UFC fight
items.detail: After controlling much of round one with wrestling, Klein was stopped by a body kick and punches at 1:31 of round two at UFC on ESPN 71: Taira vs. Park. He dropped to 0–2 in the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Nick Klein: I Belong Here; Sherdog fight result

items.label: Withdraws from scheduled Donte Johnson fight
items.detail: Was removed from a November 1, 2025 UFC Fight Night matchup with Donte Johnson for reasons that were not publicly disclosed. Sedriques Dumas replaced him; no fight took place between Klein and Johnson.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · vs. Joseph Kropschot
items.detail: Scheduled to face Joseph Kropschot at Meta APEX in Las Vegas following an extended layoff since August 2025. Klein enters 6–3 professionally and 0–2 in the UFC; Kropschot is listed at 9–3 professionally. No result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Joseph Kropschot.name: Joseph Kropschot
Joseph Kropschot.subtitle: Career chronology · 12 pro bouts (9–3), 5 amateur wins, LFA title and opponent records at fight time

items.label: Begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu in California
items.detail: Kropschot has described being brought to a jiu-jitsu gym by a friend while attending a continuation school. He says his first gi session left him overwhelmed, but he stayed with the sport and later earned his black belt under Jon Santos.
items.sourceLabel: UFC newcomer interview; Team Santos instructor biography

items.label: Develops BJJ competition and coaching career
items.detail: A black belt under Jon Santos, Kropschot competes in submission grappling and teaches at Team Santos Jiu Jitsu. The gym lists ADCC, Fight to Win and IBJJF tournament wins, but does not provide a dated complete ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Team Santos Jiu Jitsu · instructor biography

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Lawrence Gray II · first documented amateur bout
items.detail: Submitted Gray with a rear-naked choke at 1:48 of round two. This fight appears in Tapology but not Sherdog's shorter amateur list.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Dustin Blythe · 22-second submission
items.detail: Secured a first-round submission 22 seconds into the bout at 559 Fights 53; Sherdog does not specify the particular submission hold.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Diego Lopez · Conquer Fighting Championships 3
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over three rounds at Conquer Fighting Championships 3, the only decision among his five documented amateur victories.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Joseph Cardoso · Conquer FC middleweight title
items.detail: Submitted Cardoso by rear-naked choke at 1:40 of the first round to capture the vacant Conquer Fighting Championships amateur middleweight title at Conquer FC 4.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Noah Christy · Bay Area Combat middleweight title
items.detail: Submitted Christy at 0:44 of the first round to win the vacant Bay Area Combat (BAC) amateur middleweight championship in the BAC 1 main event. Finished his amateur MMA career 5–0, a record also stated by his gym.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: Holds multiple California amateur middleweight titles
items.detail: Team Santos credits Kropschot with the CAMO, Conquer Fighting and Bay Area Combat middleweight championships. His five wins can be individually matched to Tapology; not every championship has a separately verified award date.
items.sourceLabel: Team Santos Jiu Jitsu · instructor biography

items.label: WIN · Inayatullah Siddique · professional debut
items.detail: Opened his professional MMA career at Dragon House 29 with a triangle-choke submission at 2:04 of round one. Tapology indexes his opponent as Chamber Siddique, while Sherdog uses Inayatullah Siddique; both list the same date, promotion and finish.

items.label: WIN · Favian Gutierrez
items.detail: Won at Dragon House 30 by guillotine choke at 1:18 of the opening round, improving to 2–0. Tapology's fight listing shows Favian Gutierrez entering with a 2–0 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: WIN · Tyrese McCloud · first professional TKO
items.detail: Stopped McCloud with punches just 50 seconds into round one at Gladiator Challenge: MMA World Championships. Tapology classifies the matchup as welterweight. Tapology's fight listing shows Tyrese McCloud entering with a 0–4 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: WIN · Marcus Gaines · Combate Americas debut
items.detail: Submitted Gaines by rear-naked choke at 3:13 of round two at Combate Americas: Stockton, beginning his professional career with four straight victories. Tapology's fight listing shows Marcus Gaines entering with a 16–29–1 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: LOSS · Orion Cosce · first professional defeat
items.detail: Suffered his first professional defeat when Cosce stopped him with punches at 3:28 of round three at URCC: Rumble by the Bay. Tapology's fight listing shows Orion Cosce entering with a 3–0 professional record. Cosce subsequently fought in the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: Cancelled Daniel Compton fight · pandemic interruption
items.detail: Booked against Daniel Compton for Zhong Luo Cage Fighting Series 1, but the event was cancelled amid the coronavirus pandemic. The matchup was not a completed fight.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: Cancelled Bellator 242 matchup · Ivan Batinich
items.detail: Was scheduled to meet Ivan Batinich at Bellator 242. The event was cancelled because of the coronavirus pandemic, preventing this planned Bellator appearance.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: LOSS · Cody Brundage · LFA 99
items.detail: Lost by arm-triangle choke at 0:39 of round three against Cody Brundage at LFA 99, moving to 4–2. Tapology's fight listing shows Cody Brundage entering with a 5–1 professional record. Brundage subsequently competed in the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: LOSS · Daniel Compton · third straight defeat
items.detail: Lost to Daniel Compton by first-round knockout/stoppage at Zhong Luo Cage Fighting Series 2.
