Sherdog lists a 0:00 finish time, likely a placeholder, while Tapology lists a first-round TKO without a precise time; the exact stoppage time is not verified. Tapology's fight listing shows Daniel Compton entering with a 3–2 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: Extended gap after three consecutive losses
items.detail: No completed professional MMA fights appear between November 2021 and June 2023. His UFC profile describes a period of renewed commitment to training and grappling, but does not establish a single specific cause for the entire layoff.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · DWCS Season 10 Week 1 fighter preview

items.label: Cancelled comeback booking · Daniel McWilliams
items.detail: A scheduled SF Combat fight against Daniel McWilliams was cancelled. The bout does not count toward his professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: Cancelled matchup · Soslan Margiev
items.detail: An SF Combat meeting with Soslan Margiev was cancelled. Kropschot instead fought Sevak Zadourian at the same SF Combat event.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: WIN · Sevak Zadourian · ends losing streak
items.detail: Returned to competition and stopped Zadourian by first-round TKO at 2:43 at SF Combat 12: Stars and Stripes. The win snapped a three-fight losing streak. Tapology's fight listing shows Sevak Zadourian entering with a 0–1 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: COMBAT JIU-JITSU WIN · Javier Torres
items.detail: Submitted Javier Torres by rear-naked choke at 8:33 in round one at Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds. This is a combat jiu-jitsu contest, not a professional MMA fight.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: COMBAT JIU-JITSU LOSS · Kyle Chambers
items.detail: Lost to Kyle Chambers by Dead Orchard submission at 1:49 in round one of the same Combat Jiu-Jitsu Worlds event. This result is excluded from his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · full bout and cancellation history

items.label: WIN · Mauricio Alonso · Fight Night San Jose 2
items.detail: Submitted veteran Mauricio Alonso by rear-naked choke at 2:58 of round two, starting a run of three consecutive rear-naked-choke victories. Tapology's fight listing shows Mauricio Alonso entering with a 13–8 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: WIN · Adland Benson · LFA 208
items.detail: Submitted Benson with a rear-naked choke at 3:58 of round two at LFA 208: Mecate vs. Reyes. Tapology's fight listing shows Adland Benson entering with a 6–3 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: WIN · David Allakhverdiev · wins LFA middleweight championship
items.detail: Entered as challenger against undefeated champion David Allakhverdiev at LFA 226 in Clarksville, Tennessee. Won the middleweight world title by rear-naked choke at 3:24 of round two, handing Allakhverdiev his first professional loss and improving to 8–3. Tapology's fight listing shows David Allakhverdiev entering with a 7–0 professional record. Allakhverdiev was the defending champion and had not previously lost professionally.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: Prepares for Contender Series at Skrappack and Team Santos
items.detail: UFC's fighter preview identifies Skrappack and Team Santos as his training bases. Team Santos confirms he is a jiu-jitsu black belt under Jon Santos and an instructor; Sherdog separately lists Team Black as his association.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · DWCS athlete preview; Team Santos gym biography

items.label: WIN · Jon (Jonathan) Kunneman · DWCS contract
items.detail: Defeated previously unbeaten Kunneman by unanimous decision (30–27, 30–27, 29–28) in the season-ten Contender Series opener. He jabbed and kicked at range, then nearly finished a late kimura-to-armbar sequence. Kunneman refused to tap despite an apparent serious elbow injury. It was Kropschot's first professional decision victory, taking his record to 9–3. Tapology's fight listing shows Jonathan Kunneman entering with a 10–0 professional record. This was a victory over the reigning APFC middleweight champion, who had finished all 10 of his previous opponents before entering DWCS.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout result; Tapology · opponent record at matchup

items.label: Earns UFC contract following armbar attempt
items.detail: Dana White awarded Kropschot a contract, saying the late submission attempt changed his mind. Four fighters received contracts that week. Some UFC pages count the DWCS victory in a 1–0 UFC display despite his first regular UFC fight being scheduled for October 31.

items.label: Discusses first UFC booking and personal milestone
items.detail: In a September interview Kropschot said his father had died before his DWCS bout and described preparing for his first UFC fight. He also said he planned to marry his longtime partner on November 5, five days after the scheduled October 31 event.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · promotional debut vs. Nick Klein
items.detail: Booked to face Nick Klein (6–3, 0–2 in regular UFC bouts) in a middleweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Kropschot enters 9–3 professionally, with five straight wins. His UFC athlete page displays 1–0 based on his DWCS victory, although this is scheduled to be his first regular UFC fight; no October 31 result exists as of October 26.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official October 31 fight card; Sherdog · booking confirmation

Talita Alencar.name: Talita Alencar
Talita Alencar.subtitle: Career chronology · 10 professional MMA bouts, reported 1 amateur win, major BJJ titles and UFC stats

items.label: Begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu in Fortaleza
items.detail: Born in Carutapera, Maranhão, she spent her childhood practicing several sports, including swimming and triathlon. She took up jiu-jitsu in 2004 at Pirillo Roriz's academy in Fortaleza before moving to other Brazilian teams.

items.label: IBJJF World No-Gi champion at purple belt
items.detail: Won the IBJJF No-Gi World Championship and American Nationals as a purple belt. Earlier results included Brazilian Nationals silver in 2012 and a blue-belt Rio Open title in 2013.

items.label: Wins brown-belt world title and receives black belt
items.detail: Won the IBJJF World Championship at brown belt and was promoted to black belt by Júlio César Pereira, with the consent of longtime coach Theodoro Canal, at the tournament podium.

items.label: Moves to California and joins Cobrinha's Alliance academy
items.detail: Left GF Team after receiving her black belt, moving to Los Angeles to train at Alliance Academy with Rubens Charles 'Cobrinha'. Her later MMA affiliations include Fight Sports Deerfield Beach and Temple Martial Arts; exact team-change dates are not fully documented.

items.label: Wins IBJJF No-Gi world title as a black belt
items.detail: Won her first recorded black-belt IBJJF No-Gi World Championship, later repeating the accomplishment in 2017 and 2021.

items.label: Wins IBJJF gi world title and Abu Dhabi World Pro
items.detail: Won the IBJJF World Championship, Pan Championship, UAEJJF Abu Dhabi World Pro and Abu Dhabi Grand Slam in 2017, as well as another No-Gi world title. These were grappling accomplishments rather than MMA bouts.

items.label: Continues elite-level grappling competition
items.detail: Finished runner-up at the 2018 IBJJF World Championships; won 2019 European and Pan No-Gi titles, and claimed a third black-belt No-Gi world championship in 2021. These tournament results do not affect her professional MMA record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · sole reported amateur MMA bout
items.detail: In her official UFC athlete questionnaire Alencar reports one amateur MMA fight, which she won. The opponent, event, method and exact date were not sufficiently documented to add fabricated fight details.

items.label: Transitions from grappling to professional MMA
items.detail: Pursued MMA to test her skill set after establishing herself as a world-class grappler. Her UFC questionnaire states she trained MMA for several years before joining the promotion; 2021 is her professional debut year, not necessarily the year MMA training began.

items.label: WIN · Staci Vega · professional debut
items.detail: Submitted Vega by rear-naked choke at 4:14 of round one at Titan FC 70. This was the first of three consecutive Titan FC victories by rear-naked choke; her opponent was listed as 0–1–1 before the bout by an opponent-history database.

items.label: Cancelled matchup · Yasmeli Araque
items.detail: A listed Titan FC 75 bout against Yasmeli Araque was cancelled. She instead fought Laura Milena Contreras on the card; the cancellation is not a professional bout.

items.label: WIN · Laura Milena Contreras · Titan FC 75
items.detail: Submitted Contreras by rear-naked choke at 3:39 of round three. The opponent-history listing has Contreras at 1–1 entering the fight.

items.label: WIN · Karen Quintero · Titan FC 78
items.detail: Won by rear-naked choke at 1:54 of round one, completing a 3–0 Titan FC run. Some MMA databases report 1:45 instead; Sherdog's 1:54 is used here, with the timing discrepancy noted. Quintero was listed at 1–1 entering the bout.

items.label: WIN · Kelsey Arnesen · LFA 156
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision in her LFA debut, the first professional fight in which she reached the scorecards. Arnesen entered 2–2 in the opponent-history listing.

items.label: DRAW · Stephanie Luciano · Contender Series
items.detail: Fought Luciano to a three-round unanimous draw at DWCS Season 7 Week 7. Alencar entered at 4–0 and Luciano was listed at 5–1, so the draw left Alencar unbeaten without recording a win. The draw is included in her overall 8–1–1 record, but not her standard UFC 4–1 record.

items.label: WIN · Rayanne dos Santos · UFC debut
items.detail: Won a split decision (29–28, 29–28, 28–29) at UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Gutierrez. Her opponent is also indexed as Rayanne Amanda and was listed at 14–6 entering; Alencar moved to 5–0–1 overall.

items.label: LOSS · Stephanie Luciano · UFC rematch
items.detail: Lost a three-round unanimous decision in their UFC rematch, suffering her only professional MMA defeat to date. The pair had previously fought to a draw on Contender Series. Opponent-history data lists Luciano at 5–1–1 entering the rematch.

items.label: WIN · Vanessa Demopoulos · UFC on ESPN 65
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision, rebounding from the Luciano loss. Demopoulos was listed at 11–6 entering, making her one of Alencar's more experienced UFC opponents.

items.label: GRAPPLING LOSS · Cassia Moura · UFC BJJ 1
items.detail: Competed at the inaugural UFC BJJ event at 125 pounds, losing a unanimous decision to Cassia Moura after three grappling rounds. This was a professional jiu-jitsu match, not an MMA defeat; her MMA record remained unchanged.

items.label: WIN · Ariane Carnelossi · first UFC submission
items.detail: Finished Carnelossi by rear-naked choke at 4:36 of round three at UFC Fight Night: Garcia vs. Onama. Carnelossi entered 15–3 according to the opponent-history record, and Alencar earned her first submission inside the UFC.

items.label: WIN · Julia Polastri · third straight UFC victory
items.detail: Won by unanimous decision, 29–28 on all three scorecards, at UFC Fight Night: Sterling vs. Zalal. The previously completed opponent ledger lists Polastri at 14–5 entering; she has since continued competing. It was Alencar's third consecutive UFC win.

items.label: Professional MMA and UFC statistical snapshot
items.detail: Through April 25, 2026 she has ten professional MMA appearances (8–1–1), with four submission and four decision victories. UFC record: 4–1; all four career submissions came by rear-naked choke. UFCStats-attributed regular UFC averages across five bouts: 3.24 significant strikes landed and 3.24 absorbed per minute, 36% striking accuracy, 54% striking defense, 2.82 takedowns per 15 minutes, 38% takedown accuracy, 100% takedown defense (a small two-attempt sample) and 0.60 submission attempts per 15 minutes. These rates exclude her DWCS draw and independent BJJ matches.
items.sourceLabel: UFCStats · five-fight sample; Sherdog · overall record

items.label: UFC Fight Night · vs. Piera Rodriguez
items.detail: Booked against Piera Rodriguez (12–2) in a women's strawweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Enters 8–1–1, on a three-fight MMA winning streak. No result has occurred as of October 26, 2026.

Piera Rodriguez.name: Piera Rodriguez
Piera Rodriguez.subtitle: Career chronology · 14 professional fights, 1 documented amateur win, LFA title, UFC statistical records

items.label: Begins taking recreational boxing classes
items.detail: Says she tried boxing for fun in 2012. She did not begin taking combat sports seriously until after completing her education.

items.label: Transitions into fighting while working
items.detail: After completing a university degree in psychology, she worked as a restaurant waitress and began pursuing fighting more seriously while employed. Born in Maracaibo, Venezuela, she later developed her MMA career across Panama, Spain and the United States.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and LFA background

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jessica Artavia · sole documented amateur bout
items.detail: Defeated Jessica Artavia by unanimous decision after three three-minute rounds at Ultimate Combat Challenge 31 in Panama. Sherdog lists this one amateur result; it is not part of her 12–2 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Karol Naranjo · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Began her professional career at Panama Fight League's Ultimate Combat Challenge: Fantastic Fight Night 5, winning by TKO (doctor stoppage) at 5:00 of round two. Karol Naranjo · professional MMA debut entered at 0–0 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Lina Franco
items.detail: Stopped Franco by TKO (punches) at 4:41 of round three at Panama Fight League's Fantastic Fight Night 7. Lina Franco entered at 3–1 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Carmen Virginia Arancibia
items.detail: Won by second-round TKO (punches) at 2:07 at AFL 17: Coal and Blood in Spain. Some alternate databases give 3:10; Sherdog gives 2:07. Carmen Virginia Arancibia entered at 0–0 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Yamila Sanchez
items.detail: Knocked out Sanchez with punches at 1:27 of round two at Vida Fight Championships 1. Yamila Sanchez entered at 1–2 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Kayla Hracho · first decision win
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision at UCC 48 in Panama, moving to 5–0 professionally. It was her first win without a stoppage. Kayla Hracho · first decision win entered at 1–0 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: Original LFA title opportunity changes after Lupita Godinez signs UFC contract
items.detail: LFA had planned to match undefeated Rodriguez with reigning 115-pound champion Lupita Godinez. Godinez instead signed with the UFC, vacating the LFA strawweight belt. Rodriguez was then matched against Svetlana Gotsyk for the vacant championship at LFA 105.

items.label: WIN · Svetlana Gotsyk · vacant LFA strawweight championship
items.detail: Scored a TKO (punches) at 1:16 of round five in the LFA 105 main event in Shawnee, Oklahoma, capturing the vacant LFA strawweight title. The Ukrainian Gotsyk entered at 13–4; Rodriguez improved to 6–0.
items.sourceLabel: LFA · title bout announcement; Sherdog · fight result

items.label: WIN · Valesca Machado · Dana White's Contender Series
items.detail: Won by unanimous decision over three rounds at DWCS Season 5 Week 8, receiving a UFC contract. Machado entered 8–2 with one no contest. This fight counts toward her professional 12–2 record but is separate from her 5–2 UFC record.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Contender Series official recap and pre-fight records

items.label: Enters UFC undefeated as former LFA champion
items.detail: Signed with the UFC after a 7–0 start that included five TKO/KO wins and two decisions. Her UFC run has subsequently been defined more by striking volume, wrestling and control than by knockouts.

items.label: WIN · Kay Hansen · UFC debut
items.detail: Beat Hansen by unanimous decision at UFC 273, landing three takedowns and winning her first regular UFC fight. Hansen entered at 7–5. Kay Hansen · UFC debut entered at 7–5 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Sam Hughes · first meeting
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Grasso vs. Araujo, completing five takedowns. Hughes entered at 7–4; the pair would meet again in March 2026. Sam Hughes · first meeting entered at 7–4 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: LOSS · Gillian Robertson · first career defeat
items.detail: Was submitted by armbar at 4:21 of round two at UFC on ESPN: Holloway vs. Allen. Robertson entered 11–7. This remains Rodriguez's only loss by a legal fight-ending technique. Gillian Robertson · first career defeat entered at 11–7 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: LOSS · Ariane Carnelossi · disqualification
items.detail: Disqualified for illegal headbutts at 3:16 of round two at UFC Fight Night: Barboza vs. Murphy. This was an official loss, but neither a decision defeat nor a knockout/submission loss. Carnelossi entered at 14–3. Ariane Carnelossi · disqualification entered at 14–3 according to Verdict's opponent history.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · bout history; Verdict · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Josefine Knutsson · returns against undefeated prospect
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over the previously unbeaten 8–0 Knutsson at UFC on ESPN: Covington vs. Buckley. Rodriguez scored eight takedowns in ten attempts with 10:24 control time, recovering from two consecutive official losses.
items.sourceLabel: UFC statistics · bout totals; Verdict · pre-fight record

items.label: WIN · Ketlen Souza · split decision and seven takedowns
items.detail: Won a split decision (29–28, 28–29, 29–28) against Souza, who entered at 15–5, at UFC Fight Night: Taira vs. Park. Rodriguez landed seven of ten takedowns and recorded 4:36 control time; UFC's event recap describes six trips to the canvas, a difference from the official seven-takedown statistical tally.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official results and fight statistics

items.label: WIN · Sam Hughes · wins rematch by three 30–27 cards
items.detail: Beat Hughes (11–6 entering) by unanimous decision in their second meeting at UFC Fight Night: Emmett vs. Vallejos. All three judges scored 30–27. Rodriguez outlanded Hughes 107–77 in significant strikes, hit one of six takedowns, and defended all seven takedown attempts against her.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official March 14 recap; UFC fight statistics

items.label: UFC career metrics and strawweight record-book standing
items.detail: Across seven regular UFC appearances through March 14, 2026 (92:37 fight time), Rodriguez has landed 392 of 807 significant strikes (48.6%), averaging 4.23 landed and 3.25 absorbed per minute. She completed 26 of 44 takedowns (59.1%, 4.21 per 15 minutes), defended 18 of 22 attempts against her (81.8%), and recorded zero submission attempts. The UFC's active-fighter women's strawweight record book ranks her first in takedown accuracy and third in takedown defense among those meeting minimum eligibility requirements. UFC lists her reach at 63.5 inches; UFCStats-derived data displays 63 inches.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · women's strawweight record book; UFCStats-based totals

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Talita Alencar
items.detail: Booked against Talita Alencar (8–1–1, UFC 4–1) in a women's strawweight matchup at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Entering on three consecutive unanimous/split decision wins; the match has not taken place as of October 26, 2026.

Lucia Szabova.name: Lucia Szabova
Lucia Szabova.subtitle: Career chronology · 10 standard professional bouts (10–0), 2 OKTAGON Challenge qualifiers (12–0 promotional record), title history and opponent records

items.label: Develops judo and Muay Thai background in Slovakia
items.detail: Practiced judo from a young age and became a Slovak national Muay Thai champion. OKTAGON credits her with winning the 2018 Slovak Open. She trains at Hanuman Gym Bratislava.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Kamila Bałanda · Ladies Fight Night 9
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision in an identified kickboxing contest; this result is separate from her professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING WINS · Zarina Apakova, Paola Cappucci, Tereza Dvořáková
items.detail: Won three separate unanimous decisions at Bigger's Better on the same date. UFCalendar documents a 4–0 kickboxing record including the May 2018 Bałanda win; these are not MMA victories.

items.label: OKTAGON CHALLENGE WIN · Kamila Eliášová · quarterfinal
items.detail: Submitted Eliášová by armbar at 1:31 of the first round in OKTAGON Challenge qualification. Tapology, Verdict and OKTAGON include this victory in the 12–0 record; Sherdog and UFC exclude the two 2019 qualifier bouts from their standard 10–0 professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · competition classification; Verdict · opponent record

items.label: OKTAGON CHALLENGE WIN · Michaela Dostálová · semifinal
items.detail: Stopped Dostálová by TKO (punches) at 4:28 of round one in OKTAGON Challenge qualification. Dostálová entered 1–0 according to Verdict. As with the preceding qualifier, this win is included in the broader 12–0 promotional tally but not the Sherdog/UFC 10–0 standard professional MMA record.

items.label: UNDERGROUND EXHIBITION WIN · Paula Marčišová
items.detail: Won by a first-round submission in a modified-rules OKTAGON Underground bout that prohibited ground strikes. Tapology labels the contest an MMA exhibition; sources disagree on exact finishing seconds, so no finishing time is asserted.

items.label: UNDERGROUND EXHIBITION WIN · Lucia Krajčovič
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision under modified OKTAGON Underground rules. Exhibition result only, not part of either 10–0 or 12–0 professional tally.

items.label: UNDERGROUND EXHIBITION LOSS · Tereza Bledá
items.detail: Lost a split decision to Tereza Bledá in the OKTAGON Underground Super Final. This is a modified-rules exhibition, not an official professional MMA defeat; Szabová remains unbeaten in the standard professional record.

items.label: WIN · Anzelika Petkevičiūtė
items.detail: Won her first bout recognized in the Sherdog/UFC standard professional MMA ledger with a first-round armbar at 0:43 at OKTAGON 18. Anzelika Petkevičiūtė entered this bout at 0–1 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: WIN · Rizlen Zouak
items.detail: Finished Zouak with an armbar at 1:25 of round two at OKTAGON 21. Rizlen Zouak entered this bout at 3–1 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: WIN · Christina Netza
items.detail: Scored a head-kick knockout at 1:30 of the opening round at OKTAGON 22. Christina Netza entered this bout at 3–1 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: WIN · Cornelia Holm
items.detail: Went three full rounds and won by unanimous decision at OKTAGON 26. This was her first conventional professional MMA bout to reach the judges' scorecards. Cornelia Holm entered this bout at 4–3 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: Maternity leave and return to training
items.detail: Following the Holm victory, Szabová stepped away from professional MMA due to pregnancy and the birth of her son, Dragan. She continued her martial-arts activity during part of that period and later spoke publicly about juggling work, motherhood and her comeback. She returned to professional MMA on March 23, 2024, after almost three years.

items.label: MUAY THAI LOSS · Michaela Hlaváčiková
items.detail: Lost a split decision at MTO Fight Night. This was Muay Thai rather than professional MMA and does not affect her unbeaten MMA record.

items.label: MUAY THAI WIN · Alexandra Andersröd
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision in the modified-rules underground striking bout at OKTAGON 47, returning to competition during her break from MMA.

items.label: MUAY THAI WIN · Marcela Šafránová
items.detail: Won by unanimous decision at Hanuman Cup 46. This belongs to her Muay Thai record, not her pro MMA results.

items.label: WIN · Róża Gumienna
items.detail: Returned after maternity leave at OKTAGON 55 in Stuttgart and secured an armbar at 4:38 of round three. This was her fifth standard professional MMA win. Róża Gumienna entered this bout at 5–3 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: GRAPPLING LOSS · Eva Erdélyiová
items.detail: Lost an independently listed submission-grappling contest by submission at 6:26 of round one at Hanuman Cup 47. This is not counted as professional MMA.

items.label: WIN · Aitana Álvarez
items.detail: Won a unanimous decision over three rounds at OKTAGON 59 in Bratislava, moving to 6–0 in the standard ten-bout pro ledger. Aitana Álvarez entered this bout at 6–5 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: WIN · Kalindra Faria
items.detail: Submitted experienced former UFC and Invicta fighter Faria by keylock (standing Americana) at 4:16 of round one at OKTAGON 67. Her opponent had 30 prior professional MMA bouts. Kalindra Faria entered this bout at 19–10–1 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: WIN · Cecilie Maria Bolander
items.detail: Won the OKTAGON women's bantamweight title with a first-round TKO (elbows and punches from mount) at 3:11 at OKTAGON 74. Bolander entered as the reigning champion. Cecilie Maria Bolander entered this bout at 4–1 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional bout results; Verdict · pre-fight opponent record

items.label: FLYWEIGHT TITLE BOUT CANCELLED · Leidiane Fernandes injured
items.detail: Originally scheduled to meet Fernandes for the vacant OKTAGON flyweight title at OKTAGON 84. Fernandes withdrew because of injury, and the matchup was rebooked for April. The February cancellation is not a separate fight result.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · cancelled bout listing and event notes

items.label: WIN · Leidiane Fernandes
items.detail: Stopped Fernandes by elbows and punches from mount at 2:12 of round three at OKTAGON 87, winning the vacant OKTAGON women's flyweight championship in the main event. She became the organization's first simultaneous women's two-division titleholder. Leidiane Fernandes entered this bout at 7–2 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.
items.sourceLabel: OKTAGON · dual-champion biography; Verdict · opponent record

items.label: WIN · Lucie Pudilová
items.detail: Defended the OKTAGON women's bantamweight title by unanimous decision after five rounds in Prague at OKTAGON 92. Pudilová is a two-time UFC veteran and the most experienced opponent on Szabová's record. The victory left Szabová at 10–0 on Sherdog and 12–0 on OKTAGON/Verdict. Lucie Pudilová entered this bout at 17–11 according to Verdict's opponent ledger.

items.label: Confirms UFC move after defending two OKTAGON belts
items.detail: Confirmed to Slovak outlet ŠPORT.sk that she was leaving OKTAGON for the UFC, after her five-round title defense over Lucie Pudilová. OKTAGON promoter Ondřej Novotný publicly backed the move, and contemporary reporting identified her as the first Slovak woman set to compete in the UFC.

items.label: Career statistics and cross-source record check
items.detail: Standard professional MMA tally: 10–0, with three KO/TKO wins, four submissions and three decisions (70% finishing rate). OKTAGON, Tapology and Verdict also count two 2019 Challenge qualifiers, making their tally 12–0 with four KO/TKO wins, five submissions and three decisions (75% finishing rate). Verdict's opponent-history ledger gives individual opponents' pre-fight records; bouts under modified Underground rules, Muay Thai, kickboxing and grappling are excluded. She has no completed regular UFC bouts, so UFC significant-striking, takedown and submission-attempt averages are not yet available.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · standard MMA results; Verdict · expanded records

items.label: UFC FIGHT NIGHT · debut vs. Tainara Lisboa
items.detail: Booked for a women's flyweight contest with Tainara Lisboa (7–4, 2–2 in UFC) at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. The UFC's October 26 preview describes Szabová as 10–0 with seven finishes and identifies this as her UFC debut. No result exists as of October 26, 2026.

Tainara Lisboa.name: Tainara Lisboa
Tainara Lisboa.subtitle: Career chronology · 11 pro MMA bouts (7–4), two Muay Thai world titles, verified opponent histories, knee surgery and UFC statistics

items.label: Begins Muay Thai in Santos, Brazil
items.detail: Lisboa says her father, who practiced taekwondo, encouraged her to take up Muay Thai around age 13 or 14 to manage anxiety and lose weight. She had her first trial fight at 14 and joined a competitive Muay Thai team at 16.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Welcome to the UFC; Sherdog · first-person interview

items.label: MUAY THAI/KICKBOXING · bouts listed against Valentina Shevchenko
items.detail: Tapology-linked event records list a Muay Thai decision loss to Valentina Shevchenko on April 10 at Inka FC 8 and a kickboxing decision loss on October 4 at INKA Fight Championship. Other Muay Thai databases only document the October contest. Lisboa says a decision against Shevchenko was controversial and was overturned to a no-contest following an appeal, but independent confirmation of the reversal was not found. Neither striking result affects her professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Lisboa's account; Muay Thai historical results

items.label: Two professional Muay Thai world titles in Thailand
items.detail: Won two professional Muay Thai world championships in Thailand and multiple Brazilian, South American and state titles. She reports a Muay Thai black belt. UFC lists her as a BJJ purple belt and CBJJE no-gi world champion; championship years and complete striking-bout records remain unverified.

items.label: Turns to professional MMA after a long Muay Thai career
items.detail: Says she sought a new challenge after reaching her Muay Thai goals and began developing an MMA game under longtime coach Bruno Polengo. She also supported herself by giving private classes.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · first-person 2023 interview; UFC · athlete background

items.label: LOSS · Norma Dumont · professional MMA debut
items.detail: Lost by rear-naked choke at 2:58 of round one at Jungle Fight 90 in São Paulo. Both fighters entered the bout at 0–0; Dumont later competed in the UFC. Norma Dumont · professional MMA debut entered at 0–0 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · completed result; Tapology · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: Three-year gap between first two documented professional MMA bouts
items.detail: There are no completed professional MMA bouts listed between September 2016 and September 2019. Lisboa continued developing her mixed martial arts game and has discussed difficulty booking fights with her striking background, but a specific uninterrupted cause for the entire gap is unverified.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · professional ledger; MMA Fighting · 2023 interview

items.label: WIN · Mara Suzamaque · first professional victory

items.detail: Lost by unanimous decision over three rounds in Shooto Brazil. This was her second defeat, moving her to 2–2. Lorrany Santos · Shooto Brazil 103 entered at 2–1 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.

items.detail: A planned fight at JFC 3 against Larissa Vaz was cancelled. It is not included in her professional results.

items.label: WIN · Gloria Natalia Vaz Amaral · third professional TKO
items.detail: Finished Amaral with punches at 3:48 of round one at Dog Tower Fight 3. This was the second of what became a five-fight winning streak. Gloria Natalia Vaz Amaral · third professional TKO entered at 0–1 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.

items.detail: Submitted Oliveira with an arm-triangle choke at 4:20 of round one at Iron Man MMA 23. The original article's recent-form entry had a truncated description and has been corrected. items.label: Signs with UFC after rebuilding record to 5–2
items.detail: Entered UFC on a three-fight regional winning streak and worked with coach Bruno Polengo at Damas 013. Her UFC debut took place at bantamweight; the October 2026 matchup is booked for flyweight.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · fighter introduction and career Q&A

items.label: WIN · Jessica-Rose Clark · UFC debut
items.detail: Submitted UFC veteran Clark via rear-naked choke at 4:20 of round three at UFC on ABC 4: Rozenstruik vs. Almeida. Lisboa landed 42 significant strikes (of 83 attempted), completed one takedown and secured 2:09 of control time. Clark had eight UFC fights before facing her. Jessica-Rose Clark · UFC debut entered at 11–8 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.

items.label: Darya Zheleznyakova booking cancelled; replacement opponent
items.detail: Had been booked to meet Darya Zheleznyakova at UFC Fight Night: Yusuff vs. Barboza, but Zheleznyakova withdrew and Lisboa instead met Ravena Oliveira.

items.label: WIN · Ravena Oliveira · second UFC win
items.detail: Won a three-round unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night: Yusuff vs. Barboza. Landed 18 significant strikes (35 attempted), completed three of eight takedowns and logged 6:55 in control time. This was her fifth consecutive MMA victory. Ravena Oliveira · second UFC win entered at 7–1–1 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · completed result; Tapology · opponent's pre-fight record

items.label: Serious left-knee injury, cartilage surgery and rehabilitation
items.detail: Lisboa was dealing with knee pain around her 2023 UFC schedule and underwent cartilage-reconstruction surgery in December 2023. She lost substantial thigh muscle, struggled with walking and stairs, and considered retirement. She was unable to train MMA during much of the rehabilitation and missed approximately 19 months of UFC competition, from October 2023 to May 2025.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · May 2025 injury interview; UFC · return interview

items.label: Works as a UFC Fight Pass commentator during recovery
items.detail: Lisboa remained connected to MMA through broadcast commentary and worked toward her return under coach Bruno Polengo while rehabilitating the knee injury.

items.label: LOSS · Luana Santos · comeback after knee surgery
items.detail: Lost by americana (keylock) submission at 4:59 of round two in Las Vegas. Luana, a judo-based grappler, completed two takedowns and accumulated 7:57 control time; Lisboa landed six significant strikes (34 attempted) and did not complete a takedown. Luana Santos · comeback after knee surgery entered at 8–2 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · completed result; Tapology · opponent's pre-fight record

items.detail: Lost by TKO (punches) at 4:32 of round three at UFC Fight Night: de Ridder vs. Allen in Vancouver. Croden outlanded Lisboa 99–42 in significant strikes, completed two takedowns and had 5:05 control time. Lisboa completed two of eight takedown attempts. Melissa Croden · first MMA KO/TKO defeat entered at 6–2 according to Tapology's fight-by-fight records.

items.date: 2026 (published interview; exact date of weight change unverified)
items.label: Targets first UFC appearance at flyweight
items.detail: Told FightNews Portugal she planned to move down from bantamweight to the 125-pound (57 kg) flyweight division and return to winning form. All four completed UFC bouts to this point had been contested at bantamweight.

items.label: Official statistical snapshot after four UFC fights
items.detail: Professional record 7–4: three KO/TKO wins, three submission victories and one decision; 6/7 wins by finish (85.7%). UFC record 2–2 across 53:51 of Octagon time. UFCStats-derived career averages: 2.01 significant strikes landed and 2.88 absorbed per minute; 44% striking accuracy, 46% defense; 1.67 takedowns per 15 minutes, 32% takedown accuracy, 53% takedown defense and 0.30 submission attempts per 15 minutes. The sample is only four fights.

items.label: UFC Fight Night · scheduled vs. Lucia Szabova
items.detail: Set to face Lucia Szabova in a women's flyweight bout at Meta APEX in Las Vegas. Szabova holds the 10–0 UFC/Sherdog professional record or 12–0 OKTAGON/Tapology record including two 2019 qualifier wins. Lisboa enters on two UFC stoppage losses after knee surgery and is seeking her first flyweight UFC victory. No result exists as of October 26.

items.label: Born in La Roche-sur-Yon, France
items.detail: Ciryl Gane was born in La Roche-sur-Yon in the Vendée region of France. He later built his fighting career in the Paris area.

items.label: Muay Thai foundation · two French championships
items.detail: Before moving into MMA, Gane competed in Muay Thai and became a two-time French champion. He previously worked selling luxury furniture. His UFC biography does not give exact dates for the two national titles.

items.label: Transitions to MMA with Fernand Lopez
items.detail: Gane moved into full-time MMA at the MMA Factory in Paris under Fernand Lopez. Looking for a gym closer to home, he tried training there; Lopez encouraged him to pursue MMA after his first sessions.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · the story of France’s MMA Factory

items.label: WIN · Bobby Sullivan · MMA debut and TKO title
items.detail: Won his professional MMA debut by first-round submission at 1:42 at TKO Fight Night 1 in Montreal, claiming the vacant TKO heavyweight championship. Tapology lists the finish as a front choke. Professional MMA record: 1–0.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · TKO Fight Night 1 bout record

items.label: WIN · Adam Dyczka · first TKO title defense
items.detail: Defended the TKO heavyweight belt at TKO 44 in Québec City, stopping the previously unbeaten Adam Dyczka with punches at 4:57 of round two. Professional MMA record: 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Roggers Souza · second TKO title defense
items.detail: Stopped Roggers Souza with strikes at 4:26 of round one at TKO 48, retaining the heavyweight title. Gane finished all three of his regional MMA bouts before joining the UFC. Professional MMA record: 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Raphael Pessoa · UFC debut
items.detail: Submitted Raphael Pessoa with an arm-triangle choke at 4:12 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Shevchenko vs. Carmouche 2 in Montevideo, Uruguay. Professional MMA record: 4–0; UFC record: 1–0.

items.label: WIN · Don’Tale Mayes · heel-hook finish
items.detail: Submitted Don’Tale Mayes with a heel hook at 4:46 of round three at UFC Fight Night: Maia vs. Askren in Singapore. It was Gane’s second consecutive UFC submission win. Professional MMA record: 5–0; UFC record: 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Tanner Boser · first decision victory
items.detail: Defeated Tanner Boser by unanimous decision after three rounds at UFC Fight Night: Edgar vs. The Korean Zombie in Busan, South Korea. Closed his debut UFC year with three wins. Professional MMA record: 6–0; UFC record: 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Junior dos Santos · stops a former champion
items.detail: Stopped former UFC heavyweight champion Junior dos Santos at 2:34 of round two at UFC 256. UFCStats records the finish as a KO/TKO by elbow. Professional MMA record: 7–0; UFC record: 4–0.

items.label: WIN · Jairzinho Rozenstruik · first UFC main event
items.detail: Won a five-round unanimous decision over Jairzinho Rozenstruik in his first UFC main event at UFC Fight Night: Rozenstruik vs. Gane. Professional MMA record: 8–0; UFC record: 5–0.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Volkov · five-round decision
items.detail: Defeated Alexander Volkov by unanimous decision over five rounds at UFC Fight Night: Gane vs. Volkov. This was their first meeting. Professional MMA record: 9–0; UFC record: 6–0.

items.label: WIN · Derrick Lewis · first interim UFC title
items.detail: Stopped Derrick Lewis with strikes at 4:11 of round three at UFC 265 in Houston to win the interim UFC heavyweight championship. Gane became the first French fighter to win UFC gold. Professional MMA record: 10–0; UFC record: 7–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · first interim championship and career rise

items.label: LOSS · Francis Ngannou · title unification
items.detail: Lost a five-round unanimous decision to reigning heavyweight champion Francis Ngannou in the UFC 270 title-unification main event in Anaheim. It was Gane’s first professional MMA defeat. Professional MMA record: 10–1; UFC record: 7–1.

items.label: WIN · Tai Tuivasa · headlines the first UFC Paris
items.detail: Stopped Tai Tuivasa with punches at 4:23 of round three in the main event of the UFC’s first event in Paris. Returned to winning form after the Ngannou loss. Professional MMA record: 11–1; UFC record: 8–1.

items.label: LOSS · Jon Jones · vacant heavyweight title
items.detail: Submitted to a guillotine choke from Jon Jones at 2:04 of round one in the UFC 285 main event in Las Vegas. The vacant undisputed UFC heavyweight championship was at stake. Professional MMA record: 11–2; UFC record: 8–2.

items.label: WIN · Serghei Spivac · Paris rebound
items.detail: Stopped Serghei Spivac with punches at 3:44 of round two in the UFC Fight Night main event in Paris. Professional MMA record: 12–2; UFC record: 9–2.

items.label: WIN · Alexander Volkov · split-decision rematch
items.detail: Defeated Alexander Volkov by split decision after three rounds at UFC 310 in Las Vegas. Gane’s second victory over Volkov brought his UFC win total to ten. Professional MMA record: 13–2; UFC record: 10–2.

items.label: NO CONTEST · Tom Aspinall · title fight halted
items.detail: The UFC 321 heavyweight title fight in Abu Dhabi ended at 4:35 of round one after an accidental eye poke left Tom Aspinall unable to continue. The result was a no contest, and Aspinall retained the title. Gane’s record remained 13–2 with one no contest; UFC record: 10–2 with one no contest.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · UFC 321 official event and results

items.label: WIN · Alex Pereira · regains interim UFC title
items.detail: Stopped Alex Pereira with punches at 1:27 of round two at UFC Freedom 250 at the White House in Washington, D.C. Won the interim UFC heavyweight championship for a second time. Professional MMA record: 14–2 with one no contest; UFC record: 11–2 with one no contest.

items.label: Elevated to undisputed UFC heavyweight champion
items.detail: Gane became the undisputed UFC heavyweight champion after Tom Aspinall vacated the belt. UFC confirmed his new status and announced Josh Hokit as his first challenger. This was a championship promotion, not an additional fight or win.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Undisputed And Ready To Defend

items.label: UFC 334 · scheduled title defense vs. Josh Hokit
items.detail: Scheduled to defend the undisputed UFC heavyweight championship against Josh Hokit in the UFC 334 main event at Madison Square Garden in New York City. The bout is scheduled for five rounds. No result exists as of October 27, 2026.

items.label: Wins California high school wrestling championship
items.detail: Representing Clovis High School, Hokit won the 182-pound title at the 2016 CIF State Wrestling Championships. He was a three-time state medalist before moving on to Fresno State.

items.label: Competes in football and wrestling at Fresno State
items.detail: Hokit was a two-sport athlete at Fresno State, playing football while also competing on the Bulldogs' reinstated NCAA wrestling team. He spent time at linebacker and running back; the college later credited him with 1,260 rushing yards and 17 rushing touchdowns across his football career.

items.label: Finishes fifth at NCAA Wrestling Championships
items.detail: Wrestling at 197 pounds, Hokit placed fifth at the NCAA Division I Championships and became Fresno State's first wrestling All-American since 2003. He finished that season with 27 wins, including a 6-2 run at the national tournament, and faced eventual champion Bo Nickal during the event.

items.label: Named NWCA Second-Team All-American at heavyweight
items.detail: After moving up to heavyweight, Hokit went 24-4 in his senior college season and finished third at the Big 12 Championships. With the NCAA tournament canceled during the pandemic, the NWCA selected him as a 2020 second-team All-American.

items.label: NFL stint · San Francisco 49ers and Arizona Cardinals
items.detail: After college, Hokit joined the San Francisco 49ers as an undrafted free agent and spent time on their practice squad during the 2020 and 2021 seasons. He later had a short stint with the Arizona Cardinals in August 2022. These were practice-squad/offseason opportunities, not regular-season NFL appearances.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Josh Hokit, One of One

items.label: Turns his attention to mixed martial arts
items.detail: After his professional football opportunities ended in 2022, Hokit began pursuing MMA full time. His college wrestling background became his foundation, but he entered the sport with little professional fight experience and had to develop his striking and submissions.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Josh Hokit, One of One

items.label: WIN · Spencer Smith · Bellator 300 pro debut
items.detail: Made his professional MMA debut at Bellator 300 and submitted Spencer Smith with an arm-triangle choke at 3:48 of round three. It was his first recorded professional fight. Professional MMA record: 1-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Sean Rose · Bellator Champions Series
items.detail: Submitted Sean Rose with an armbar at 4:58 of round one at Bellator Champions Series in San Diego. Both of Hokit's first two pro MMA wins came by submission. Professional MMA record: 2-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · John Lopez · LFA 199
items.detail: Stopped John Lopez with punches from back mount at 2:53 of round one at LFA 199. This was his first professional MMA victory by TKO. Professional MMA record: 3-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Ezekiel Latu · LFA 203
items.detail: Submitted Ezekiel Latu with a rear-naked choke just 42 seconds into round one at LFA 203. He had now earned three submission wins in four professional bouts. Professional MMA record: 4-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Eric Lunsford · LFA 208
items.detail: Stopped Eric Lunsford with punches from the crucifix position at 2:00 of round one at LFA 208. Hokit completed a three-fight run in LFA with three first-round finishes. Professional MMA record: 5-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Guilherme Uriel · Contender Series contract
items.detail: Stopped Guilherme Uriel with elbows at 1:06 of round two on Dana White's Contender Series, Season 9, Week 2. The victory earned Hokit a UFC contract. Professional MMA record: 6-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · DWCS result and UFC contract

items.label: WIN · Max Gimenis · UFC debut
items.detail: Stopped Max Gimenis with a right hook and follow-up strikes at 0:56 of round one at UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brown. Hokit received a Performance of the Night bonus in his UFC debut. Professional MMA record: 7-0; UFC record: 1-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Denzel Freeman · UFC 324
items.detail: Freeman retired after the opening round, recorded as a TKO at 4:59 of round one at UFC 324. Hokit earned another Performance of the Night bonus. Professional MMA record: 8-0; UFC record: 2-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: WIN · Curtis Blaydes · UFC 327
items.detail: Defeated Curtis Blaydes by unanimous decision after three rounds at UFC 327. It was his first professional MMA fight to reach the scorecards and his first win over a long-established UFC heavyweight contender. The bout earned Fight of the Night honors, and Hokit also received a Performance of the Night bonus. Professional MMA record: 9-0; UFC record: 3-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · result; UFC · post-fight bonuses

items.label: WIN · Derrick Lewis · UFC Freedom 250
items.detail: Stopped Derrick Lewis with punches at 4:09 of round two at UFC Freedom 250 in Washington, D.C. The victory moved him to four straight UFC wins, three of them by stoppage, and set up his first heavyweight title opportunity. Professional MMA record: 10-0; UFC record: 4-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Josh Hokit fight history

items.label: UFC announces heavyweight title fight with Ciryl Gane
items.detail: During the UFC 331 broadcast, the promotion announced Hokit as the challenger to undisputed heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane at UFC 334. Hokit entered the booking undefeated at 10-0 and ranked No. 4 in the UFC heavyweight division. The matchup was announced for Madison Square Garden on November 14.

items.label: UFC 334 · first UFC title fight vs. Ciryl Gane
items.detail: Scheduled to challenge Ciryl Gane for the undisputed UFC heavyweight title in the five-round main event at Madison Square Garden, New York City. As of October 27, 2026, the bout has not taken place and no result should be recorded.

Kayla Harrison.name: Kayla Harrison
Kayla Harrison.subtitle: Career chronology · Olympic judo, PFL and UFC · 20 MMA bouts

items.label: Born in Middletown, Ohio
items.detail: Born July 2, 1990, in Middletown, Ohio. Her mother, who had taken judo in college, later introduced her to the sport when she was six. Harrison would represent the United States in the women's 78 kg judo division at London 2012 and Rio 2016.

items.label: Begins judo at age six
items.detail: Her mother enrolled her in judo at age six after seeing how energetic she was. Harrison has said she did not win a match for her first three years, but by her early teens she was training daily and pursuing national-level competition.

items.label: Wins Junior World Judo Championship
items.detail: Won the World Junior Championships in the women's 78 kg division, becoming only the third American judoka to win a junior world title. That season also brought the U.S. senior national championship and an Olympic trials win, though she did not represent the U.S. in Beijing.

items.label: Wins senior World Judo Championship in Tokyo
items.detail: Won her first senior world judo championship in Tokyo at 78 kg, defeating Brazil's Mayra Aguiar in the final. It was her second senior world championship appearance and made her the fourth American to win a senior world judo gold medal.

items.label: World Championship bronze · Paris
items.detail: Earned the bronze medal in the 78 kg division at the World Judo Championships in Paris. This was her second senior world medal after the 2010 gold; the Pan American Championships and Pan American Games were separate tournaments that year.

items.label: Olympic gold · first American to win judo gold
items.detail: Defeated Great Britain's Gemma Gibbons in the women's 78 kg final at the London Olympics. It was the first Olympic judo gold medal won by an American, male or female. She entered the history books at age 22.

items.label: Establishes the Fearless Foundation
items.detail: Founded the Fearless Foundation, an organization focused on supporting survivors of child sexual abuse through education, prevention, wellness and sport. It became a significant part of Harrison's work outside competition.

items.label: Wins another World Judo Championship bronze
items.detail: Took bronze at the 2014 World Judo Championships in Chelyabinsk, Russia, following her 2010 world gold and 2011 world bronze. This medal came after a major 2013 knee injury and rehabilitation; it demonstrated a competitive return at 78 kg.

items.label: Wins Pan American Games judo gold in Toronto
items.detail: Won gold in women's 78 kg judo at the 2015 Pan American Games in Toronto, four years after also winning Pan American Games gold in Guadalajara. She continued competing internationally in the buildup to Rio.

items.label: Defends Olympic judo title in Rio de Janeiro
items.detail: Won her second Olympic women's 78 kg gold, defeating France's Audrey Tcheuméo in the final by armbar submission. Harrison won all four matches at Rio by ippon, becoming the first American judoka to defend an Olympic title. Her two golds remain a central part of her sporting record.
items.sourceLabel: Olympedia · 2016 Olympic 78 kg bracket and final

items.label: Transitions from elite judo to MMA training
items.detail: After Rio, Harrison began formally preparing for professional MMA. She had already done some boxing and jiu-jitsu training while competing in judo, but now needed an integrated striking game, cage work and ground-and-pound to accompany her elite throws and top control. She initially joined World Series of Fighting in a non-fighting role before making her MMA debut with PFL in 2018.
items.sourceLabel: NBC Sports · transition and early training history

items.label: Publishes Fighting Back
items.detail: Published Fighting Back with Cynthia S. Kaplan and Blaise Aguirre. The book discusses Harrison's experience of abuse by a former coach and offers guidance for recognizing grooming and helping children recover, rather than serving as a conventional athletic autobiography.
items.sourceLabel: Guilford Press · book details and publication date

items.label: WIN · Brittney Elkin · PFL 2018 #2
items.detail: Defeated Brittney Elkin by armbar submission in round 1 at 3:18 at PFL 2018 #2. This was her professional MMA debut, a first-round submission that immediately showcased her ability to convert judo control into MMA finishing positions. Professional MMA record: 1-0. Her first MMA bout after a two-Olympic career in judo. Harrison closed distance, brought the fight to the ground and finished with an armbar. She was competing at 155 pounds, before PFL introduced a women's lightweight tournament in 2019.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Jozette Cotton · PFL 2018 #6
items.detail: Defeated Jozette Cotton by TKO (ground-and-pound) in round 3 at 1:24 at PFL 2018 #6. Her first professional stoppage by strikes came against Cotton, a more experienced opponent. Professional MMA record: 2-0. The third-round TKO showed her using top position and ground strikes rather than relying exclusively on submission holds. Her professional record moved to 2-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Moriel Charneski · PFL 2018 #11
items.detail: Defeated Moriel Charneski by TKO (ground-and-pound) in round 1 at 3:39 at PFL 2018 #11. Finished her debut professional year with three wins and three finishes. Professional MMA record: 3-0. A first-round ground-and-pound stoppage on the PFL 2018 championship card. Despite the event name, this was not a women's tournament title fight; PFL launched that women's 155-pound season in 2019.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Larissa Pacheco · PFL 2019 #1
items.detail: Defeated Larissa Pacheco by unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00 at PFL 2019 #1. Their first meeting went the full three rounds, a different test from Harrison's three finishes in 2018. Professional MMA record: 4-0. FIRST MEETING: A unanimous decision over Pacheco during the 2019 regular season, her first recorded professional MMA bout to reach the judges. Pacheco became a central opponent in her PFL story.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Morgan Frier · PFL 2019 #4
items.detail: Defeated Morgan Frier by keylock (americana) submission in round 1 at 3:35 at PFL 2019 #4. A first-round submission during the PFL regular season. Professional MMA record: 5-0. A first-round keylock submission in the 2019 regular season that put Harrison on track for a playoff berth. She continued building wins at lightweight rather than making the immediate jump to the UFC.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Bobbi-Jo Dalziel · PFL 2019 #7
items.detail: Defeated Bobbi-Jo Dalziel by armbar submission in round 1 at 3:32 at PFL 2019 #7. Advanced through the women's lightweight playoffs and into the championship final. Professional MMA record: 6-0. An armbar in the first round of the 2019 playoffs sent Harrison into the division's inaugural season final. This was a tournament semifinal, not the championship victory itself.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Larissa Pacheco · PFL 2019 #10
items.detail: Defeated Larissa Pacheco by unanimous decision in round 5 at 5:00 at PFL 2019 #10. Won the 2019 PFL women's lightweight championship and its $1 million season prize by defeating Pacheco for the second time, this time over five rounds. Professional MMA record: 7-0. SECOND MEETING: This five-round unanimous decision secured the inaugural 2019 PFL women's lightweight championship and $1 million title prize. Harrison was now 2-0 against Pacheco.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: PFL season canceled during COVID-19 pandemic
items.detail: The PFL canceled its entire 2020 season during the COVID-19 pandemic, interrupting Harrison's planned tournament schedule. Rather than remain idle all year, she booked an Invicta FC featherweight bout with Courtney King, giving her an opportunity to test 145 pounds.

items.label: WIN · Courtney King · Invicta FC 43
items.detail: Defeated Courtney King by TKO (punches) in round 2 at 4:48 at Invicta FC 43. Made her Invicta FC debut at featherweight (145 lb), a lighter weight than her PFL women's lightweight bouts. The contest became the Invicta 43 main event. Professional MMA record: 8-0. With the PFL's 2020 season canceled, Harrison took a one-off Invicta FC fight at 145 pounds against King. It was her first MMA bout below lightweight and the first time she fought outside PFL.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Mariana Morais · PFL 2021 #3
items.detail: Defeated Mariana Morais by TKO (ground-and-pound) in round 1 at 1:23 at PFL 2021 #3. Returned to PFL competition after the canceled 2020 season and opened the 2021 campaign with a fast finish. Professional MMA record: 9-0. Harrison returned to the PFL league format in 2021, finishing Morais with strikes from top position early in the opening round. It was her first fight back in the league after the canceled 2020 season.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Cindy Dandois · PFL 2021 #6
items.detail: Defeated Cindy Dandois by armbar submission in round 1 at 4:44 at PFL 2021 #6. Extended her unbeaten start to ten professional fights. Professional MMA record: 10-0. Finished the more experienced Dandois by first-round armbar in the 2021 regular season, reaching ten straight professional victories.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Genah Fabian · PFL 2021 #8
items.detail: Defeated Genah Fabian by TKO (ground-and-pound) in round 1 at 4:01 at PFL 2021 #8. Won a playoff semifinal with a first-round finish to reach another season final. Professional MMA record: 11-0. Stopped Fabian from top position in round one during the 2021 playoffs. The semifinal victory put her into her second PFL women's lightweight championship final.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Taylor Guardado · PFL 2021 #10
items.detail: Defeated Taylor Guardado by armbar submission in round 2 at 4:00 at PFL 2021 #10. Won a second PFL women's lightweight season championship and another $1 million prize. Professional MMA record: 12-0. Won the 2021 PFL women's lightweight championship with a second-round armbar and claimed a second $1 million season prize.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Marina Mokhnatkina · PFL 2022 #3
items.detail: Defeated Marina Mokhnatkina by unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00 at PFL 2022 #3. Opened the 2022 PFL season with a three-round decision against the decorated sambo fighter. Professional MMA record: 13-0. A three-round unanimous decision over a decorated sambo practitioner. Mokhnatkina defended and attacked through grappling exchanges, but Harrison controlled enough of the fight to win all three judges' cards 30-27. This was the start of her 2022 PFL season.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Kaitlin Young · PFL 2022 #6
items.detail: Defeated Kaitlin Young by TKO (punches from the back) in round 1 at 2:35 at PFL 2022 #6. Secured another regular-season win with strikes from a dominant position. Professional MMA record: 14-0. Stopped Young with punches from back control in the first round. It was her first stoppage in the 2022 regular season after going the distance with Mokhnatkina.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Martina Jindrová · PFL 2022 #9
items.detail: Defeated Martina Jindrová by arm-triangle choke submission in round 1 at 3:17 at PFL 2022 #9. Earned her place in the 2022 women's lightweight championship final. Professional MMA record: 15-0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: LOSS · Larissa Pacheco · PFL 2022 #10
items.detail: Lost to Larissa Pacheco by unanimous decision in round 5 at 5:00 at PFL 2022 #10. Suffered the first defeat of her professional MMA career in the 2022 PFL women's lightweight championship final. Pacheco won their third meeting after losing the first two in 2019. Professional MMA record: 15-1. THIRD MEETING: Pacheco reversed the series trend after two 2019 defeats, damaging Harrison on the feet and continuing to attack when taken down. All three judges scored it 48-47; Harrison lost the 2022 championship and her 15-fight unbeaten streak ended. This was a genuine loss, not a title defense retained.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · third fight; 2022 championship loss

items.label: WIN · Aspen Ladd · PFL 2023 #10
items.detail: Defeated Aspen Ladd by unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00 at PFL 2023 #10. Returned after nearly a year away and defeated former UFC contender Aspen Ladd on the PFL championship card in a non-tournament bout. Professional MMA record: 16-1. After a year away following the Pacheco defeat, Harrison returned in a non-tournament bout against a former UFC bantamweight contender. She won all three rounds on the scorecards, and this proved to be her final fight under the PFL banner.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: UFC signing announced; Holly Holm booked for UFC 300
items.detail: UFC announced Harrison's signing after her 16-1 MMA run, setting a UFC 300 debut against former bantamweight champion Holly Holm. UFC had no women's 155-pound division; she committed to competing at 135 pounds, 20 pounds below her usual PFL fight limit. Her new weight class became a major test alongside the level of UFC opposition.

items.label: WIN · Holly Holm · UFC 300
items.detail: Defeated Holly Holm by rear-naked choke submission in round 2 at 1:47 at UFC 300. Made her UFC and bantamweight debuts on the UFC 300 main card in Las Vegas. UFC record: 1-0. Professional MMA record: 17-1. Made her UFC debut at bantamweight, having previously competed at 155 pounds in PFL and once at 145 in Invicta. In the second round, she took Holm down, established back control and finished with a rear-naked choke. It answered the immediate question of whether she could compete effectively at 135.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Ketlen Vieira · UFC 307
items.detail: Defeated Ketlen Vieira by unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00 at UFC 307. Beat an established contender across three rounds to strengthen her case for a women's bantamweight title shot. UFC record: 2-0. Professional MMA record: 18-1. Won 30-27, 30-27 and 29-28 against a well-established UFC bantamweight contender. Vieira's defensive grappling and striking made the second round difficult, opening Harrison up with strikes, before Harrison controlled the final round from top position. This was a more competitive test than her UFC debut.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional bout record

items.label: WIN · Julianna Peña · UFC 316
items.detail: Defeated Julianna Peña by kimura submission in round 2 at 4:55 at UFC 316. Won the undisputed UFC women's bantamweight championship in Newark, New Jersey. Peña was deducted a point for illegal upkicks in the first round; Harrison earned a Performance of the Night bonus. UFC record: 3-0. Professional MMA record: 19-1. Captured the UFC women's bantamweight championship. Peña was penalized a point for illegal upkicks from guard in round one. Harrison took her down again in round two, threatened an arm triangle near the cage, then switched to a kimura for the finish at 4:55. It made Harrison an Olympic gold medalist and UFC champion.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · result; UFC · championship recap

items.label: Amanda Nunes returns for post-fight faceoff
items.detail: Former two-division UFC champion Amanda Nunes entered the cage after Harrison's title win, congratulated her and agreed to a future meeting. The two had previously trained at American Top Team, though Nunes had since left the team, adding a longstanding professional connection to the proposed fight.

items.label: Neck surgery postpones planned UFC 324 defense
items.detail: Harrison underwent cervical spine surgery in January at Hospital for Special Surgery in New York because of severe nerve pain, weakness and herniated discs. Her surgeon performed spinal fusion after deciding disc replacement was not the safest option. She withdrew from a scheduled January 24 title defense against Amanda Nunes; the bout was postponed, not a loss or no contest.
items.sourceLabel: Hospital for Special Surgery · Harrison's own recovery account

items.label: Harrison–Nunes rebooked for UFC 334
items.detail: The UFC confirmed Harrison's first women's bantamweight title defense against Amanda Nunes for November 14 at Madison Square Garden, as the UFC 334 co-main event beneath Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit. The bout had originally been scheduled for UFC 324 before Harrison's neck surgery.

items.label: Discusses recovery and readiness after neck fusion
items.detail: In interviews and her hospital recovery account, Harrison said the surgery was followed by an extended period in a neck brace, limits on lifting and difficult rehabilitation. She reported that her nerve pain had improved and that she had resumed training. Treat these as her reported recovery status, not a guarantee about performance against Nunes.
items.sourceLabel: Hospital for Special Surgery · October 2026 recovery account

items.label: UFC 334 · first title defense vs. Amanda Nunes
items.detail: Scheduled to defend the UFC women's bantamweight championship against returning former two-division champion Amanda Nunes in the UFC 334 co-main event at Madison Square Garden in New York. This is a scheduled contest, not a completed fight; no result exists as of October 27, 2026.

items.label: Discloses abuse by former coach; relocates to Massachusetts
items.detail: As a teenager, Harrison disclosed years of sexual abuse by a former judo coach. Afterward she left Ohio for Massachusetts, training under Olympic medalist Jimmy Pedro and his father Jim Pedro Sr. Their gym offered both a safer environment and a route back into elite competition. The episode is included because Harrison has spoken publicly about it as a turning point in her life and sport.
items.sourceLabel: United States Judo Federation · biographical profile

items.label: Wins U.S. Olympic judo trials but misses Beijing selection
items.detail: Won the U.S. 78 kg Olympic team trials, but the United States had not qualified an Olympic berth in her weight class, so the trials win did not send her to Beijing. She instead traveled to China as training partner to Ronda Rousey, who took bronze at 70 kg. Harrison's first Olympic appearance was London 2012.
items.sourceLabel: Boston Globe · 2008 Olympic qualification and Rousey

items.label: Silver · World Junior Judo Championships
items.detail: Followed her 2008 junior world gold with silver at the 2009 junior worlds, while gaining experience on the senior international circuit. This is a separate medal and year, not a second junior world title.

items.label: Gold · Pan American Judo Championships
items.detail: Won the continental judo championship in Guadalajara at 78 kg. The continental championships should not be confused with the quadrennial Pan American Games, which took place later in 2011 and where Harrison also won gold.

items.label: Gold · Pan American Games in Guadalajara
items.detail: Won the women's 78 kg title at the 2011 Pan American Games, adding a major multi-sport competition gold to her world championship medals ahead of London 2012. This was distinct from her April continental championship win.
items.sourceLabel: Olympedia · Harrison's Pan American Games results

items.label: Builds London Olympic campaign through IJF circuit
items.detail: Won Grand Prix Düsseldorf, the Budapest World Cup and the Rio de Janeiro Grand Slam in the buildup to the London Olympics; she also took silver at the Paris Grand Slam. These results established her as a leading contender at 78 kg before she won Olympic gold.

items.label: Undergoes reconstructive knee surgery
items.detail: After her London Olympic title, chronic knee problems worsened. Harrison underwent major reconstructive surgery in June 2013, involving realignment of the kneecap, and faced a long rehabilitation. She returned to the international circuit the following year and ultimately defended her Olympic title in 2016.
items.sourceLabel: NBC Sports · knee operation and recovery

items.label: Gold · Tokyo Grand Slam comeback
items.detail: Won the Tokyo Grand Slam at 78 kg after returning from her 2013 knee surgery. Along with her 2014 world bronze, the result showed she was again competing at the top level of international judo.

items.label: Gold · IJF World Masters in Morocco
items.detail: Won the World Masters title at 78 kg in Morocco during a season that also brought multiple Grand Prix victories. The Masters title is not an Olympic or world championship, but it is a major event in the IJF calendar.

items.label: Finishes year atop IJF prestige rankings
items.detail: Team USA lists Harrison first in the 2015 IJF prestige ranking. Her international season included Pan American Games gold, World Masters gold and Tokyo Grand Slam gold, strengthening her position for a second Olympic run.

items.label: Gold · Tokyo Grand Slam
items.detail: Won the Tokyo Grand Slam again, following her 2014 victory there. This was one of the last major gold medals of her pre-Rio Olympic campaign and is recorded separately from her 2015 Pan American Games title.

items.label: Gold · Pan American Judo Championships in Havana
items.detail: Added a continental championship gold in Havana, a significant late-cycle result before Rio. She then won the 2016 World Masters and Budapest Grand Prix as part of her final Olympic preparations.

items.label: Gold · World Masters, final Olympic preparations
items.detail: Won another World Masters title at 78 kg. Harrison also earned gold at the Budapest Grand Prix in June, entering Rio having reestablished her form after the earlier knee surgery.

items.label: Develops MMA game at American Top Team
items.detail: Joined the American Top Team system in Florida as she pursued pro MMA, working with a staff including Mike Brown and strength coach Jeremy Fedoruk. Her wrestling-style clinch entries, mat control and submissions came from judo; the key new work was MMA-specific striking, wall work and ground-and-pound.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · ATT training and strength-coach history

items.label: PFL launches women's 155-pound championship season
items.detail: PFL formally introduced its women's lightweight tournament with regular-season standings, playoffs and a $1 million title prize. Harrison had fought three PFL bouts in 2018 but competed in this new division's inaugural championship season in 2019.

items.label: Re-signs with PFL after MMA free agency
items.detail: After two PFL championship seasons, Harrison entered free agency and attracted interest from competing promotions. She instead signed a new multi-year PFL agreement that brought her back for the 2022 league season and promoted her as a central part of its planned superfight offering.

items.label: Former teammate Amanda Nunes leaves American Top Team
items.detail: Nunes left American Top Team after her December 2021 defeat to Julianna Peña. Nunes later said Harrison's emergence as a potential future opponent was part of the situation; Harrison said she had no ill will toward her former teammate. Accounts differ on how important that factor was to Nunes's departure.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Mania · Harrison responds to former teammate

items.label: Tests cut to 135 pounds before UFC debut
items.detail: Ahead of UFC 300, Harrison completed a controlled test weight cut, rehydration and fight simulation with her team. She officially weighed 136 pounds for her non-title UFC debut against Holm, using the one-pound allowance. Future championship bouts required making 135.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · 2024 weight-cut preparations and weigh-in

items.label: First Harrison–Nunes booking confirmed for UFC 324
items.detail: UFC officially scheduled Harrison's first bantamweight title defense against Amanda Nunes for January 24, 2026, at UFC 324 in Las Vegas. The announcement took place months after their UFC 316 faceoff; the original booking was eventually postponed because of Harrison's January neck surgery.

items.label: UFC says it will wait to rebook Nunes title fight
items.detail: With Harrison recovering from surgery, UFC leadership said Nunes would not be assigned a replacement opponent and the intention was to preserve their title matchup once Harrison could return. The January fight cancellation did not change Harrison's 19-1 record.

items.label: Resumes full camp for Nunes fight
items.detail: American Top Team coach Anderson Franca reported in September that Harrison had returned to full training several weeks earlier following neck surgery. The team began preparing specifically for Amanda Nunes rather than scheduling a tune-up contest.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · ATT coach discusses training return

items.label: Qualifies for Olympic trials; chooses not to compete
items.detail: Harrison says she accumulated enough ranking points to qualify for the 2004 U.S. Olympic judo trials while still a young teenager. She opted not to compete because making the lighter weight class had become difficult during adolescence, later moving up in weight. Qualifying for trials was not qualifying for the Olympic team.

items.label: Trains with Ronda Rousey at Pedro's Judo Center
items.detail: At Jimmy Pedro's gym near Boston, Harrison trained and lived alongside Ronda Rousey, the future UFC champion. Their rivalry and regular sparring helped develop Harrison's competitiveness, and she traveled to Beijing as Rousey's training partner for the 2008 Olympics. This was part of Harrison's judo career, years before either woman's eventual UFC overlap.
items.sourceLabel: WHDH · 2016 interview about Pedro's gym and Rousey

items.label: Joins World Series of Fighting as analyst and ambassador
items.detail: After her second Olympic gold, Harrison signed with World Series of Fighting, the organization that later became PFL. She was initially announced as a commentator and brand ambassador with a possible future in the cage; there was no confirmed fight date. This was her first formal link to the organization in which she later made her MMA debut.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · first WSOF contract announcement

items.label: Commits to making a professional MMA debut
items.detail: Harrison publicly confirmed her intention to enter MMA competition after initially taking a broadcasting and ambassador role with WSOF. The promotion had been renamed the Professional Fighters League, and her team planned a debut once her MMA training had progressed. Her eventual first pro fight came in June 2018.
items.sourceLabel: NBC Sports · 2017 decision to enter MMA

Amanda Nunes.name: Amanda Nunes
Amanda Nunes.subtitle: Career chronology · 28 professional MMA bouts · two UFC divisions

items.label: Born in Pojuca, Bahia, Brazil
items.detail: Amanda Lourenço Nunes was born in Pojuca, a small town near Salvador in Brazil's Bahia state. She grew up with two older sisters in a family where boxing and vale tudo already had a presence: her mother trained boxing and her uncle had competed in vale tudo.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · early-life reporting and family interviews

items.label: Begins capoeira, karate and boxing
items.detail: Her mother encouraged combat sports as an outlet for a very active child. Nunes describes beginning karate at seven, while other accounts discuss earlier capoeira training; the exact order and dates of those childhood lessons are not consistently documented. She later added boxing.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete biography and training Q&A

items.label: Moves to Salvador; begins Brazilian jiu-jitsu
items.detail: At around sixteen she followed her sister Vanessa into jiu-jitsu and moved from Pojuca to Salvador. She trained under Edson Carvalho, adding ground-fighting skill to her earlier striking background.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Roar of the Lioness

items.label: Lives inside gym; receives Lioness nickname
