items.detail: To stay close to training, Nunes lived for a period at Edson Carvalho's academy, waking early to help clean mats before practice. As the only woman in a gym whose emblem featured two lions, she began to be called 'Leoa'—Lioness. The nickname followed her into MMA.

items.label: Gold · Pan-American Brazilian jiu-jitsu championship
items.detail: Won a Pan-American jiu-jitsu championship gold while advancing through the colored-belt ranks. Her success in grappling preceded—and overlapped with—her first professional MMA appearances; this was a jiu-jitsu medal, not an MMA championship.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame career biography

items.label: LOSS · Ana Maria · Prime MMA Championship 2
items.detail: Lost to Ana Maria by armbar submission at Prime MMA Championship 2 (Mar. 8, 2008; round 1, 0:35). Made her professional MMA debut in Brazil and tapped to an armbar 35 seconds into round one. She began her career with a loss rather than an undefeated run. Professional MMA record after the fight: 0-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Paty Barbosa · Demo Fight 3
items.detail: Defeated Paty Barbosa by TKO (corner stoppage) at Demo Fight 3 (May 24, 2008; round 1, 0:11). Returned less than three months after her debut loss and finished the fight in 11 seconds. Professional MMA record after the fight: 1-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Nadja · Prime MMA Championship 3
items.detail: Defeated Nadja by TKO (punches) at Prime MMA Championship 3 (Jul. 1, 2008; round 1, 0:10). Won another quick first-round stoppage, this time in ten seconds. Early opponent records are not uniformly complete. Professional MMA record after the fight: 2-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Gold · World Jiu-Jitsu Championship
items.detail: Captured a world Brazilian jiu-jitsu championship gold in the purple-belt ranks, alongside a developing MMA record. Her later professional career drew on her submission skills even though many of her early MMA victories came by strikes.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame career biography

items.label: WIN · Deise Rocha · Samurai Fight Combat
items.detail: Defeated Deise Rocha by TKO (punches) at Samurai Fight Combat (Sep. 12, 2009; round 1, 1:08). Finished another regional bout by punches in the opening round. Professional MMA record after the fight: 3-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Vanessa Porto · Samurai Fight Combat 2
items.detail: Defeated Vanessa Porto by TKO (corner stoppage) at Samurai Fight Combat 2 (Dec. 12, 2009; round 2, 5:00). Beat a more experienced Brazilian opponent; Porto went on to become a notable flyweight and Invicta champion. It was Nunes's first recorded professional bout to reach the end of round two. Professional MMA record after the fight: 4-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Ediane Gomes · Bitetti Combat 6
items.detail: Defeated Ediane Gomes by TKO (punches) at Bitetti Combat 6 (Feb. 25, 2010; round 2, 3:00). Stopped previously unbeaten Gomes in round two, closing her regional Brazilian run at five wins and one loss. Professional MMA record after the fight: 5-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Leaves Brazil to pursue MMA in the United States
items.detail: Nunes moved to the United States after her early regional victories. She spent time in New Jersey with Edson Carvalho and then in South Florida, training at MMA Masters as she sought fights in larger North American promotions. Exact relocation dates vary across accounts.

items.label: WIN · Julia Budd · Strikeforce Challengers 13
items.detail: Defeated Julia Budd by TKO (punches) at Strikeforce Challengers 13 (Jan. 7, 2011; round 1, 0:14). Made her Strikeforce debut at featherweight, stopping Budd in 14 seconds. This brought her early Brazilian finishing style to a major U.S. television promotion. Professional MMA record after the fight: 6-1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Moves from featherweight toward bantamweight
items.detail: Her Strikeforce win over Julia Budd came at featherweight (145 pounds); she then competed against Alexis Davis at bantamweight (135 pounds). The weight-class change was part of her early North American career, before the UFC had a women's bantamweight division.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete biography and Strikeforce history

items.label: LOSS · Alexis Davis · Strikeforce: Barnett vs. Kharitonov
items.detail: Lost to Alexis Davis by TKO (punches) at Strikeforce: Barnett vs. Kharitonov (Sep. 10, 2011; round 2, 4:53). Lost her second Strikeforce bout in the closing seconds of round two after beginning strongly. The setback exposed difficulties sustaining her offense and controlling position against experienced opposition. Professional MMA record after the fight: 6-2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Trains at MMA Masters and meets Nina Ansaroff
items.detail: At MMA Masters in Miami, Nunes began training with fellow fighter Nina Ansaroff. They became training partners and later a couple. Nunes has credited that relationship and a better balance between training and recovery with helping her mature as a professional; the exact date of their first meeting is not consistently reported.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Nunes and Nina interviews

items.label: Wins NAGA grappling world titles
items.detail: Won North American Grappling Association titles in both a lightweight class and the absolute division. This was an additional submission-grappling accomplishment separate from her 2008 Pan-American and 2009 world jiu-jitsu medals.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame career biography

items.label: WIN · Raquel Canuto · Invicta FC 2
items.detail: Defeated Raquel Canuto by technical submission (rear-naked choke) at Invicta FC 2 (Jul. 28, 2012; round 1, 2:24). Made her Invicta FC debut, stopping Canuto—also listed in some historical records as Raquel Pa'aluhi—with a rear-naked choke. The result was classified as a technical submission. Professional MMA record after the fight: 7-2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: LOSS · Sarah D'Alelio · Invicta FC 4
items.detail: Lost to Sarah D'Alelio by unanimous decision at Invicta FC 4 (Jan. 5, 2013; round 3, 5:00). Lost her first professional fight that went to the judges. The defeat occurred before her move to UFC, so it is not part of her UFC record. Professional MMA record after the fight: 7-3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Joins the UFC women's bantamweight division
items.detail: The UFC signed Nunes in 2013 as its women's roster expanded. Her first UFC appearance was set for UFC 163 in Rio de Janeiro, the first women's UFC bout held in Brazil. Jessica Andrade had already become the first Brazilian woman to fight in the UFC on July 27, 2013; Nunes would become the first to win.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · history of Brazilian women in the Octagon

items.label: WIN · Sheila Gaff · UFC 163
items.detail: Defeated Sheila Gaff by TKO (punches and elbows) at UFC 163 (Aug. 3, 2013; round 1, 2:08). Made her UFC debut in Rio, finishing Gaff with elbows and punches from top position. Became the first Brazilian woman to win a UFC fight. UFC record: 1-0. Professional MMA record after the fight: 8-3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Germaine de Randamie · UFC Fight Night 31: Fight for the Troops 3
items.detail: Defeated Germaine de Randamie by TKO (elbows) at UFC Fight Night 31: Fight for the Troops 3 (Nov. 6, 2013; round 1, 3:56). Beat a strong striker with takedowns and elbows on the ground, bringing her UFC start to 2-0. They would meet again in a much different five-round title fight in 2019. Professional MMA record after the fight: 9-3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: LOSS · Cat Zingano · UFC 178
items.detail: Lost to Cat Zingano by TKO (elbows and punches) at UFC 178 (Sep. 27, 2014; round 3, 1:21). Started well and landed damaging offense but faded as the fight progressed. Zingano took over in grappling exchanges and stopped her in the third round. Nunes was 2-1 in the UFC. Professional MMA record after the fight: 9-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Moves to American Top Team after the Zingano defeat
items.detail: Following the Cat Zingano loss, Nunes joined American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. She worked with coaches including Conan Silveira and Mike Brown, with an increased focus on pacing, wrestling integration and complete fight preparation. The switch preceded a 12-fight UFC winning streak.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · journey from early setbacks to title contention

items.label: WIN · Shayna Baszler · UFC Fight Night 62
items.detail: Defeated Shayna Baszler by TKO (leg kicks and punches) at UFC Fight Night 62 (Mar. 21, 2015; round 1, 1:56). Returned after the Zingano loss and attacked Baszler's lead leg before forcing the first-round stoppage. UFC record: 3-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 10-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Sara McMann · UFC Fight Night 73
items.detail: Defeated Sara McMann by rear-naked choke submission at UFC Fight Night 73 (Aug. 8, 2015; round 1, 2:53). Defeated Olympic silver-medalist wrestler Sara McMann by hurting her with strikes and transitioning to the rear-naked choke. Won a Performance of the Night award; UFC record: 4-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 11-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Valentina Shevchenko · UFC 196
items.detail: Defeated Valentina Shevchenko by unanimous decision at UFC 196 (Mar. 5, 2016; round 3, 5:00). Their first meeting went all three rounds. Nunes banked early offense and grappling control before Shevchenko finished strongly; all three judges scored it for Nunes. UFC record: 5-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 12-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: UFC 200 elevated to a championship main event
items.detail: After Jon Jones was removed from UFC 200 shortly before fight night, the women's bantamweight title contest between Miesha Tate and Nunes became the event's main event. Nunes entered on three straight UFC victories and faced the reigning champion for her first UFC title shot.

items.label: WIN · Miesha Tate · UFC 200
items.detail: Defeated Miesha Tate by rear-naked choke submission at UFC 200 (Jul. 9, 2016; round 1, 3:16). Hurt the reigning champion with punches, followed her to the ground and finished with a rear-naked choke. Won the UFC women's bantamweight championship in her first title fight; UFC record: 6-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 13-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Becomes UFC women's bantamweight champion
items.detail: The Tate victory brought Nunes her first UFC belt and made her the first Brazilian woman to hold a UFC championship. This championship milestone is separated from the fight result for career context; it was not an additional bout.

items.label: WIN · Ronda Rousey · UFC 207
items.detail: Defeated Ronda Rousey by TKO (punches) at UFC 207 (Dec. 30, 2016; round 1, 0:48). Stopped Rousey in 48 seconds in her first bantamweight title defense. Rousey was returning after a year away following her loss to Holly Holm; Nunes's sustained straight punching ended the fight before Rousey could establish a clinch. UFC record: 7-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 14-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: First bantamweight title defense completed
items.detail: The 48-second Rousey finish was Nunes's first successful defense of the title she won at UFC 200. It also marked Rousey's final professional MMA fight. The result accelerated Nunes's standing as the division's established champion.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Nunes career profile and championship history

items.label: Shevchenko rematch removed from UFC 213
items.detail: Nunes withdrew from her scheduled main event with Valentina Shevchenko on the day of UFC 213, citing illness and sinus symptoms. UFC replaced the main event with Yoel Romero vs. Robert Whittaker. The canceled booking was not recorded as a fight or loss.

items.label: WIN · Valentina Shevchenko · UFC 215
items.detail: Defeated Valentina Shevchenko by split decision at UFC 215 (Sep. 9, 2017; round 5, 5:00). Defended the bantamweight belt in a tactical five-round rematch. Two judges scored it for Nunes and one for Shevchenko; the close result remains contested by some observers. UFC record: 8-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 15-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Second bantamweight title defense; close decision
items.detail: The UFC 215 split-decision win secured Nunes's second successful defense at bantamweight. It was her second victory over Shevchenko, and the first of their two meetings scheduled for five rounds.

items.label: WIN · Raquel Pennington · UFC 224
items.detail: Defeated Raquel Pennington by TKO (elbows and punches) at UFC 224 (May 12, 2018; round 5, 2:36). Headlined a UFC pay-per-view in Rio de Janeiro and stopped Pennington midway through round five after an extended title fight. It was her third successful bantamweight defense. UFC record: 9-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 16-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Pursues a second UFC championship at featherweight
items.detail: Still holding the women's bantamweight title, Nunes accepted a fight against reigning featherweight champion Cris Cyborg. The bout offered her the chance to become the UFC's first female simultaneous two-division champion.

items.label: WIN · Cris Cyborg · UFC 232
items.detail: Defeated Cris Cyborg by KO/TKO (punches) at UFC 232 (Dec. 29, 2018; round 1, 0:51). Exchanged power punches with Cyborg and scored multiple knockdowns before the referee stopped the fight at 51 seconds. Won the UFC women's featherweight championship while retaining her bantamweight belt. UFC record: 10-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 17-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: First woman to hold two UFC championships simultaneously
items.detail: By knocking out Cris Cyborg at UFC 232, Nunes became the first woman in UFC history to hold championship belts in two weight classes simultaneously. Cyborg had not lost since 2005. This was one of the defining outcomes of Nunes's career.

items.label: WIN · Holly Holm · UFC 239
items.detail: Defeated Holly Holm by TKO (head kick and punches) at UFC 239 (Jul. 6, 2019; round 1, 4:10). Returned to bantamweight and stopped the former champion with a head kick and follow-up punches. It was her fourth successful 135-pound title defense and her first fight after capturing the featherweight belt. UFC record: 11-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 18-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Germaine de Randamie · UFC 245
items.detail: Defeated Germaine de Randamie by unanimous decision at UFC 245 (Dec. 14, 2019; round 5, 5:00). Won the five-round rematch with de Randamie by repeatedly using takedowns and ground control. De Randamie had moments on the feet, making this a different tactical contest from Nunes's first-round finish of her in 2013. Fifth successful bantamweight defense; UFC record: 12-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 19-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Completes fifth successful bantamweight defense
items.detail: The decision over Germaine de Randamie brought Nunes to five successful defenses of the 135-pound championship during her first reign. Having retained the bantamweight belt after winning the featherweight title, she next focused on defending the latter.

items.label: WIN · Felicia Spencer · UFC 250
items.detail: Defeated Felicia Spencer by unanimous decision at UFC 250 (Jun. 6, 2020; round 5, 5:00). Made her first defense of the UFC women's featherweight championship in a five-round main event. She controlled the stand-up exchanges and much of the wrestling while Spencer survived to the final bell. UFC record: 13-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 20-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Defends featherweight belt while holding bantamweight title
items.detail: After defending 135 pounds at UFC 245, Nunes successfully defended her 145-pound belt against Felicia Spencer at UFC 250. She had now defended championships in both divisions while holding them simultaneously.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame championship summary

items.label: Nunes and Nina welcome their first child
items.detail: Nunes and her wife, fellow UFC fighter Nina Ansaroff, welcomed daughter Raegan Ann in September 2020. The family milestone came between her UFC 250 featherweight defense and the 2021 fight with Megan Anderson.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · first child's birth announcement

items.label: WIN · Megan Anderson · UFC 259
items.detail: Defeated Megan Anderson by inverted triangle armbar submission at UFC 259 (Mar. 6, 2021; round 1, 2:03). Submitted Anderson in a little over two minutes using a triangle-and-armbar combination after damaging her early. It was Nunes's second successful featherweight title defense, and her twelfth straight UFC victory. UFC record: 14-1. Professional MMA record after the fight: 21-4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Reaches twelve straight UFC wins
items.detail: The win against Megan Anderson extended Nunes's uninterrupted UFC winning streak from March 2015 to March 2021 to twelve fights. That streak included her first bantamweight title victory over Miesha Tate and eight subsequent successful championship bouts at bantamweight and featherweight.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame career records

items.label: LOSS · Julianna Peña · UFC 269
items.detail: Lost to Julianna Peña by rear-naked choke submission at UFC 269 (Dec. 11, 2021; round 2, 3:26). Lost the bantamweight title when Peña pressured through the second round, landed repeated punches and secured the rear-naked choke. The defeat ended Nunes's twelve-fight winning streak. Her featherweight title remained hers; UFC record: 14-2. Professional MMA record after the fight: 21-5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Leaves American Top Team and builds private training base
items.detail: Following the Peña defeat, Nunes departed American Top Team and established her own training setup. She said she had long wanted a private space rather than creating a rival to ATT. The move changed her coaching team and separated her from former training partner Kayla Harrison.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Nunes details departure from ATT

items.label: Names new coaches for Peña rematch
items.detail: Nunes reunited with wrestling coach Kami Barzini and coach Roger Krahl in her independent setup after leaving ATT. She emphasized the value of controlling her own preparation for the bantamweight title rematch.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · interviews about new coaching team

items.label: Coaches The Ultimate Fighter 30 opposite Julianna Peña
items.detail: Nunes and Peña coached opposing teams on The Ultimate Fighter's 30th season, featuring men's heavyweights and women's flyweights. The show premiered May 3, 2022, and their bantamweight title rematch followed in July.

items.label: Explains how Harrison factored into gym decision
items.detail: Nunes later said the possibility of eventually fighting fellow American Top Team athlete Kayla Harrison was one factor in her departure. This added context to her February remarks that she had always planned to create a private facility. It does not establish that she and Harrison had a personal feud.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · 2022 interview about ATT and Harrison

items.label: WIN · Julianna Peña · UFC 277
items.detail: Defeated Julianna Peña by unanimous decision at UFC 277 (Jul. 30, 2022; round 5, 5:00). Used southpaw striking, repeated knockdowns and effective wrestling to dominate the rematch across five rounds. Regained the UFC women's bantamweight title while still holding the 145-pound championship. UFC record: 15-2. Professional MMA record after the fight: 22-5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Regains bantamweight title to restore dual-champion status
items.detail: The Peña rematch returned the 135-pound title to Nunes after a seven-month absence. She again simultaneously held the UFC women's bantamweight and featherweight championships; the victory was not a new featherweight title defense.

items.label: Peña injury changes planned trilogy to Irene Aldana fight
items.detail: The UFC initially planned a third Nunes–Peña championship bout for UFC 289. Peña withdrew because of a rib injury; Irene Aldana replaced her as the bantamweight title challenger. This was a booking change, not an additional Nunes fight.

items.label: WIN · Irene Aldana · UFC 289
items.detail: Defeated Irene Aldana by unanimous decision at UFC 289 (Jun. 10, 2023; round 5, 5:00). Defended the bantamweight championship over five rounds in Vancouver, winning wide scorecards through controlled striking, footwork and timely wrestling. She announced her retirement afterward. UFC record at retirement: 16-2. Professional MMA record after the fight: 23-5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional fight history

items.label: Announces retirement inside the Octagon
items.detail: After beating Aldana at UFC 289, Nunes placed both belts and her gloves on the canvas and announced she was retiring from MMA at 35. Her career record was 23-5, including 16 UFC wins and two UFC defeats; she had held UFC titles in both women's bantamweight and featherweight divisions.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Nunes retirement and Hall of Fame biography

items.label: Vacates bantamweight and featherweight championships
items.detail: Nunes vacated both UFC championships following her retirement. Her second bantamweight reign ended without a defeat; the women's featherweight belt also became vacant rather than changing hands in a fight. It was the end of her active championship tenure, not an additional loss.

items.label: UFC announces 2025 Hall of Fame induction
items.detail: UFC announced that Nunes would enter the Hall of Fame as part of the 2025 class, in the Modern Wing. The organization highlighted her 23-5 professional record, simultaneous UFC championship reigns, and women's UFC records for finishes and title-fight wins.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame induction announcement

items.label: Returns to Octagon for faceoff with Kayla Harrison
items.detail: After Harrison submitted Julianna Peña to become UFC bantamweight champion at UFC 316, Nunes entered the cage for a faceoff. The moment publicly signaled her intention to return from retirement and challenge Harrison. No fight took place that night.

items.label: Confirms Harrison connection to earlier ATT departure
items.detail: In post-UFC 316 remarks, Nunes said the prospect of facing Harrison in the future had contributed to her 2022 decision to leave American Top Team. She described wanting independent space to prepare for a matchup between former teammates.

items.label: Inducted into UFC Hall of Fame, Modern Wing
items.detail: Nunes was inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame at the International Fight Week ceremony in Las Vegas. The induction took place after her retirement announcement and during her preparation for a comeback; it was not a new championship or competition result.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Hall of Fame official profile

items.label: Harrison title bout booked for UFC 324
items.detail: UFC announced that Nunes would challenge reigning bantamweight champion Kayla Harrison on January 24, 2026, at UFC 324. The matchup would have been Nunes's first fight since June 2023.

items.label: Harrison injury postpones UFC 324 comeback
items.detail: Harrison withdrew from their planned January 24 title fight after neck surgery for herniated discs. Nunes did not compete at UFC 324, and no opponent replacement or official fight result was entered for the canceled matchup.

items.label: Nunes affirms commitment to delayed comeback
items.detail: Following the cancellation of UFC 324's co-main event, Nunes publicly indicated she remained committed to fighting Harrison. UFC said it intended to preserve the matchup and reschedule it later in 2026 rather than immediately arrange a substitute opponent.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · reaction to the UFC 324 cancellation

items.label: Nunes–Harrison rebooked for UFC 334 in New York
items.detail: UFC confirmed the title bout for November 14 at Madison Square Garden in New York City, as co-main event under Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit. It will be Nunes's return after more than three years without an official bout.

items.label: Discusses comeback plans and possible future defenses
items.detail: During UFC 334 media appearances, Nunes said the return was not simply a one-fight appearance and that she would intend to defend the bantamweight championship if she beat Harrison. Her comments are statements of intention, not future fight results or guarantees.

items.label: UFC 334 · championship challenge vs. Kayla Harrison
items.detail: Scheduled to challenge Kayla Harrison for the UFC women's bantamweight championship in the UFC 334 co-main event at Madison Square Garden in New York. Nunes enters with a 23-5 professional record and has not fought since UFC 289 on June 10, 2023. No result exists as of October 27, 2026.

Luis Gurule.name: Luis Gurule
Luis Gurule.subtitle: Career chronology · wrestling, regional titles and 15 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in Sheridan, Colorado
items.detail: Luis Abraham Gurule grew up in the south Denver area of Sheridan, Colorado. His hometown appears as Sheridan on his UFC athlete Q&A and his college wrestling rosters; Denver is sometimes listed as his birthplace.

items.label: Third at Colorado state high-school wrestling tournament
items.detail: Representing Sheridan High School, Gurule finished third at the 2011 Colorado 3A wrestling championships at 112 pounds. His next high-school season brought a state title at a slightly heavier weight.
items.sourceLabel: Colorado School of Mines · athlete wrestling biography

items.label: Wins Colorado 3A state wrestling championship
items.detail: Won the Colorado Class 3A high-school state title at 113 pounds as a Sheridan High School senior. College wrestling records independently confirm the achievement and the weight class.
items.sourceLabel: Colorado School of Mines · high-school results

items.label: Colorado freestyle and Greco-Roman state titles
items.detail: Gurule reports winning Colorado state freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling titles during 2012, in addition to his scholastic state championship. These were separate wrestling disciplines, not three titles in the same tournament.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A on amateur wrestling honors

items.label: Finishes fifth at Fargo Nationals in Greco-Roman
items.detail: He also lists a fifth-place finish in Greco-Roman wrestling at the 2012 Fargo national tournament. Fargo draws junior freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestlers from across the country; the result helps explain his background beyond state-level competition.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A on wrestling credentials

items.label: Wrestles at Colorado School of Mines
items.detail: Competed at NCAA Division II Colorado School of Mines, initially wrestling at 125 pounds as a freshman and sophomore before moving to 133 pounds for his junior season. He attended the school after graduating from Sheridan High School.
items.sourceLabel: Colorado School of Mines · season-by-season roster

items.label: Records 24th win of first college season
items.detail: A Colorado School of Mines report from February 7, 2013 credited Gurule with a 24-14 record after winning a 125-pound dual match against New Mexico Highlands. He was tied for his team's lead in victories at that point of his freshman season.
items.sourceLabel: Colorado School of Mines · Feb. 7, 2013 wrestling report

items.label: Transfers to Adams State for final wrestling years
items.detail: After Colorado School of Mines, Gurule appeared on Adams State University's wrestling roster as a 141-pound redshirt junior for 2016–17 and a redshirt senior for 2017–18. Both schools competed in NCAA Division II.
items.sourceLabel: Adams State University · wrestling athlete roster

items.label: Knee injuries disrupt end of college wrestling career
items.detail: In his UFC athlete Q&A, Gurule said he suffered serious knee injuries at regional competitions during his final two years of college wrestling while highly ranked. The injuries affected his ability to complete the wrestling career he had planned; exact surgery dates or recovery durations are not established in the available records.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · firsthand athlete account of college injuries

items.label: Works as a geologist before pursuing MMA
items.detail: After his Adams State wrestling career, Gurule worked as a geologist. A 2024 MMA Junkie profile explains that he missed competition, tried Brazilian jiu-jitsu and eventually found Factory X in Colorado. The profile does not establish the precise start and end dates of his geology job.

items.label: Begins serious MMA training at Factory X
items.detail: Around mid-2021, Gurule started full MMA training after investigating jiu-jitsu. He had high-level wrestling experience but was new to professional striking; in a UFC interview he said he had taken his first kickboxing class roughly five months before his first MMA fight.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie · MMA transition and debut preparations

items.label: Develops striking alongside Colorado UFC teammates
items.detail: Trained at Factory X in the Denver area. In UFC interviews Gurule named Brandon Royval, Corey Sandhagen and Alexander Hernandez among his main training partners. He was building boxing, kicking and submission offense around his competitive wrestling base rather than entering MMA as an experienced kickboxer.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · training partners and MMA background

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · DeMarcus Patterson · LFA 116
items.detail: In his earliest listed amateur MMA fight, Gurule stopped DeMarcus Patterson by punches at 1:45 of the first round at LFA 116: Fremd vs. Valente. This was an amateur result and is not counted in his professional 11-4 record.

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Bryan Mears · MCF 22
items.detail: Stopped Bryan Mears by strikes at 1:22 of round one at MCF 22: St. Paddy's Beatdown 10. Sherdog lists his documented amateur start at two wins from two bouts, both by first-round stoppage.

items.label: WIN · Anthony Valenzuela · LFA 133: Stack vs. Delano
items.detail: Defeated Anthony Valenzuela by TKO (punches) at 1:16 of round 1 at LFA 133: Stack vs. Delano. Made his professional debut with a first-round finish after two documented amateur victories. Professional record: 1-0.

items.label: WIN · Josiah Reyes · LFA 141: Talundžić vs. Brown
items.detail: Defeated Josiah Reyes by TKO (knee and punches) at 1:15 of round 1 at LFA 141: Talundžić vs. Brown. A second straight first-round stoppage in LFA; Gurule was already showing finishing ability rather than relying exclusively on his wrestling. Professional record: 2-0.

items.label: WIN · Jayson Scott · MCF 23: Salute to Veterans 2
items.detail: Defeated Jayson Scott by TKO (strikes) at 2:44 of round 1 at MCF 23: Salute to Veterans 2. Moved to 3-0 in the professional ranks with his third consecutive opening-round finish. Professional record: 3-0.

items.label: WIN · Ryan Mondala · Colorado Combat Club 15
items.detail: Defeated Ryan Mondala by TKO (punches and elbows) at 3:28 of round 2 at Colorado Combat Club 15. Continued his four-fight finishing run, this time in the second round rather than the first. Professional record: 4-0.

items.label: Closes rookie professional year 4-0
items.detail: Gurule finished his first year as a professional with four victories by TKO: two under the LFA banner, one with MCF and one at Colorado Combat Club. All four ended inside two rounds.

items.label: WIN · Carlos Lozoya · Fury FC 79
items.detail: Defeated Carlos Lozoya by TKO (punches) at 0:41 of round 3 at Fury FC 79. Made his Fury FC debut and earned a third-round stoppage. This was the first of his professional fights to reach round three. Professional record: 5-0.

items.label: WIN · Jonathan Davis · Fury FC 82: Moran vs. Trujillo
items.detail: Defeated Jonathan Davis by unanimous decision at 5:00 of round 3 at Fury FC 82: Moran vs. Trujillo. Went the full distance for the first time as a professional and won on all three judges' cards. The bout was contested at bantamweight. Professional record: 6-0.

items.label: WIN · Gerardo Graniel · Fury Challenger Series 8
items.detail: Defeated Gerardo Graniel by unanimous decision at 5:00 of round 3 at Fury Challenger Series 8. Banked another three-round decision on the Fury regional circuit, demonstrating he could win over a full fight without an early finish. Professional record: 7-0.

items.label: Proposed Josh Walker fight canceled
items.detail: A scheduled bantamweight matchup against Josh Walker at Fury FC 85 was canceled, with Tapology identifying an injury to Gurule as the reason. This booking produced no official result and should not be counted as a bout.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · fight schedule and canceled booking

items.label: WIN · Alberto Trujillo · Fury FC 89: Richardson vs. Aswell
items.detail: Defeated Alberto Trujillo by unanimous decision at 5:00 of round 3 at Fury FC 89: Richardson vs. Aswell. Gurule later described this as his hardest fight to that point because Trujillo switched tactics and was shorter than him, making it difficult to land cleanly. It was his third consecutive decision win. Professional record: 8-0.

items.label: Moves into regional flyweight title contention
items.detail: At 8-0, Gurule was described by MMA Junkie as one of the leading unsigned flyweights in North America. The outlet reported prior UFC short-notice inquiries that did not develop into bookings, ahead of his five-round Fury FC title fight.

items.label: WIN · Jacob Silva · Fury FC 96: Silva vs. Gurule
items.detail: Defeated Jacob Silva by technical submission (arm-triangle choke) at 2:32 of round 4 at Fury FC 96: Silva vs. Gurule. Won the Fury FC flyweight championship in the main event in Houston. This was his first professional submission finish and the longest fight of his career to that point. Professional record: 9-0.

items.label: Claims Fury FC flyweight championship
items.detail: Gurule's fourth-round arm-triangle finish of Jacob Silva brought him the Fury FC flyweight title. The title outcome is a separate career milestone, not another fight or win. He was 9-0 in professional MMA.

items.label: Accepts Contender Series fight on six days' notice
items.detail: Gurule says he accepted the Nick Piccininni matchup on only six days' notice and had to cut about 30 pounds to make flyweight. Piccininni was a decorated American collegiate wrestler. The short preparation and rapid cut added an unusual challenge to the opportunity.

items.label: WIN · Nick Piccininni · DWCS Season 8, Week 10
items.detail: Defeated Nick Piccininni by split decision (29-28, 29-28, 28-29) at 5:00 of round 3 at DWCS Season 8, Week 10. Despite repeated takedowns by Piccininni, Gurule repeatedly returned to his feet and landed enough offense to win two judges' cards. He earned a UFC contract at the conclusion of the final episode of the 2024 Contender Series season. Professional record: 10-0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Contender Series results and scorecards

items.label: Awarded UFC contract after DWCS split decision
items.detail: Dana White signed Gurule following the split-decision win over Piccininni. The victory moved his professional record to 10-0 and advanced him directly from Fury FC to the UFC roster; the contract itself is not a separate bout.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · DWCS Season 8, Week 10 contract winners

items.label: LOSS · Ode' Osbourne · UFC Fight Night: Emmett vs. Murphy
items.detail: Lost to Ode' Osbourne by TKO (punches) at 1:54 of round 2 at UFC Fight Night: Emmett vs. Murphy. Made his official UFC debut as the betting favorite against the more experienced Ode' Osbourne, but was stopped in the second round. It was his first professional loss and ended a 10-fight winning streak. Professional record: 10-1.

items.label: LOSS · Jesus Aguilar · Noche UFC: Lopes vs. Silva
items.detail: Lost to Jesus Aguilar by unanimous decision (30-27, 29-28, 29-28) at 5:00 of round 3 at Noche UFC: Lopes vs. Silva. Lost a competitive three-round fight to Aguilar. The result was scored for Aguilar by all three judges, with two giving Gurule one round; it was not a split decision. Professional record: 10-2.

items.label: LOSS · Alden Coria · UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Hernandez
items.detail: Lost to Alden Coria by unanimous decision at 5:00 of round 3 at UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Hernandez. Lost his third straight UFC fight by unanimous decision in Houston, Texas. His pro record stood at 10-3, and he was still looking for his first UFC victory. Professional record: 10-3.

items.label: WIN · Daniel Barez · UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa
items.detail: Defeated Daniel Barez by unanimous decision (30-27 on all three cards) at 5:00 of round 3 at UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Costa. Earned his first UFC victory after three consecutive defeats. All three judges awarded Gurule every round, 30-27, demonstrating a full-fight performance rather than another close decision. Professional record: 11-3.

items.label: Returns to competition only two weeks after Barez win
items.detail: After beating Daniel Barez on May 16, Gurule accepted a short-notice replacement booking against Rei Tsuruya for UFC Macau on May 30. He stepped in after Jesus Aguilar withdrew. This set up two UFC fights within 14 days, and the second contest was booked at bantamweight because both fighters usually compete at flyweight.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Mania · May 2026 short-notice replacement booking

items.label: LOSS · Rei Tsuruya · UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Figueiredo
items.detail: Lost to Rei Tsuruya by submission (recorded as a rear-naked choke on UFC's athlete page and a neck crank by Sherdog) at 3:19 of round one in the UFC Macau preliminary card. He stepped in on short notice after Jesus Aguilar withdrew, just 14 days after his victory over Daniel Barez. Tsuruya landed an early left hook, took top position, transitioned to the back and secured the finish. This was Gurule's fourth UFC loss. Professional record: 11-4; UFC record: 1-4.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · UFC Macau play-by-play and bout report

items.label: Booked to face unbeaten Bilal Hasan at UFC 334
items.detail: MMA Junkie and MMA Fighting reported Gurule's matchup with unbeaten prospect Bilal Hasan, scheduled for November 14 at Madison Square Garden. Gurule was 11-4 and Hasan 10-0 at the announcement; the contest was a booking, not a completed fight.

items.label: UFC 334 · vs. Bilal Hasan in New York
items.detail: Scheduled to face Bilal Hasan at UFC 334 in Madison Square Garden, New York City. Gurule enters at 11-4 overall and 1-4 in the UFC, with the May 30 submission loss as his most recent result. No outcome exists as of October 27, 2026.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · official matchup listing; UFC 334 event

Bilal Hasan.name: Bilal Hasan
Bilal Hasan.subtitle: Career chronology · taekwondo, CFFC championship, and 11 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in Hawaii; raised in Washington
items.detail: Bilal Hasan was born on July 16, 2001, in Hawaii and grew up in Mukilteo, Washington. His parents are from Indonesia, whose flag he represents in combat sports. His birth date comes from his Sherdog fighter listing and his birthplace and upbringing from a University of Washington Bothell alumni interview.

items.label: Starts taekwondo at age five
items.detail: Hasan began martial arts through taekwondo at five. He recalled struggling badly in his earliest tournaments before becoming an accomplished junior competitor; his striking background predates MMA by well over a decade.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · early martial arts account

items.label: U.S. junior taekwondo medals and Korea team-demo bronze
items.detail: Team USA's taekwondo profile lists a silver medal in 33 kg black-belt sparring at the 2013 national championships, a silver in black-belt poomsae and bronze in team demonstration at Hanmadang Korea. These are taekwondo results, not MMA bouts.

items.label: Gold · Pan Am International junior taekwondo
items.detail: Won gold in black-belt sparring at 37 kg at the 2014 Pan Am International and a national team-demonstration gold. Hasan later identified the Pan Am International title as one of his proudest youth taekwondo achievements.
items.sourceLabel: Team USA · competition results and athlete Q&A

items.label: AAU national taekwondo champion
items.detail: Won the 2015 AAU national black-belt sparring title at 41 kg. Team USA also lists a silver at the U.S. national championships in the same weight class, and a U.S. Open bronze at 37 kg.

items.label: Selected for USA Taekwondo cadet national B team
items.detail: Named to the USA Taekwondo cadet national B team in the 41 kg class, an early step toward competing for the United States internationally.

items.label: Gold · Canada Open junior taekwondo
items.detail: Won the junior 45 kg division at the Canada Open. He was competing in international Olympic-style taekwondo before turning sixteen.

items.label: Competes at Junior World Taekwondo Championships
items.detail: Represented Team USA in the men's finweight (45 kg) division at the World Junior Championships in Burnaby, British Columbia. The record confirms participation, not a medal at that event.
items.sourceLabel: Team USA · junior world championship appearance

items.label: Gold · U.S. Open junior taekwondo
items.detail: Won the junior 48 kg gold medal at the U.S. Open, beating five opponents in the elimination bracket and defeating Ian Kim 18–2 in the final. This was a documented international junior competition rather than a national MMA championship.
items.sourceLabel: Team USA · 2017 U.S. Open bracket and results

items.label: Gold · Spanish Open junior taekwondo
items.detail: Added a Spanish Open gold in 2017, one of the final international taekwondo results listed on his Team USA profile. The exact contest date is not specified there.

items.label: Shifts focus from taekwondo to mixed martial arts
items.detail: Hasan gradually moved from competitive taekwondo into MMA, applying his kicking and movement skills to the wider demands of striking, wrestling, ground control and submissions. Available sources do not establish an exact first MMA training date.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · martial arts and MMA career account

items.label: Trains at Charlie's Combat Club in Everett
items.detail: Established his MMA base at Charlie's Combat Club in Everett, Washington, where he later also worked as a coach. The exact date he first joined is not publicly confirmed, but the gym was his listed affiliation throughout his professional rise.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · club affiliation and coaching work

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Aman Amwar · LOC 1: A New Beginning
items.detail: Defeated Aman Amwar by TKO (strikes) in round 2 at 2:59 at LOC 1: A New Beginning. Earliest documented amateur MMA win; he began testing his taekwondo-based offense in full mixed-martial-arts competition. Amateur results do not count toward Hasan's professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Bilal Hasan amateur fight history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Aaron Cortez · Legion of Combat 2
items.detail: Defeated Aaron Cortez by TKO (strikes) in round 1 at 2:49 at Legion of Combat 2. Second recorded amateur win, another stoppage, this time in the opening round. Amateur results do not count toward Hasan's professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Bilal Hasan amateur fight history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Jaiden Bundy · COGA: Supreme Showdown 6
items.detail: Defeated Jaiden Bundy by TKO (strikes) in round 3 at 1:04 at COGA: Supreme Showdown 6. His third documented amateur victory and third stoppage. Amateur results do not count toward Hasan's professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Bilal Hasan amateur fight history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Xavier Rake · COGA Amateur Fight Series: Fight Quest 4
items.detail: Defeated Xavier Rake by TKO (punches) in round 2 at 2:54 at COGA Amateur Fight Series: Fight Quest 4. Fourth documented amateur victory, all four achieved by strikes. Amateur results do not count toward Hasan's professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Bilal Hasan amateur fight history

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Christian Tariji · Rogue Promotions: Arena Wars Fighting Series
items.detail: Defeated Christian Tariji by unanimous decision in round 5 at Rogue Promotions: Arena Wars Fighting Series. Went to a decision in a scheduled five-round amateur bout, giving him more distance-fighting experience before his professional debut. His five documented amateur fights were all victories. Amateur results do not count toward Hasan's professional record.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Bilal Hasan amateur fight history

items.label: Studies Health Studies at UW Bothell while training
items.detail: Attended the University of Washington Bothell, balancing full-time MMA training with his Health Studies coursework. He later described studying health as a way to better understand the human body and build useful routines for athletic performance.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · academic and training biography

items.label: WIN · Xhelal Lleshi · CFFC 116
items.detail: Defeated Xhelal Lleshi by split decision in round 3 at 5:00 at CFFC 116. Sherdog · CFFC 116 pro debut Professional record: His professional MMA debut was also his only win by judges' decision through October 2026. It is important not to describe every victory in his unbeaten run as a finish..

items.label: Graduates from UW Bothell with Health Studies degree
items.detail: Graduated from the School of Nursing & Health Studies in 2023, after having already made his professional MMA debut in December 2022. He later credited the demands of education and full-time training with improving his preparation and self-analysis.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · Health Studies Class of 2023

items.label: NC · Sonny Suranjin · COGA 75: MMA Summer Showdown
items.detail: Faced Sonny Suranjin; official result: no contest in round 1 at 0:07 at COGA 75: MMA Summer Showdown. Sherdog · COGA 75 no-contest record Professional record: The scheduled fight ended after only seven seconds with no official winner. It is a separate professional no contest, not an eleventh victory or a defeat; records should read 10-0 with 1 NC..

items.label: WIN · Orlando Ortega · CFFC 123
items.detail: Defeated Orlando Ortega by TKO (body kick and punches) in round 1 at 4:15 at CFFC 123. undefined Professional record: First professional stoppage and second official win. Hasan used body attacks to put the fight away inside the opening round..

items.label: WIN · Jacob Romano · CFFC 129
items.detail: Defeated Jacob Romano by KO (spinning wheel kick) in round 2 at 0:23 at CFFC 129. undefined Professional record: Scored a spectacular second-round knockout with a spinning wheel kick, one of the results that raised his visibility on the Cage Fury circuit. The UFC later specifically highlighted this finish in his athlete biography..

items.label: WIN · Shamel Findley · CFFC 132
items.detail: Defeated Shamel Findley by KO (punches) in round 1 at 4:33 at CFFC 132. undefined Professional record: Another first-round finish, taking Hasan to 4-0 with a no contest ahead of a Cage Fury championship opportunity..

items.label: Harris Bonfiglio withdraws; Jose Leon steps in
items.detail: Hasan had been scheduled to face submission specialist Harris Bonfiglio for CFFC's vacant flyweight title, but Bonfiglio withdrew through injury. Jose Leon accepted the championship bout as a replacement, making it a changed booking rather than a second fight.

items.label: WIN · Jose Leon · CFFC 136
items.detail: Defeated Jose Leon by rear-naked choke submission in round 2 at 2:16 at CFFC 136. CFFC · official title-winning result Professional record: Won the vacant CFFC flyweight championship in New Town, North Dakota. He took Leon's back during a scramble and secured the first submission victory of his professional career..

items.label: Becomes CFFC flyweight champion
items.detail: The win over Jose Leon gave Hasan the vacant 125-pound Cage Fury championship. This milestone records the belt change, not a second victory. He was 5-0, with one no contest, and had won four of five professional victories inside the distance.

items.label: WIN · Brian Hauser · CFFC 139
items.detail: Defeated Brian Hauser by KO/TKO (body punch) in round 2 at 2:11 at CFFC 139. CFFC · CFFC 139 official results Professional record: Made his first CFFC flyweight title defense in Philadelphia. Hauser attempted to use wrestling, but Hasan hurt him early, escaped his takedown attempts and ended the fight with a body shot..

items.label: WIN · Jason Eastman · CFFC 143
items.detail: Defeated Jason Eastman by TKO (front kick to the body and punches) in round 4 at 1:46 at CFFC 143. CFFC · full championship bout recap Professional record: Second successful defense of the CFFC title. Eastman attacked with dangerous leg locks and grappling attempts, carrying the fight into round four before Hasan's sustained strikes forced the stoppage. This was his first fight into the fourth round..

items.label: Survives strongest grappling test of CFFC reign
items.detail: Eastman scored takedowns, attacked the heel and threatened other submissions. Hasan defended long enough to regain the standing exchanges and stop him in round four. Hasan described the extended test as valuable experience that his prior quick finishes had not provided.

items.label: UW Bothell profiles Hasan as regional champion
items.detail: His university published an alumni profile describing his 2023 Health Studies graduation, work coaching at Charlie's Combat Club, Indonesian family connections, and growing following in Indonesia. Hasan explained that he viewed his fighting career as both a competition and a way of entertaining an audience.

items.label: Visits Indonesia; builds connection with local fans
items.detail: In a 2025 interview, Hasan described visiting Indonesia to work with sponsors and being surprised by the number of supporters who recognized him. His nickname 'The IndoNinja' reflects that Indonesian heritage. The date of that sponsor visit was not independently established.
items.sourceLabel: UW Bothell · Indonesia trip and athlete interview

items.label: WIN · Renaldy Manse · CFFC 149
items.detail: Defeated Renaldy Manse by TKO (body punch) in round 1 at 2:47 at CFFC 149. CFFC · official CFFC 149 results Professional record: Successfully defended his CFFC flyweight title for a third time against another unbeaten prospect, Manse, who also had Indonesian roots. The stoppage came by a body shot in the first round..

items.label: Completes third CFFC flyweight title defense
items.detail: Hasan's consecutive championship defenses came against Brian Hauser, Jason Eastman and Renaldy Manse in February, June and December 2025. He finished all three challengers and closed the year 8-0 with one no contest.

items.label: Trains with Demetrious Johnson while preparing for UFC opportunity
items.detail: Hasan's training circle included UFC Hall of Famer and former flyweight champion Demetrious Johnson. The UFC documented their connection ahead of the 2026 Contender Series; the precise date of the first training sessions was not published.

items.label: WIN · Mridul Saikia · DWCS Season 10, Week 1
items.detail: Defeated Mridul Saikia by TKO (right hand and ground punches) in round 1 at 0:45 at DWCS Season 10, Week 1. UFC · official DWCS results and contract winners Professional record: Dropped Saikia with a counter right hand and finished with ground strikes in 45 seconds at the Meta APEX in Las Vegas. The first DWCS win of his career moved him to 9-0 with one no contest..

items.label: Earns UFC contract from Dana White
items.detail: Dana White awarded Hasan a UFC contract after the 45-second Saikia stoppage, noting the considerable pre-fight expectations surrounding him. It was Season 10's opening week of Contender Series. This is a contract milestone, not a separate fight result.

items.label: Offered UFC Shanghai debut within hours
items.detail: Hasan said his coach Ryan Diaz received an offer to fight Nilson Rojas in Shanghai only about two hours after he finished his Contender Series opponent. He accepted the fight, setting up a promotional debut 18 days after the contract win.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Junkie · interview about short-notice Shanghai offer

items.label: WIN · Nilson Rojas · UFC Shanghai: Nurmagomedov vs. Song
items.detail: Defeated Nilson Rojas by KO (right hand) in round 2 at 2:28 at UFC Shanghai: Nurmagomedov vs. Song. UFC · official Shanghai results and fight recap Professional record: Won his official UFC debut against the previously unbeaten Rojas. Rojas briefly disrupted Hasan with a push kick in round two, but Hasan recovered and knocked him out with a right hand; the fight opened the main card. UFC record: 1-0..

items.label: Moves to 10-0 with nine professional finishes
items.detail: The victory over Rojas brought his professional record to ten wins, no losses and one no contest. Eight were KO/TKO victories, one a submission and one a split decision; his UFC record stood at 1-0. This is a record milestone, not an additional fight.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete record and finish breakdown

items.label: Bilal Hasan vs. Luis Gurule booked for UFC 334
items.detail: MMA Fighting confirmed the flyweight matchup for November 14 at Madison Square Garden. Gurule was 11-4 entering the booking, while Hasan was 10-0 (1 NC), coming off his Shanghai knockout. The planned bout will be Hasan's second official UFC fight.

items.label: Discusses rapid UFC schedule before second bout
items.detail: Hasan told a podcast he had initially wanted to build his UFC career gradually, but accepted two fast bookings after his DWCS win: a UFC debut 18 days later and another appearance before year-end. These statements described his plans as of October, not additional completed fights.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · October 21 comments ahead of UFC 334

items.label: UFC 334 · scheduled flyweight bout vs. Luis Gurule
items.detail: Scheduled to face Luis Gurule at Madison Square Garden in New York City as part of UFC 334. Hasan enters at 10-0 with one no contest, and an official UFC record of 1-0. As of October 27, 2026, the fight has not taken place and no outcome should be recorded.

Caio Borralho.name: Caio Borralho
Caio Borralho.subtitle: Career chronology · judo, Fighting Nerds, and 21 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in São Luís, Maranhão, Brazil
items.detail: Caio Vinicius Silva Borralho was born in São Luís in the state of Maranhão, Brazil. His career later developed in São Paulo, where he became a central member of the Fighting Nerds team.

items.label: Begins training in judo under Emílio Moreira
items.detail: Borralho says his mother enrolled him in judo at six to help him use his energy and develop discipline. His first coach, Emílio Moreira, remained an important figure in his life. He later competed at state, regional and national levels in judo.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and judo background

items.label: Competes in regional and national judo
items.detail: He has described winning regional and national judo titles before choosing MMA. The available UFC biography does not give a complete dated medal list, so individual championships are not assigned invented years.

items.label: Works teaching mathematics, chemistry and judo
items.detail: Borralho has said he began teaching mathematics around age 15 and later worked teaching chemistry and judo. He studied industrial chemistry before leaving his hometown, and subsequently completed a physical education degree. Those jobs helped support him before MMA became his career.

items.label: Adds Brazilian jiu-jitsu to his judo foundation
items.detail: After losing a judo bout by armlock, Borralho's sensei pushed him toward Brazilian jiu-jitsu so he could improve his ground fighting. He initially disliked the switch but grew to appreciate the discipline and later earned a BJJ black belt.

items.label: Wins amateur kickboxing match and commits to MMA
items.detail: Borralho has recalled an amateur kickboxing victory by second-round knockout that helped convince him to pursue professional fighting. He considered Olympic judo a difficult path and instead set his sights on MMA.

items.label: Moves from São Luís to São Paulo to pursue fighting
items.detail: Left his home city and chemistry studies to move to São Paulo in 2014. He has said the move was financially difficult, without established sponsorship, but he wanted stronger MMA training opportunities and a path toward the UFC.

items.label: Meets coach Pablo Sucupira at Combat Club
items.detail: Borralho began working with Pablo Sucupira, then running Combat Club, originally a striking-focused training operation in São Paulo. Their collaboration pushed the gym toward a dedicated MMA program. The group later became known as Fighting Nerds.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · history of Fighting Nerds

items.label: AMATEUR WIN · Rômulo Oliveira · Bradar Fight
items.detail: Stopped Rômulo Oliveira with punches at 2:10 of round one at Bradar Fight Night 1. Sherdog records this as an amateur MMA contest; it does not count toward his 18–2 professional record.

items.label: WIN · Cleiton Rafael · Evocke Fight: Gods of War
items.detail: Defeated Cleiton Rafael at Evocke Fight: Gods of War. via KO (punch) in round 1 at 1:48. Won his professional MMA debut by first-round knockout. The win came after moving to São Paulo to pursue fighting full time. Professional MMA record after the bout: 1–0.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: LOSS · João Carvalho · Bradar Fight 3
items.detail: Lost to João Carvalho at Bradar Fight 3. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. His first professional defeat came in front of friends and family in his home region. Borralho has said he expected the trip home to be an easier fight; the experience changed his approach to training. Professional MMA record after the bout: 1–1.

items.label: Rebuilds regional career after first loss
items.detail: Following the Carvalho defeat, Borralho returned to his São Paulo training base and began a long run without a professional loss. The setback remained his only defeat until the UFC Paris fight with Nassourdine Imavov in 2025.

items.label: WIN · Edson Junior · Thunder Fight 9
items.detail: Defeated Edson Junior at Thunder Fight 9. via rear-naked choke submission in round 3 at 3:05. Earned the second victory of his professional career and his first recorded submission win after a year away from competition. Professional MMA record after the bout: 2–1.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Luiz Carlos Alves · Arena Combat: Fight Night 2
items.detail: Defeated Luiz Carlos Alves at Arena Combat: Fight Night 2. via TKO in round 1 at 0:20. First of two professional victories against Alves. This was the 2017 stoppage; the two fought again in 2019 under the Mega Fight Championship banner. Professional MMA record after the bout: 3–1.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: NC · Raylander Marques · Vikings Fight Club 2
items.detail: Fought Raylander Marques at Vikings Fight Club 2. The contest was ruled a no contest in round 1. The result was officially recorded as a no contest. Public fight records do not consistently explain the cause; it is not a win or loss. Professional MMA record after the bout: 3–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Douglas Nascimento · Batalha MMA 14
items.detail: Defeated Douglas Nascimento at Batalha MMA 14. via TKO (punches) in round 1 at 1:13. Won by first-round strikes in his next recorded appearance. By this period his regional career was centered on middleweight. Professional MMA record after the bout: 4–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: Helps develop the early Fighting Nerds training system
items.detail: Coach Pablo Sucupira and Borralho worked closely on an analytical approach to MMA training. Coaches Wagner Mota and later Flavio Alvaro added grappling and MMA-specific experience. It was a developing São Paulo team, not yet the high-profile UFC stable it became in 2024–25.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · founding coaches and team development

items.label: WIN · Luiz Carlos Alves · Mega Fight Championship 2
items.detail: Defeated Luiz Carlos Alves at Mega Fight Championship 2. via anaconda choke submission in round 1 at 1:37. Beat Alves again, this time by anaconda choke. Tapology lists the finish at 1:37; some historical databases list 2:03, a timing discrepancy preserved by prioritizing the Tapology entry. Professional MMA record after the bout: 5–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Otávio Sagás · Future FC 8
items.detail: Defeated Otávio Sagás at Future FC 8. via guillotine choke submission in round 1 at 3:44. Made his first Future FC appearance and finished in round one. The victory advanced him toward a future middleweight championship opportunity. Professional MMA record after the bout: 6–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Ykaro Queiroz · Future FC 10
items.detail: Defeated Ykaro Queiroz at Future FC 10. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Won a three-round decision against Queiroz in the co-main event, showing a more measured, distance-managing approach than in his earlier submission finishes. Professional MMA record after the bout: 7–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: Becomes a Future FC middleweight title contender
items.detail: After wins over Otávio Sagás and Ykaro Queiroz, Borralho secured a fight for the vacant Future FC 185-pound championship. This was his first major regional belt opportunity.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Future FC fight and title history

items.label: WIN · Wildemar Souza Santos · Future FC 12: Night of Champions
items.detail: Defeated Wildemar Souza Santos at Future FC 12: Night of Champions. via unanimous decision in round 5 at 5:00. Won the vacant Future FC middleweight championship over five rounds. Some databases incorrectly show a three-round duration; Tapology identifies it as a scheduled five-round title bout. Professional MMA record after the bout: 8–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: Becomes Future FC middleweight champion
items.detail: The Wildemar Souza Santos decision earned Borralho his first recorded professional MMA championship. This marks the belt win separately from the fight result and does not add a second bout.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A confirms Future FC championship

items.label: Strengthens Fighting Nerds coaching team
items.detail: As the team prepared its first major Contender Series breakthrough, longtime coach Pablo Sucupira brought in veteran MMA fighter Flavio Alvaro alongside jiu-jitsu coach Wagner Mota. Their work helped turn the gym from a local team into a more complete professional training program.

items.label: WIN · Aaron Jeffery · DWCS Season 5, Week 5
items.detail: Defeated Aaron Jeffery at DWCS Season 5, Week 5. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Won his first Contender Series opportunity at middleweight but did not receive a UFC contract. The promotion later gave him a second chance only three weeks later. Professional MMA record after the bout: 9–1 (1 NC).

items.label: Returns to Contender Series after first win without contract
items.detail: Dana White did not sign Borralho following the decision over Aaron Jeffery. Rather than waiting for another season, Borralho accepted a second Contender Series appearance three weeks later, this time at light heavyweight.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Contender Series official fight recap

items.label: WIN · Jesse Murray · DWCS Season 5, Week 8
items.detail: Defeated Jesse Murray at DWCS Season 5, Week 8. via TKO (ground punches) in round 1 at 1:41. Competed at light heavyweight for the second DWCS appearance, dropped Murray with a left hand and finished with punches on the ground. This second win convinced the UFC to offer him a contract. Professional MMA record after the bout: 10–1 (1 NC).

items.label: Signs UFC contract on second DWCS attempt
items.detail: Dana White signed Borralho after the stoppage of Jesse Murray. Borralho became the first member of the Fighting Nerds team to earn a UFC contract, establishing a path followed by later teammates.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · first Fighting Nerds UFC breakthrough

items.label: Dustin Stoltzfus UFC debut booking canceled
items.detail: Borralho was booked against Dustin Stoltzfus for December 2021 but withdrew. This planned debut did not produce a fight result; his first official UFC bout took place four months later against Gadzhi Omargadzhiev.

items.label: WIN · Gadzhi Omargadzhiev · UFC Fight Night: Luque vs. Muhammad 2
items.detail: Defeated Gadzhi Omargadzhiev at UFC Fight Night: Luque vs. Muhammad 2. via unanimous technical decision in round 3 at 3:56. In his official UFC debut, Borralho won a technical decision after landing an illegal knee on a grounded Omargadzhiev. The foul was deemed accidental and cost Borralho a point; Omargadzhiev could not continue, so the scorecards were read 29–27 on all three judges' cards. UFC record: 1–0. Professional MMA record after the bout: 11–1 (1 NC).

items.label: First UFC appearance ends with unusual technical ruling
items.detail: Borralho's first UFC victory was not a normal three-round decision. The referee ruled a foul late in round three, deducted a point and sent the fight to the scorecards. The technical decision is recorded as an official win, without counting a fourth round or a second bout.

items.label: WIN · Armen Petrosyan · UFC on ESPN: dos Anjos vs. Fiziev
items.detail: Defeated Armen Petrosyan at UFC on ESPN: dos Anjos vs. Fiziev. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Used clinch work and takedowns to disrupt the former kickboxer while limiting the amount of open striking Petrosyan could impose. UFC record: 2–0. Professional MMA record after the bout: 12–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: WIN · Makhmud Muradov · UFC 280
items.detail: Defeated Makhmud Muradov at UFC 280. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Won against the experienced Muradov in Abu Dhabi, extending his official UFC start to three victories in 2022. The bout lasted the full three rounds. Professional MMA record after the bout: 13–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: Completes first UFC year unbeaten at 3–0
items.detail: The technical decision over Omargadzhiev and regular three-round decisions over Petrosyan and Muradov gave Borralho a 3–0 UFC record in his first season. This was a wins-by-decision stretch, not three knockouts or submissions.

items.label: WIN · Michal Oleksiejczuk · UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Simón
items.detail: Defeated Michal Oleksiejczuk at UFC Fight Night: Song vs. Simón. via rear-naked choke submission in round 2 at 2:49. Dropped Oleksiejczuk, advanced to back control and finished with the choke. It was Borralho's first UFC finish and earned Performance of the Night. UFC record: 4–0. Professional MMA record after the bout: 14–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: UFC · first performance bonus and finish

items.label: Earns first UFC Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: The second-round submission of Michal Oleksiejczuk earned Borralho a post-fight performance bonus. It was the first time he had finished an opponent in an official UFC fight.

items.label: WIN · Abus Magomedov · UFC Fight Night: Almeida vs. Lewis
items.detail: Defeated Abus Magomedov at UFC Fight Night: Almeida vs. Lewis. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Won at home in São Paulo. After closely fought opening rounds, Borralho increased his jab and pressure late to secure the decision. He moved to 5–0 in the UFC. Professional MMA record after the bout: 15–1 (1 NC).
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Caio Borralho professional fight history

items.label: Enters UFC middleweight rankings
items.detail: After the November win over Abus Magomedov, Borralho entered the UFC middleweight rankings. His five-fight UFC start had now included one finish and four decisions.

items.label: WIN · Paul Craig · UFC 301: Pantoja vs. Erceg
items.detail: Defeated Paul Craig at UFC 301: Pantoja vs. Erceg. via KO (punches) in round 2 at 2:10. Fought in Rio de Janeiro and knocked out Craig with a left hand after hurting him with combinations. It was Borralho's first knockout inside the UFC, and he earned Performance of the Night. UFC record: 6–0. Professional MMA record after the bout: 16–1 (1 NC).

items.label: Receives second UFC Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: The knockout of Paul Craig earned Borralho another performance bonus and showed that his UFC wins were no longer exclusively decisions or grappling finishes.

items.label: WIN · Jared Cannonier · UFC on ESPN: Cannonier vs. Borralho
items.detail: Defeated Jared Cannonier at UFC on ESPN: Cannonier vs. Borralho. via unanimous decision in round 5 at 5:00. Headlined his first UFC main event against a former middleweight title challenger. Borralho hurt Cannonier late and won 49–45, 49–45 and 48–46 after five rounds. They received Fight of the Night honors. UFC record: 7–0. Professional MMA record after the bout: 17–1 (1 NC).

items.label: First UFC main event and Fight of the Night bonus
items.detail: In his first scheduled five-round UFC main event, Borralho defeated Jared Cannonier and shared Fight of the Night honors. He emerged from 2024 with seven consecutive UFC victories and greater visibility as a ranked contender.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official Fight of the Night report

items.label: Fighting Nerds establish a major UFC presence
items.detail: The gym's fighters Carlos Prates, Jean Silva and Mauricio Ruffy joined Borralho in posting a high-profile run of UFC wins. Their coaches emphasized fight study and customized preparation, and the team became widely recognized in MMA. Borralho was the original UFC breakthrough but not the sole founder.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Fighting Nerds coaches and expansion

items.label: GRAPPLING WIN · Brendan Allen · Karate Combat 53
items.detail: Defeated UFC middleweight Brendan Allen by unanimous decision over two five-minute rounds in an openweight professional grappling match. The contest was not an MMA bout, is not an eighth UFC win and does not change his professional MMA record.

items.label: LOSS · Nassourdine Imavov · UFC Fight Night: Imavov vs. Borralho
items.detail: Lost to Nassourdine Imavov at UFC Fight Night: Imavov vs. Borralho. via unanimous decision in round 5 at 5:00. Headlined in Paris and lost 50–45, 49–46 and 49–46. Imavov controlled much of the striking rhythm and forced Borralho to retreat; the defeat ended his 7–0 undefeated UFC start. UFC record: 7–1. Professional MMA record after the bout: 17–2 (1 NC).

items.label: First UFC defeat ends seven-fight UFC winning streak
items.detail: The five-round decision to Nassourdine Imavov was Borralho's first loss since July 2015 and his first UFC loss. He remained a ranked middleweight but had to rebuild momentum before securing a title opportunity.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · 2025 Paris result and event report

items.label: WIN · Reinier de Ridder · UFC 326: Holloway vs. Oliveira 2
items.detail: Defeated Reinier de Ridder at UFC 326: Holloway vs. Oliveira 2. via unanimous decision in round 3 at 5:00. Defeated former ONE Championship two-division champion de Ridder 30–27 on all three scorecards in the co-main event. Borralho defended most takedown attempts and finished the third round in top control. UFC record: 8–1. Professional MMA record after the bout: 18–2 (1 NC).

items.label: Discloses rib injury suffered shortly before UFC 326
items.detail: In an interview after the Reinier de Ridder victory, Borralho said he had suffered a displaced rib about fifteen days before the bout, interfering with grappling training. This is his reported injury and its effect on preparation, not an independent medical finding.
items.sourceLabel: Ag Fight · Borralho post-fight injury disclosure

items.label: UFC 334 fight with Yousri Belgaroui announced
items.detail: The UFC announced a three-round middleweight matchup between Borralho and Yousri Belgaroui at Madison Square Garden on November 14. The promotion described Borralho as coming off his March win over de Ridder and placed him sixth in its Meta UFC Rankings at the time of announcement.

items.label: UFC 334 · scheduled bout vs. Yousri Belgaroui
items.detail: Scheduled to fight Yousri Belgaroui at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Borralho enters at 18–2 with one no contest and an 8–1 official UFC record. The bout has not occurred as of October 27, 2026; no result should be assigned.

Yousri Belgaroui.name: Yousri Belgaroui
Yousri Belgaroui.subtitle: Career chronology · GLORY kickboxing and 14 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in Amsterdam, Netherlands
items.detail: Belgaroui grew up in North Amsterdam in a family with Tunisian roots. He has represented Dutch and Tunisian heritage throughout his kickboxing and MMA career. His birth date is June 2, 1992.

items.label: Begins training for combat sports
items.detail: In his UFC athlete Q&A, Belgaroui said he started training to fight at sixteen because he enjoyed watching fights. His early work led toward Dutch-style kickboxing rather than wrestling or Brazilian jiu-jitsu.

items.label: Earns University of Amsterdam degree
items.detail: Belgaroui studied at the University of Amsterdam, in a field he describes to the UFC as organizational sciences; GLORY describes his degree as Public Governance and Management. His exact graduation year is not established by the available athlete biographies.
items.sourceLabel: GLORY Kickboxing · university and career background

items.label: Works in security
items.detail: Belgaroui lists security work as an occupation before establishing himself as a professional fighter. His later media appearances included Dutch television punditry; the dates of his employment and broadcasting jobs are not fully documented.

items.label: Starts professional kickboxing career
items.detail: Belgaroui's UFC biography dates his professional kickboxing career to 2014. He developed in the Dutch kickboxing system and spent several years training at Mike's Gym under Mike Passenier before competing for GLORY.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · kickboxing record and start date

items.label: Early Enfusion kickboxing victories
items.detail: Recorded wins over Tagir Bokov (April 4), Alcorac Caballero (April 18) and Youssef El Yaacoubi (May 24) across Enfusion events. The sequence illustrates his pre-GLORY development and is not part of his eventual MMA fight record.

items.label: European kickboxing title reported
items.detail: Career biographies credit Belgaroui with an IRO European middleweight kickboxing title in 2015. It was not the GLORY world middleweight championship; the available source does not provide a reliably verified bout date or opponent for this specific belt.
items.sourceLabel: MN2S · professional biography and title summary

items.label: Volunteers in Greece at refugee processing center
items.detail: GLORY reports that Belgaroui traveled to Greece at his own expense and spent several weeks helping at a refugee processing center during the European refugee crisis. This is a career-background milestone rather than a competition result.

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Israel Adesanya · Glory of Heroes 4
items.detail: Lost to Israel Adesanya by decision at Glory of Heroes 4. Their first kickboxing meeting was contested outside GLORY and ended in a decision victory for Adesanya. They would meet again in a GLORY contender tournament later in 2016. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.
items.sourceLabel: Muay Thai Records · dated kickboxing bout

items.label: Introduced as GLORY middleweight contender
items.detail: GLORY announced Belgaroui's entry into its middleweight tournament at GLORY 34 Denver, listing him at 18-1 with nine knockouts at the time. At roughly 6 feet 6 inches, his knees and long-range offense made him an unusual middleweight striker.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Ariel Machado · GLORY 34 Denver semifinal
items.detail: Defeated Ariel Machado by unanimous decision at GLORY 34 Denver semifinal. Won his GLORY debut and advanced to the middleweight contender tournament final that same evening. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Israel Adesanya · GLORY 34 Denver final
items.detail: Lost to Israel Adesanya by split decision at GLORY 34 Denver final. The rematch with Adesanya was closely scored but went to Adesanya, leaving Belgaroui runner-up in his first GLORY contender tournament. His kickboxing record against Adesanya stood at 0-2. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: GLORY tournament runner-up on debut
items.detail: Belgaroui reached the GLORY 34 middleweight contender final by beating Ariel Machado before losing a split decision to Israel Adesanya. It was a tournament final, not a fight for the GLORY world middleweight championship.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Agron Preteni · GLORY 40 Copenhagen semifinal
items.detail: Defeated Agron Preteni by unanimous decision at GLORY 40 Copenhagen semifinal. Won the first fight of GLORY's four-man middleweight contender tournament, advancing to a final against Alex Pereira on the same card. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Alex Pereira · GLORY 40 Copenhagen final
items.detail: Defeated Alex Pereira by unanimous decision at GLORY 40 Copenhagen final. Swept all five judges' scorecards for all three rounds against Pereira. The win earned the Ramon Dekkers Memorial Trophy and a title opportunity and gave Belgaroui his only victory in their three-fight kickboxing series.
