Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: Wins GLORY middleweight contender tournament
items.detail: By defeating Agron Preteni and Alex Pereira on the same night, Belgaroui won the GLORY 40 contender tournament and the Ramon Dekkers Memorial Trophy. This was a tournament victory that earned a future world-title shot, not the world title itself.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Jason Wilnis · GLORY 45 Amsterdam
items.detail: Defeated Jason Wilnis by TKO at GLORY 45 Amsterdam in round 1 (2:47). Stopped former middleweight champion Wilnis at home, strengthening his claim to a title fight against Pereira. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Alex Pereira · GLORY 49 Rotterdam world title
items.detail: Lost to Alex Pereira by TKO at GLORY 49 Rotterdam world title in round 3 (1:52). Challenged newly crowned champion Pereira for the GLORY middleweight belt. Belgaroui had success early but Pereira stopped him in round three, making their kickboxing series 1-1. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: First GLORY world middleweight title challenge ends in defeat
items.detail: Belgaroui fought Pereira for the championship at GLORY 49 after having beaten him in the April contender tournament. He lost by third-round stoppage. Pereira had received the earlier title opportunity because of scheduling, a distinction explained in GLORY's contemporary preview.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Dawid Kasperski · GLORY 53 Lille
items.detail: Defeated Dawid Kasperski by TKO at GLORY 53 Lille in round 2. Kasperski stepped in after Jason Wilnis withdrew. Belgaroui scored repeated knockdowns with strikes including body kicks and used the result to call for another world-title fight with Pereira. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Alex Pereira · GLORY 55 New York world title
items.detail: Lost to Alex Pereira by KO at GLORY 55 New York world title in round 1 (2:29). Lost a second GLORY title challenge to Pereira by first-round knockout. Their complete kickboxing series finished with two wins for Pereira and one for Belgaroui. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: Second GLORY title defeat concludes Pereira trilogy
items.detail: The GLORY 55 knockout made Belgaroui 1-2 across three kickboxing meetings with Pereira. This remained a significant rivalry even though they later became MMA training partners in Connecticut.
items.sourceLabel: GLORY · official championship and opponent chronology

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Yassine Ahaggan · GLORY 60 Lyon
items.detail: Defeated Yassine Ahaggan by first-round stoppage at GLORY 60 Lyon in round 1 (1:22). Returned to competition after the Pereira title defeat and secured another finish. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Donovan Wisse · GLORY 65 Utrecht
items.detail: Lost to Donovan Wisse by unanimous decision at GLORY 65 Utrecht. Lost their first kickboxing meeting; all five judges scored the three-round fight 29-27 for Wisse. The rivalry would later lead to a 2021 middleweight world-title match. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Ulric Bokeme · GLORY 69 Düsseldorf
items.detail: Defeated Ulric Bokeme by unanimous decision at GLORY 69 Düsseldorf. Won a GLORY middleweight bout by decision, maintaining his standing among contenders after the Wisse loss. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: KICKBOXING WIN · Jakob Styben · GLORY 75 Utrecht
items.detail: Defeated Jakob Styben by TKO (strikes) at GLORY 75 Utrecht in round 2. Hurt Styben with knees and punches, forcing the stoppage. GLORY's event recap describes a second-round finish; some databases place it in round three, so a disputed exact finishing time is not presented as settled. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: Calls for another shot at Alex Pereira
items.detail: Following the Styben win, Belgaroui publicly challenged GLORY middleweight champion Alex Pereira to a fourth fight. The proposed rematch never became another recorded kickboxing bout between them.

items.label: WIN · Badreddine Diani · UAE Warriors 16: Arabia 1
items.detail: Defeated Badreddine Diani by unanimous decision at UAE Warriors 16: Arabia 1, round 3 (5:00). https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/fighters/237485-yousri-belgaroui-baby-face-assassin Professional MMA record: Made his professional MMA debut after his high-level kickboxing career. His first bout went the full three rounds and was a decision, not a knockout..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: WIN · Sallah-Eddine Dekhissi · UAE Warriors 17: Arabia 2
items.detail: Defeated Sallah-Eddine Dekhissi by TKO (head kick and follow-up strikes) at UAE Warriors 17: Arabia 2, round 1 (2:44). undefined Professional MMA record: Earned his first MMA stoppage. Tapology and Verdict both place the finish in round one; some other databases list round two, a discrepancy kept out of the career totals..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: Begins adapting elite kickboxing to full MMA
items.detail: His early MMA appearances required integrating takedown defense, clinch wrestling, get-ups and ground defense with his existing Dutch-style kickboxing skill. His tall frame and knee attacks remained central weapons, but the new rule set created different vulnerabilities.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete biography and career profile

items.label: KICKBOXING LOSS · Donovan Wisse · GLORY 78 Rotterdam world title
items.detail: Lost to Donovan Wisse by TKO (doctor stoppage) at GLORY 78 Rotterdam world title in round 3 (2:10). Challenged for the vacant GLORY middleweight world championship while also pursuing MMA. The doctor stopped the contest in round three; Wisse took the belt. It was Belgaroui's third unsuccessful GLORY world-title challenge. Kickboxing contests are separate from his professional MMA record.

items.label: Third GLORY world-title challenge ends without the belt
items.detail: After title-fight defeats to Pereira in 2017 and 2018, Belgaroui fought Donovan Wisse for the vacant GLORY middleweight belt in 2021 and lost by doctor stoppage. His kickboxing record must not be described as a GLORY world championship reign.

items.label: LOSS · Ahmed Sami · UAE Warriors 25: Africa
items.detail: Lost to Ahmed Sami by split decision at UAE Warriors 25: Africa, round 3 (5:00). undefined Professional MMA record: Suffered his first MMA defeat in a closely scored fight; he would meet Sami again for a regional light heavyweight championship in 2024..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: WIN · Samir Zaidi · UAE Warriors 27: Africa 2
items.detail: Defeated Samir Zaidi by TKO (punches) at UAE Warriors 27: Africa 2, round 1 (4:32). undefined Professional MMA record: Rebounded from the split-decision loss to Sami with a first-round stoppage..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: LOSS · Mohamad Osseili · UAE Warriors 31: Arabia 8
items.detail: Lost to Mohamad Osseili by unanimous decision at UAE Warriors 31: Arabia 8, round 3 (5:00). undefined Professional MMA record: Fell to 3-2 as an MMA professional. His first two MMA defeats came on the scorecards, not by a stoppage..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: WIN · Bogdan Kotlovyanov · Levels Fight League 7
items.detail: Defeated Bogdan Kotlovyanov by KO/TKO (body punch) at Levels Fight League 7, round 1 (1:15). https://www.tapology.com/fightcenter/fighters/237485-yousri-belgaroui-baby-face-assassin Professional MMA record: Won at approximately 198 pounds in a light heavyweight bout. Tapology and Verdict show the 1:15 stoppage; Sherdog lists 1:50, so the timeline follows the two agreeing sources..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results
items.source: Tapology · LFL 7 result and finish time

items.label: WIN · Stefan Pretorius · UAE Warriors 35: Africa 4
items.detail: Defeated Stefan Pretorius by TKO (knee and punches) at UAE Warriors 35: Africa 4, round 2 (0:43). undefined Professional MMA record: Followed the LFL body-shot finish with another knockout victory three weeks later..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: LOSS · Marco Tulio · DWCS Season 7, Week 4
items.detail: Lost to Marco Tulio by unanimous decision at DWCS Season 7, Week 4, round 3 (5:00). undefined Professional MMA record: Lost his first Dana White's Contender Series appearance to Brazilian middleweight Marco Tulio. The defeat put him at 5-3 and meant he had not earned an UFC contract..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: First Contender Series attempt ends in defeat
items.detail: Belgaroui's three-round loss to Marco Tulio on DWCS was his third MMA loss, all by decision. He continued taking regional fights rather than returning immediately to kickboxing full time.

items.label: WIN · Giorgi Kvelidze · Levels Fight League 10
items.detail: Defeated Giorgi Kvelidze by TKO (body knee and punches) at Levels Fight League 10, round 1 (4:59). undefined Professional MMA record: Returned to the Netherlands regional scene and stopped Kvelidze with one second remaining in the first round..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: WIN · Ahmed Sami · Levels Fight League 11
items.detail: Defeated Ahmed Sami by unanimous decision at Levels Fight League 11, round 5 (5:00). undefined Professional MMA record: Avenged the 2022 split-decision defeat to Sami over five rounds and captured the vacant LFL light heavyweight championship, contested above his usual UFC middleweight class..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: Wins LFL light heavyweight championship
items.detail: His five-round victory over Ahmed Sami secured the vacant Levels Fight League light heavyweight title. This was an MMA belt at light heavyweight, not a GLORY kickboxing world championship and not a second bout.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · Levels Fight League 11 title bout

items.label: Trains with former kickboxing rival Alex Pereira
items.detail: After facing Pereira three times in kickboxing, Belgaroui became a training partner at Teixeira MMA & Fitness in Connecticut, working alongside Pereira and Glover Teixeira. He also served as a corner team member for Pereira's UFC title fights; the exact date of his first camp there is not established.

items.label: WIN · Taiga Iwasaki · DWCS Season 8, Week 5
items.detail: Defeated Taiga Iwasaki by TKO (punches) at DWCS Season 8, Week 5, round 3 (2:34). undefined Professional MMA record: Earned a stoppage in his second Contender Series appearance and improved to 8-3. UFC reporting confirms he did not receive a contract on the night, despite the win..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: Second DWCS win does not immediately earn UFC contract
items.detail: Belgaroui finished Taiga Iwasaki but was not one of the fighters signed after that episode. He eventually entered the UFC roster for his October 2025 debut. The DWCS result counts in his overall pro record, not his official UFC Octagon record.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · 2026 retrospective on unsigned DWCS win

items.label: Original UFC debut with Azamat Bekoev delayed
items.detail: Belgaroui was scheduled to fight Azamat Bekoev at a UFC Fight Night in August, but the bout was canceled after visa issues involving Belgaroui, as listed by Tapology. They instead fought in October in Vancouver; the canceled August booking carries no result.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · canceled booking and stated reason

items.label: WIN · Azamat Bekoev · UFC Fight Night: de Ridder vs. Allen
items.detail: Defeated Azamat Bekoev by TKO (punches) at UFC Fight Night: de Ridder vs. Allen, round 3 (0:55). undefined Professional MMA record: Made his official UFC debut in Vancouver and stopped Bekoev less than a minute into round three after using long strikes and sustained pressure through the earlier rounds. UFC record: 1-0..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: First official UFC victory after two DWCS attempts
items.detail: The stoppage of Bekoev was Belgaroui's first official UFC win, separate from the 2024 DWCS victory. It was his fourth consecutive professional MMA win, with his last loss still being the 2023 decision to Marco Tulio.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Octagon debut and opponent summary

items.label: WIN · Mansur Abdul-Malik · UFC Fight Night: Adesanya vs. Pyfer
items.detail: Defeated Mansur Abdul-Malik by TKO (clinch knee) at UFC Fight Night: Adesanya vs. Pyfer, round 3 (3:39). undefined Professional MMA record: Stopped previously unbeaten Abdul-Malik late in round three in Seattle, earning his second consecutive UFC TKO. UFC record: 2-0..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: Hands Abdul-Malik his first professional defeat
items.detail: Belgaroui's win over Mansur Abdul-Malik was significant because Abdul-Malik had entered undefeated. The finish came through striking in the clinch, demonstrating how the long-range kickboxer could also damage an opponent at close quarters.

items.label: Relocates to Connecticut with family
items.detail: Belgaroui told the UFC that he, his wife and their two children moved to Connecticut, where he trains at Teixeira MMA & Fitness. He has also spoken about supporting anti-bullying and youth outreach through Moving Up. The exact move date is not published.

items.label: WIN · Djorden Santos · Noche UFC: Silva vs. Delgado
items.detail: Defeated Djorden Santos by TKO (strikes) at Noche UFC: Silva vs. Delgado, round 1 (4:25). https://www.ufc.com/news/noche-ufc-official-scorecards-silva-vs-delgado Professional MMA record: Stopped Santos in the opening round in Glendale, Arizona, making it three TKO wins in three official UFC appearances. UFC record: 3-0..
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · dated professional MMA results

items.label: Reaches 11–3 overall and 3–0 in UFC
items.detail: With the finish of Santos, Belgaroui recorded his sixth straight professional MMA victory, including the Contender Series win, and his third official UFC win. His 11 MMA victories consisted of nine KO/TKOs and two decisions; all three losses were on the scorecards.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · record and method summary

items.label: Booked against ranked Caio Borralho at UFC 334
items.detail: UFC announced a three-round middleweight bout against Caio Borralho for November 14 at Madison Square Garden. Borralho was an established top-10 middleweight while Belgaroui entered with three UFC stoppages; this was an announced booking, not a completed result.
items.sourceLabel: UFC Brazil · official September booking announcement

items.label: UFC 334 · Caio Borralho at Madison Square Garden
items.detail: Scheduled to face Caio Borralho in a middleweight bout at UFC 334 in New York City. Enters at 11–3 in professional MMA and 3–0 in official UFC competition. No outcome should be recorded before the scheduled November 14, 2026 fight.

Uroš Medić.name: Uroš Medić
Uroš Medić.subtitle: Career chronology · Serbian kickboxing, Alaska MMA and 17 professional bouts

items.label: Born in Novi Sad, Serbia
items.detail: Uroš Medić was born and raised in Novi Sad, Serbia, then part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. He later represented Serbia while building his fighting career in the United States, initially in Alaska.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · fighter birth date and hometown

items.label: Introduced to judo in childhood
items.detail: Medić has been described as beginning judo around age four before becoming involved in competitive kickboxing as a teenager. This was his earliest foundation in martial arts, preceding his move toward MMA by many years.

items.label: Begins kickboxing at Fight Club Novi Sad
items.detail: A friend introduced Medić to kickboxing at Fight Club Novi Sad when he was sixteen. Kickboxing became his primary competitive base, with timing, southpaw straight punches and attacking combinations later carrying into his MMA style.

items.label: Wins Serbian K-1 and regional kickboxing honors
items.detail: Medić lists a Serbian K-1 national championship and multiple titles in kickboxing disciplines within Vojvodina province. The UFC confirms the honors but does not give exact dates or individual opponents; they are grouped rather than assigned unverified event years.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete listing of kickboxing championships

items.label: Earns WAKO European and Serbia Open medals
items.detail: Medić also lists a medal at the WAKO European Championships in Lignano Sabbiadoro, Italy, and a medal at the Serbia Open World Cup in Belgrade. The placements and dates are not specified in his official UFC biography, so neither is characterized as a world championship victory.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · fighter Q&A on pre-MMA competition honors

items.label: Studies sports and physical education at University of Novi Sad
items.detail: He studied sports and physical education at the University of Novi Sad but moved abroad before completing the degree. His education and early competitive kickboxing both took place in his hometown.

items.label: Moves to Anchorage, Alaska, from Serbia
items.detail: Medić arrived in the United States in 2015 intending to pursue education and work. He settled in Anchorage, Alaska, and later remained there to coach and train. The international move preceded his professional MMA debut by about a year.

items.label: Works varied jobs while building MMA career
items.detail: Before making MMA his full-time occupation, Medić said he had worked in a Serbian betting shop and later in U.S. restaurants, landscaping, construction and car sales, while continuing to train. He also coached at an Anchorage Brazilian jiu-jitsu academy.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete interview and career Q&A

items.label: Develops at Anchorage Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu
items.detail: Anchorage Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu became his early American training base. He combined his established striking background with grappling, competing in Alaska Fighting Championship events while also working as a coach.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · Alaska career and coaching background

items.label: WIN · Rob Rivera · Alaska FC: Land of the Midnight Sun 3
items.detail: Defeated Rob Rivera by TKO (strikes) at Alaska FC: Land of the Midnight Sun 3, round 1 (time not reliably recorded). Made his professional MMA debut in Alaska. Databases differ by one day on the date (June 10 versus June 11), and do not report a reliable finish time; the timeline therefore leaves the time unspecified. This was a regional event, not an UFC appearance. Professional record after bout: 1–0.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · debut date and early professional record

items.label: Limited MMA activity while working in Alaska
items.detail: After his initial professional bout in mid-2016, Medić did not have another recorded professional MMA fight until January 2018. His activities during this gap included continued employment and training; no undocumented bouts are added.

items.label: WIN · Seth Kroll · Alaska FC 136: Cook vs. Mitchell
items.detail: Defeated Seth Kroll by triangle choke submission at Alaska FC 136: Cook vs. Mitchell, round 1 at 1:46. Recorded the first of two triangle-choke finishes in his early professional career. Despite his kickboxing background, the submission showed growth in his ground game. Professional record after bout: 2–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Nathan Feitosa · Alaska FC 138: Lopez vs. Ryan 2
items.detail: Defeated Nathan Feitosa by TKO (punches) at Alaska FC 138: Lopez vs. Ryan 2, round 2 at 0:51. Fought into the second round for the first time in professional MMA and earned his first stoppage beyond round one. Professional record after bout: 3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Jason Flowers · Alaska FC 142: Medić vs. Flowers
items.detail: Defeated Jason Flowers by triangle choke submission at Alaska FC 142: Medić vs. Flowers, round 1 at 3:38. Headlined an Alaska Fighting Championship show and secured another triangle choke. He finished 2018 at 4–0 overall with no fight decided by judges. Professional record after bout: 4–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Finishes first active Alaska MMA season unbeaten
items.detail: Medić had won three fights in 2018—two submissions and one TKO—after returning from his long gap in professional activity. All four of his career wins to this point had been finishes.

items.label: WIN · Alonzo Leisholm Jr. · Alaska FC 148
items.detail: Defeated Alonzo Leisholm Jr. by TKO (punches) at Alaska FC 148, round 1 at 2:52. Stopped a previously unbeaten local opponent in round one in the Alaska FC 148 co-main event. The actual title fight on that card was Charlie Johnson versus Jason Flowers; this victory should not be described as a championship win. Professional record after bout: 5–0.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · Alaska FC 148 event and result

items.label: Builds 5–0 record with a 100% finish rate
items.detail: Medić had four regional stoppage wins in Alaska after his debut and entered 2020 at 5–0. Two wins were by triangle choke, the others by strikes. He had yet to fight outside regional competition on a major televised MMA stage.

items.label: Contender Series booking changes opponents
items.detail: A scheduled DWCS pairing against Taylor Callens was canceled after Callens withdrew. Medić remained on the August 4 card and faced Mikey Gonzalez instead. The canceled pairing is not counted as an actual fight.

items.label: WIN · Mikey Gonzalez · DWCS Season 4, Week 1
items.detail: Defeated Mikey Gonzalez by TKO (kicks and ground strikes) at DWCS Season 4, Week 1, round 1 at 2:12. In his Contender Series appearance in Las Vegas, Medić repeatedly hurt Gonzalez with kicks and punches and forced a first-round stoppage. The official fight result and contemporary UFC recap report 2:12. He entered the UFC with a 6–0 professional record. Professional record after bout: 6–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official DWCS Week 1 fight result

items.label: Receives UFC contract after Contender Series finish
items.detail: Dana White awarded Medić a UFC contract after the Gonzalez stoppage. It was his first professional fight in the promotion's Contender Series system, but not yet an official UFC Octagon appearance; his official debut followed in March 2021.

items.label: Moves training camp to Kings MMA in California
items.detail: After signing with the UFC, Medić began training under Rafael Cordeiro at Kings MMA in Southern California, alongside experienced fighters including Beneil Dariush, Marvin Vettori, Kelvin Gastelum and Giga Chikadze. Back problems and immigration matters disrupted the initial move from Alaska before his debut camp stabilized.

items.label: Explains origin of nickname 'The Doctor'
items.detail: Medić said his manager, Nic, gave him the nickname because of the precision of his strikes and his surname, which resembles the English word 'medic.' It is a fight nickname, not a claim that he holds a medical qualification.

items.label: WIN · Aalon Cruz · UFC 259: Błachowicz vs. Adesanya
items.detail: Defeated Aalon Cruz by TKO (flying knee and ground punches) at UFC 259: Błachowicz vs. Adesanya, round 1 at 1:40. Made his official UFC debut at lightweight (155 pounds) and finished Cruz quickly. UFC record: 1–0. Earned his first UFC Performance of the Night bonus. Professional record after bout: 7–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Earns UFC debut Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: The opening-round finish over Aalon Cruz on the UFC 259 preliminary card earned Medić a performance bonus. This was his seventh consecutive professional win by stoppage; the bonus and the victory are separate timeline events, not separate fights.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete bonus history and UFC 259 result

items.label: LOSS · Jalin Turner · UFC 266: Volkanovski vs. Ortega
items.detail: Lost to Jalin Turner by rear-naked choke submission at UFC 266: Volkanovski vs. Ortega, round 1 at 4:01. Suffered his first professional loss as Turner hurt him and completed a back-take and rear-naked choke. The defeat exposed the difficulty of sustaining his attack against a larger grappling threat at lightweight. UFC record: 1–1. Professional record after bout: 7–1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: First career defeat ends 7–0 start
items.detail: The Turner submission ended a seven-fight perfect professional record, all by stoppage. Medić remained at lightweight for one more UFC fight before later moving to welterweight.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · first career loss and career chronology

items.label: WIN · Omar Morales · UFC Fight Night: Holm vs. Vieira
items.detail: Defeated Omar Morales by TKO (punches) at UFC Fight Night: Holm vs. Vieira, round 2 at 3:05. Returned from the Turner loss with a second-round stoppage of Morales in another lightweight bout. UFC record: 2–1. Professional record after bout: 8–1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Commits to welterweight after three UFC lightweight fights
items.detail: His first three official UFC bouts were contested at 155 pounds against Cruz, Turner and Morales. Medić then moved to 170 pounds, describing the lighter weight cut as increasingly difficult to manage. The Semelsberger bout in July 2023 was his first official UFC welterweight appearance.

items.label: WIN · Matthew Semelsberger · UFC 291: Poirier vs. Gaethje 2
items.detail: Defeated Matthew Semelsberger by TKO (spinning backfist and follow-up punches) at UFC 291: Poirier vs. Gaethje 2, round 3 at 2:36. Made his welterweight debut in Salt Lake City and scored a third-round stoppage with a spinning backfist and punches. It was his first professional fight to last into the third round. UFC record: 3–1. Professional record after bout: 9–1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Wins first official UFC fight at welterweight
items.detail: The Semelsberger finish marked a successful debut at 170 pounds after three lightweight UFC bouts. The late finish also showed that Medić could stop an opponent beyond his usual first-round window.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · results and welterweight debut history

items.label: LOSS · Myktybek Orolbai · UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Craig
items.detail: Lost to Myktybek Orolbai by neck crank submission at UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Craig, round 2 at 4:12. Lost his second professional fight by submission after Orolbai took over the grappling exchanges. It was his first loss at welterweight, and all his career defeats to this point had come by submission. UFC record: 3–2. Professional record after bout: 9–2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Tim Means · UFC on ESPN: Nicolau vs. Perez
items.detail: Defeated Tim Means by TKO (uppercut and punches) at UFC on ESPN: Nicolau vs. Perez, round 1 at 2:09. Stopped veteran southpaw Tim Means early in round one with a damaging uppercut and follow-up punches. The finish earned a Performance of the Night bonus. UFC record: 4–2. Professional record after bout: 10–2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Second UFC Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: Medić's quick stoppage of Tim Means earned his second UFC performance bonus, adding to the first from his UFC 259 debut against Cruz.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fighter record and bonus history

items.label: LOSS · Punahele Soriano · UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2
items.detail: Lost to Punahele Soriano by KO (punches) at UFC Fight Night: Dern vs. Ribas 2, round 1 at 0:31. Was knocked out in 31 seconds in Las Vegas, his first professional defeat by strikes. His previous two career losses were submissions. UFC record: 4–3. Professional record after bout: 10–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Rebuilds after first career knockout defeat
items.detail: The Soriano loss left Medić at 10–3, with a 4–3 UFC record, and no wins by decision. It also made his tendency toward high-risk early exchanges a career-defining feature, even while his knockout offense remained potent.

items.label: WIN · Gilbert Urbina · UFC on ESPN: Dolidze vs. Hernandez
items.detail: Defeated Gilbert Urbina by KO (straight left hand) at UFC on ESPN: Dolidze vs. Hernandez, round 1 at 1:03. Returned after the Soriano defeat with a 63-second knockout. The decisive southpaw straight left established the first win of what became a four-fight first-round finishing streak. UFC record: 5–3. Professional record after bout: 11–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: WIN · Muslim Salikhov · UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brown
items.detail: Defeated Muslim Salikhov by TKO (straight left and ground punches) at UFC Fight Night: Bonfim vs. Brown, round 1 at 1:03. Stopped the experienced kickboxer in 63 seconds, exactly the same official finish time as the Urbina bout. He was now on consecutive first-round knockouts. UFC record: 6–3. Professional record after bout: 12–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Two consecutive 63-second UFC stoppages
items.detail: The victories over Gilbert Urbina and Muslim Salikhov each ended at 1:03 of round one. This was an unusual statistical coincidence, but they were separate fights on different 2025 UFC cards.

items.label: WIN · Geoff Neal · UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Hernandez
items.detail: Defeated Geoff Neal by KO (left hook) at UFC Fight Night: Strickland vs. Hernandez, round 1 at 1:19. Stopped ranked welterweight Geoff Neal with a left hook in Houston, Texas. The 79-second win earned another Performance of the Night bonus and moved Medić into the UFC top 15 at 170 pounds. UFC record: 7–3. Professional record after bout: 13–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: Enters ranked welterweight field with Neal knockout
items.detail: The win over Geoff Neal made it three consecutive opening-round UFC knockouts and advanced Medić into the welterweight top 15. After the result, he asked to compete on a UFC show in Serbia, which the promotion later arranged.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · profile of first Serbia homecoming event

items.label: Belgrade main event against Daniel Rodriguez announced
items.detail: UFC confirmed Medić would headline its first event held in Serbia, on August 1 at Belgrade Arena. It was his first UFC five-round main-event booking and a return to his home country after nearly nine years away.

items.label: Reports meniscus injury before Belgrade main event
items.detail: Medić later said his knee shifted during a warm-up on Monday of fight week, swelled and was assessed as a meniscus injury. He said the team concealed the issue while he received treatment and completed his weight cut. These are his reported circumstances, not independently verified surgical findings.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · Aug. 2026 interview about knee injury

items.label: WIN · Daniel Rodriguez · UFC Fight Night: Medić vs. Rodriguez (Belgrade)
items.detail: Defeated Daniel Rodriguez by TKO (left-hand combination and ground strikes) at UFC Fight Night: Medić vs. Rodriguez (Belgrade), round 1 at 0:30. Headlined the UFC's inaugural event in Serbia in front of his home crowd at Belgrade Arena. Rodriguez landed an early low kick, but Medić quickly recovered, dropped him with punches and forced the stoppage after 30 seconds. This was his first UFC main-event win and fourth straight first-round stoppage. UFC record: 8–3. Professional record after bout: 14–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete dated MMA fight record

items.label: First UFC Serbia main-event winner; fourth straight knockout
items.detail: Medić became the winner of the first UFC main event staged in Serbia. His Rodriguez finish was his fourth consecutive first-round UFC knockout, and he received his fourth Performance of the Night award. It was not a completed five-round fight despite the main-event booking.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official Belgrade event bonus report

items.label: Discusses knee recovery and potential surgery
items.detail: In interviews after the Rodriguez win, Medić said he expected to need an arthroscopic procedure for the meniscus issue that had occurred during fight week. Reports described anticipated surgery, not a verified postoperative date; no completed surgery is assumed here.

items.label: UFC 334 bout against Kevin Holland announced
items.detail: Medić was booked to face Kevin Holland in a welterweight matchup at Madison Square Garden on November 14. The pairing matched his four-fight winning run with Holland's experience across two UFC divisions; the announcement is separate from a completed result.

items.label: Holds 14–3 record with no decisions
items.detail: As of October 27, 2026, all 17 of Medić's professional MMA bouts had ended by stoppage. His 14 wins comprised 12 KO/TKOs and two submissions, while three defeats came by two submissions and one knockout. He stood 8–3 in the UFC and had won four straight first-round finishes.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · full professional record and methods

items.label: UFC 334 · welterweight fight vs. Kevin Holland
items.detail: Scheduled to face Kevin Holland at Madison Square Garden in New York. As of October 27, 2026, Medić is 14–3 professionally and 8–3 inside the UFC, coming off a 30-second finish of Daniel Rodriguez. This is a future booking and no result is assigned.

Kevin Holland.name: Kevin Holland
Kevin Holland.subtitle: Career chronology · Regional MMA, UFC middleweight breakout and welterweight run

items.label: Born in Riverside, California
items.detail: Kevin Holland was born in Riverside, California. He later built his professional career out of Texas, training in the Dallas–Fort Worth area.

items.label: Age 16 — starts training (approx. 2008–09)
items.detail: Holland has said he started training at age 16 in a kung-fu gym. The date here represents an approximate early-training period, not a documented exact day.

items.label: Early amateur competition
items.detail: Wins a documented amateur decision over Richard Bailey under the PCG banner. The UFC credits him with a 4–0 amateur record, while the Sherdog profile displays three amateur bouts.

items.label: Last listed amateur appearance
items.detail: Stops William Clark in the second round of a PCG event before turning professional the following year.

items.label: WIN · Marcos Ayub · XKO 25
items.detail: Defeated Marcos Ayub by TKO (punches) at XKO 25, Round 1 at 1:54. His professional MMA debut ends with a first-round stoppage. Career record after the bout: 1–0.

items.label: WIN · Jason Perrotta · GCS 3: Hub City Havoc
items.detail: Defeated Jason Perrotta by TKO (punches) at GCS 3: Hub City Havoc, Round 1 at 1:36. A second straight first-round stoppage early in his regional career. Career record after the bout: 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Aaron Reves · Kickass Productions: Border Wars
items.detail: Defeated Aaron Reves by Submission (method unspecified) at Kickass Productions: Border Wars, Round 1 at 0:22. The third consecutive first-round finish comes in just 22 seconds. Career record after the bout: 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Victor Reyna · XKO 26
items.detail: Defeated Victor Reyna by Submission (guillotine choke) at XKO 26, Round 1 at 3:44. A guillotine gives him four stoppage wins in his first four professional bouts. Career record after the bout: 4–0.

items.label: LOSS · Ramil Mustapaev · GCS 4: Key City Chaos 2
items.detail: Lost to Ramil Mustapaev by Unanimous decision at GCS 4: Key City Chaos 2, Round 3 at 3:00. His first professional defeat, on the scorecards after three rounds. Career record after the bout: 4–1.

items.label: LOSS · Rafael Lovato Jr. · Legacy FC 46
items.detail: Lost to Rafael Lovato Jr. by Submission (rear-naked choke) at Legacy FC 46, Round 1 at 1:24. Future Bellator middleweight champion Rafael Lovato Jr. hands him his first submission loss. Career record after the bout: 4–2.

items.label: WIN · Sam Liera · KOTC: Night of Champions
items.detail: Defeated Sam Liera by TKO (punches) at KOTC: Night of Champions, Round 2 at 2:56. Returns to winning form against Liera in King of the Cage. Career record after the bout: 5–2.

items.label: WIN · Sam Liera · KOTC: Martial Law
items.detail: Defeated Sam Liera by Submission (guillotine choke) at KOTC: Martial Law, Round 2 at 4:23. Beats Liera a second time, now by guillotine in the second round. Career record after the bout: 6–2.

items.label: WIN · Jose Alfredo Leija · XKO 33
items.detail: Defeated Jose Alfredo Leija by Strikes / submission to punches at XKO 33, Round 1 at 4:03. Wins an XKO middleweight title bout; record databases differ on the exact stoppage classification. The victory secured the XKO middleweight championship. Career record after the bout: 7–2.

items.label: WIN · Geoff Neal · XKO 34
items.detail: Defeated Geoff Neal by TKO (punches) at XKO 34, Round 3 at 3:50. Stops future UFC welterweight contender Geoff Neal in round three while defending his XKO middleweight belt. Career record after the bout: 8–2.

items.label: WIN · David Gomez · KOTC: Supernova
items.detail: Defeated David Gomez by TKO (punches) at KOTC: Supernova, Round 1 at 3:34. Scores another regional stoppage, this time under the King of the Cage banner. Career record after the bout: 9–2.

items.label: LOSS · Curtis Millender · LFA 13: Millender vs. Holland
items.detail: Lost to Curtis Millender by Unanimous decision at LFA 13: Millender vs. Holland, Round 3 at 5:00. A loss in an LFA main event interrupts his regional winning streak. Career record after the bout: 9–3.

items.label: WIN · Grady Hurley · LFA 21
items.detail: Defeated Grady Hurley by TKO (knee and punches) at LFA 21, Round 1 at 1:24. Rebounds with a first-round finish in his second LFA appearance. Career record after the bout: 10–3.

items.label: WIN · Hayward Charles · XKO 39
items.detail: Defeated Hayward Charles by TKO (punches) at XKO 39, Round 3 at 3:34. Begins the year with a third-round stoppage on the regional scene. Career record after the bout: 11–3.

items.label: WIN · Teagan Dooley · Bellator 195
items.detail: Defeated Teagan Dooley by Submission (triangle choke) at Bellator 195, Round 1 at 2:59. Makes a Bellator appearance and finishes Dooley with a first-round triangle. Career record after the bout: 12–3.

items.label: WIN · Will Santiago Jr. · Dana White's Contender Series, Season 2, Week 1
items.detail: Defeated Will Santiago Jr. by Unanimous decision at Dana White's Contender Series, Season 2, Week 1, Round 3 at 5:00. Wins his Contender Series appearance but is not immediately awarded a UFC contract. Career record after the bout: 13–3.

items.label: LOSS · Thiago Santos · UFC 227
items.detail: Lost to Thiago Santos by Unanimous decision at UFC 227, Round 3 at 5:00. Accepts a UFC opportunity against Santos and loses a competitive three-round decision in his promotional debut. Career record after the bout: 13–4.

items.label: WIN · John Phillips · UFC Fight Night 141
items.detail: Defeated John Phillips by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC Fight Night 141, Round 3 at 4:05. Earns his first UFC victory with a late third-round submission. Career record after the bout: 14–4.

items.label: WIN · Gerald Meerschaert · UFC on ESPN 2
items.detail: Defeated Gerald Meerschaert by Split decision at UFC on ESPN 2, Round 3 at 5:00. Wins a close decision over an experienced middleweight grappler. Career record after the bout: 15–4.

items.label: WIN · Alessio Di Chirico · UFC Fight Night 154
items.detail: Defeated Alessio Di Chirico by Unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 154, Round 3 at 5:00. Picks up a second straight UFC decision victory. Career record after the bout: 16–4.

items.label: LOSS · Brendan Allen · UFC on ESPN 6
items.detail: Lost to Brendan Allen by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC on ESPN 6, Round 2 at 3:38. Allen ends his two-fight winning streak with a second-round submission. Career record after the bout: 16–5.

items.label: WIN · Anthony Hernandez · UFC on ESPN 8
items.detail: Defeated Anthony Hernandez by TKO (knees and punches) at UFC on ESPN 8, Round 1 at 0:39. Returns with a 39-second finish, beginning his five-win year. Career record after the bout: 17–5.

items.label: WIN · Joaquin Buckley · UFC Fight Night 174
items.detail: Defeated Joaquin Buckley by TKO (punches) at UFC Fight Night 174, Round 3 at 0:32. Stops Buckley early in the third round for his second win of 2020. Career record after the bout: 18–5.

items.label: WIN · Darren Stewart · UFC Fight Night 178
items.detail: Defeated Darren Stewart by Split decision at UFC Fight Night 178, Round 3 at 5:00. Takes a close, physical decision for his third win of the year. Career record after the bout: 19–5.

items.label: WIN · Charlie Ontiveros · UFC Fight Night 181
items.detail: Defeated Charlie Ontiveros by TKO (slam injury) at UFC Fight Night 181, Round 1 at 2:39. A takedown and slam forces the fight-ending stoppage. Career record after the bout: 20–5.

items.label: WIN · Ronaldo Souza · UFC 256
items.detail: Defeated Ronaldo Souza by KO (punches) at UFC 256, Round 1 at 1:45. Knocks Souza out with punches from the bottom position and completes five UFC wins in 2020. Career record after the bout: 21–5.

items.label: LOSS · Derek Brunson · UFC on ESPN 21
items.detail: Lost to Derek Brunson by Unanimous decision at UFC on ESPN 21, Round 5 at 5:00. Brunson uses wrestling and positional control to win Holland's first UFC main event. Career record after the bout: 21–6.

items.label: LOSS · Marvin Vettori · UFC on ABC 2
items.detail: Lost to Marvin Vettori by Unanimous decision at UFC on ABC 2, Round 5 at 5:00. Takes a second main event just 21 days later; Vettori's takedowns and control again decide the fight. This was his second UFC main event in 21 days, following the Derek Brunson fight. Career record after the bout: 21–7.

items.label: NO CONTEST · Kyle Daukaus · UFC Fight Night 193
items.detail: Fight with Kyle Daukaus ruled a no contest at UFC Fight Night 193, Round 1 at 3:43 after an accidental clash of heads. An accidental collision of heads precedes the stoppage; the result is recorded as a no contest. Career record after the bout: 21–7 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Alex Oliveira · UFC 272
items.detail: Defeated Alex Oliveira by TKO (elbows and punches) at UFC 272, Round 2 at 0:38. His UFC welterweight debut ends with a second-round finish after a difficult opening round. Career record after the bout: 22–7 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Tim Means · UFC on ESPN 37
items.detail: Defeated Tim Means by Submission (D'Arce choke) at UFC on ESPN 37, Round 2 at 1:28. Extends his run at 170 pounds by submitting Means in the second round. Career record after the bout: 23–7 (1 NC).

items.label: UFC 279 card reshuffled
items.detail: Chimaev misses weight for his original fight with Nate Diaz. Holland, originally booked against Daniel Rodriguez, is matched with Chimaev at 180 pounds the following day.

items.label: LOSS · Khamzat Chimaev · UFC 279
items.detail: Lost to Khamzat Chimaev by Submission (D'Arce choke) at UFC 279, Round 1 at 2:13. After a last-minute card reshuffle, he faces Chimaev at 180 pounds and is submitted quickly. Career record after the bout: 23–8 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Stephen Thompson · UFC on ESPN 42
items.detail: Lost to Stephen Thompson by TKO (corner stoppage) at UFC on ESPN 42, Round 4 at 5:00. A striking-led main event ends between rounds four and five after Holland breaks his right hand. Career record after the bout: 23–9 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Santiago Ponzinibbio · UFC 287
items.detail: Defeated Santiago Ponzinibbio by KO (left hook) at UFC 287, Round 3 at 3:16. Returns from the Thompson defeat to stop Ponzinibbio in the third round. Career record after the bout: 24–9 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Michael Chiesa · UFC 291
items.detail: Defeated Michael Chiesa by Submission (D'Arce choke) at UFC 291, Round 1 at 2:39. Catches a seasoned grappler with a first-round D'Arce choke. Career record after the bout: 25–9 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Jack Della Maddalena · Noche UFC / UFC Fight Night 227
items.detail: Lost to Jack Della Maddalena by Split decision at Noche UFC / UFC Fight Night 227, Round 3 at 5:00. Loses a closely scored three-round striking contest to the Australian contender. Career record after the bout: 25–10 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Michael Page · UFC 299
items.detail: Lost to Michael Page by Unanimous decision at UFC 299, Round 3 at 5:00. Page's distance management and unorthodox movement produce a decision loss for Holland. Career record after the bout: 25–11 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Michał Oleksiejczuk · UFC 302
items.detail: Defeated Michał Oleksiejczuk by Technical submission (armbar) at UFC 302, Round 1 at 1:34. Recovers from an early knockdown and attacks an armbar, forcing a quick stoppage. Career record after the bout: 26–11 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Roman Dolidze · UFC 307
items.detail: Lost to Roman Dolidze by TKO (corner stoppage due to rib injury) at UFC 307, Round 1 at 5:00. A rib injury prevents Holland from continuing after the opening round. Career record after the bout: 26–12 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Reinier de Ridder · UFC 311
items.detail: Lost to Reinier de Ridder by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC 311, Round 1 at 3:31. A return to middleweight ends in a first-round submission loss to de Ridder. Career record after the bout: 26–13 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Gunnar Nelson · UFC Fight Night 255
items.detail: Defeated Gunnar Nelson by Unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 255, Round 3 at 5:00. Back at welterweight, Holland controls enough of the contest to earn a decision win. Career record after the bout: 27–13 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Vicente Luque · UFC 316
items.detail: Defeated Vicente Luque by Submission (D'Arce choke) at UFC 316, Round 2 at 1:03. Hurts Luque in striking exchanges before securing the D'Arce choke in the second round. Career record after the bout: 28–13 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Daniel Rodriguez · UFC 318
items.detail: Lost to Daniel Rodriguez by Unanimous decision at UFC 318, Round 3 at 5:00. His two-fight winning streak ends against Rodriguez on the scorecards. Career record after the bout: 28–14 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Mike Malott · UFC Fight Night 262
items.detail: Lost to Mike Malott by Unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 262, Round 3 at 5:00. Another three-round decision defeat leaves Holland 2–3 in 2025. Career record after the bout: 28–15 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Randy Brown · UFC 327
items.detail: Defeated Randy Brown by Unanimous decision at UFC 327, Round 3 at 5:00. Nearly finishes an anaconda choke in round two and wins all three judges' scorecards, 30–27. Career record after the bout: 29–15 (1 NC).

items.label: Scheduled: Uroš Medić at UFC 334
items.detail: Holland is booked for a welterweight fight against Medić at Madison Square Garden. This is a future scheduled bout, not a result.

Stephen Thompson.name: Stephen Thompson
Stephen Thompson.subtitle: Career chronology · Undefeated kickboxing career, two UFC title shots and 27 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in South Carolina
items.detail: Stephen Randall Thompson was born February 11, 1983. He grew up around the family martial arts school in the Greenville–Simpsonville area of South Carolina.

items.label: Begins karate under his father Ray Thompson
items.detail: He began training as a small child at his family's karate school. Ray Thompson, a former fighter and longtime instructor, taught Stephen and his siblings. The school's training later became the foundation of his UFC striking style.

items.label: Starts full-contact karate training
items.detail: Thompson has said he moved into full-contact kempo training at about twelve, after years of childhood practice in the family school.

items.label: Wins first kickboxing bout against older opponent
items.detail: His father matched him with an older, more experienced kickboxer for his first competition. Thompson won, beginning the unbeaten striking record he accumulated before switching to MMA. The year is estimated from his age.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and first competition

items.label: Builds undefeated kickboxing career and wins world titles
items.detail: Thompson became a five-time world-champion kickboxer and competed in Chuck Norris's World Combat League. UFC materials list an undefeated 57–0 combined kickboxing record, with more than 40 knockouts; this is kickboxing, not part of his MMA record. Individual title dates are not consistently documented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · kickboxing record and listed titles

items.label: Serious knee injury interrupts kickboxing career
items.detail: Thompson described tearing major ligaments in his left knee during World Combat League competition and having several knee surgeries, including meniscus removal. Recovery kept him from fighting for approximately three years. Accounts vary on the exact injury year.

items.label: Shifts focus from kickboxing to professional MMA
items.detail: After knee rehabilitation, Thompson expanded his preparation toward mixed martial arts, including grappling and wrestling, and chose MMA as the next step in his fighting career. His first recorded professional MMA bout followed in February 2010.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · 2012 account of the move to MMA

items.label: Withdraws from UFC 154 because of torn meniscus
items.detail: Following the Matt Brown defeat, Thompson suffered another knee injury in training. A torn meniscus forced him out of a planned November UFC 154 bout with Besam Yousef; he underwent treatment before returning the following May.

items.label: Seven-fight UFC winning streak brings a title shot
items.detail: After his first professional defeat against Matt Brown in 2012, Thompson won seven straight UFC bouts between 2013 and June 2016, including victories over Robert Whittaker, Johny Hendricks and Rory MacDonald. The run earns him his first UFC welterweight title challenge.

items.label: First UFC welterweight championship bout
items.detail: Thompson challenged Tyron Woodley at UFC 205, the promotion's first event at Madison Square Garden. Their five-round contest ended in a majority draw and Woodley retained the title; Thompson was granted a rematch.

items.label: Second title attempt ends in majority-decision defeat
items.detail: The UFC 209 rematch was fought more cautiously than their first meeting. Woodley won a majority decision and remained welterweight champion. These are Thompson's only two UFC title fights through October 2026.

items.label: Darren Till misses weight ahead of Liverpool main event
items.detail: Till weighed 174.5 pounds, 3.5 pounds above the non-title welterweight allowance. Thompson made weight at 171 pounds, accepted the bout under revised conditions, and faced Till the next day. This is a weigh-in event, not a separate fight.

items.label: UFC 291 booking canceled after Michel Pereira misses weight
items.detail: Thompson made weight at 170.5 pounds but Pereira weighed 174 pounds, three pounds above the allowance. Thompson declined a catchweight contest, and the UFC canceled the matchup before fight night. No bout result is assigned.

items.label: Confirms UFC compensation issue from canceled fight was resolved
items.detail: After initially reporting that he had not been paid for the canceled Pereira fight, Thompson later said the payment issue had been settled with the UFC. The dispute is separate from his professional fight record.

items.label: Explains decision to take retirement fight with Charles Radtke
items.detail: Ahead of UFC 334, Thompson described wanting to give a less-established fighter the kind of opportunity older veterans had given him. He has indicated the Radtke matchup is intended to be his final UFC appearance; the fight has not yet taken place.

items.label: UFC 334 · welterweight bout vs. Charles Radtke
items.detail: Thompson is scheduled to face Charles Radtke at Madison Square Garden in New York City. He enters the booking 17–9–1 professionally and 12–9–1 in the UFC. The bout has been described as his planned retirement fight; no result is recorded.

items.label: WIN · Jeremy Joles · Fight Party: Greenville Kage Fighting
items.detail: Defeated Jeremy Joles by TKO (punches) at Fight Party: Greenville Kage Fighting, Round 2 (3:40). Professional MMA debut. Thompson brings his undefeated kickboxing background into MMA at age 26. Professional MMA record afterward: 1–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Danny Finz · Fight Party: Xtreme Cage Fighting 2
items.detail: Defeated Danny Finz by TKO (punches) at Fight Party: Xtreme Cage Fighting 2, Round 1 (3:45). Second professional MMA win and first-round finish. Professional MMA record afterward: 2–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Marques Worrell · Fight Party: Greenville Kage Fighting
items.detail: Defeated Marques Worrell by Submission (rear-naked choke) at Fight Party: Greenville Kage Fighting, Round 2 (3:08). His first and, through October 2026, only professional MMA submission victory. Professional MMA record afterward: 3–0–0.

items.label: WIN · William Kuhn · XC: Xtreme Chaos 2
items.detail: Defeated William Kuhn by Decision (unanimous) at XC: Xtreme Chaos 2, Round 3 (5:00). Goes three rounds for his first professional MMA decision victory. Professional MMA record afterward: 4–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Patrick Mandio · Fight Party: Masquerade Fight Party
items.detail: Defeated Patrick Mandio by Decision (unanimous) at Fight Party: Masquerade Fight Party, Round 3 (5:00). Completes an undefeated 5–0 regional run before signing with the UFC. Professional MMA record afterward: 5–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Daniel Stittgen · UFC 143
items.detail: Defeated Daniel Stittgen by KO (head kick) at UFC 143, Round 1 (4:13). UFC debut. The head-kick knockout earned a Knockout of the Night bonus. Professional MMA record afterward: 6–0–0.

items.label: LOSS · Matt Brown · UFC 145
items.detail: Lost to Matt Brown by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 145, Round 3 (5:00). First professional MMA defeat. Brown closes distance, imposes clinch and wrestling pressure, and wins all three rounds on the scorecards. Professional MMA record afterward: 6–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Nah-Shon Burrell · UFC 160
items.detail: Defeated Nah-Shon Burrell by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 160, Round 3 (5:00). Returns from an injury-related layoff and begins a seven-fight UFC winning streak. Professional MMA record afterward: 7–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Chris Clements · UFC 165
items.detail: Defeated Chris Clements by TKO (punches) at UFC 165, Round 2 (1:27). Finishes Clements with strikes in Toronto for his second consecutive UFC win. Professional MMA record afterward: 8–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Robert Whittaker · UFC 170
items.detail: Defeated Robert Whittaker by TKO (punches) at UFC 170, Round 1 (3:43). Stops Whittaker in the opening round, an important early win over a future UFC middleweight champion. Professional MMA record afterward: 9–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Patrick Côté · UFC 178
items.detail: Defeated Patrick Côté by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 178, Round 3 (5:00). Beats the experienced Canadian veteran over three rounds in Las Vegas. Professional MMA record afterward: 10–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Jake Ellenberger · The Ultimate Fighter 21 Finale
items.detail: Defeated Jake Ellenberger by KO (spinning hook kick) at The Ultimate Fighter 21 Finale, Round 1 (4:29). After surviving an early knockdown, Thompson finishes Ellenberger with spinning kicks and wins a Performance of the Night bonus. Professional MMA record afterward: 11–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Johny Hendricks · UFC Fight Night 82
items.detail: Defeated Johny Hendricks by TKO (punches) at UFC Fight Night 82, Round 1 (3:31). Stops former UFC welterweight champion Hendricks in the first round, establishing himself as an immediate title contender. Professional MMA record afterward: 12–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Rory MacDonald · UFC Fight Night 89
items.detail: Defeated Rory MacDonald by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night 89, Round 5 (5:00). Wins his first five-round UFC main event, extending his UFC winning streak to seven and securing a title opportunity. Professional MMA record afterward: 13–1–0.

items.label: DRAW · Tyron Woodley · UFC 205
items.detail: Fought Tyron Woodley to a majority draw at UFC 205, five rounds (5:00 of Round 5). First UFC welterweight championship challenge at Madison Square Garden. An eventful fourth round helps define a close fight, which ends in a majority draw; Woodley retains the title. Professional MMA record afterward: 13–1–1.

items.label: LOSS · Tyron Woodley · UFC 209
items.detail: Lost to Tyron Woodley by Decision (majority) at UFC 209, Round 5 (5:00). Second consecutive UFC title challenge. The tactical rematch goes the distance; Woodley keeps the belt on a majority decision. Professional MMA record afterward: 13–2–1.

items.label: WIN · Jorge Masvidal · UFC 217
items.detail: Defeated Jorge Masvidal by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 217, Round 3 (5:00). Rebounds from the Woodley rematch with a clear three-round striking victory over Masvidal at Madison Square Garden. Professional MMA record afterward: 14–2–1.

items.label: LOSS · Darren Till · UFC Fight Night 130
items.detail: Lost to Darren Till by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night 130, Round 5 (5:00). Liverpool main event. Till weighed 174.5 pounds, 3.5 pounds over the non-title welterweight allowance, but the fight went ahead. Till won on all three scorecards. Professional MMA record afterward: 14–3–1.

items.label: LOSS · Anthony Pettis · UFC Fight Night 148
items.detail: Lost to Anthony Pettis by KO (punches) at UFC Fight Night 148, Round 2 (4:55). Suffers the first knockout defeat of his professional MMA career after Pettis lands a late second-round superman punch. Professional MMA record afterward: 14–4–1.

items.label: WIN · Vicente Luque · UFC 244
items.detail: Defeated Vicente Luque by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 244, Round 3 (5:00). Returns to winning form against a powerful pressure fighter in a bout that earns Fight of the Night. Professional MMA record afterward: 15–4–1.

items.label: WIN · Geoff Neal · UFC Fight Night 183
items.detail: Defeated Geoff Neal by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night 183, Round 5 (5:00). Wins a five-round main event against Neal, using movement, straight punches and consistent volume. Professional MMA record afterward: 16–4–1.

items.label: LOSS · Gilbert Burns · UFC 264
items.detail: Lost to Gilbert Burns by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 264, Round 3 (5:00). Burns uses grappling and control to disrupt Thompson's preferred distance and take a decision. Professional MMA record afterward: 16–5–1.

items.label: LOSS · Belal Muhammad · UFC Fight Night 199
items.detail: Lost to Belal Muhammad by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night 199, Round 3 (5:00). Another three-round defeat driven by an opponent's wrestling pressure and positional control. Professional MMA record afterward: 16–6–1.

items.label: WIN · Kevin Holland · UFC on ESPN 42: Thompson vs. Holland
items.detail: Defeated Kevin Holland by TKO (corner stoppage) at UFC on ESPN 42: Thompson vs. Holland, Round 4 (5:00). Wins a striking-heavy main event in Orlando; Holland's corner stops the contest before the fifth round due to injuries. Earns Fight of the Night. Professional MMA record afterward: 17–6–1.

items.label: LOSS · Shavkat Rakhmonov · UFC 296
items.detail: Lost to Shavkat Rakhmonov by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC 296, Round 2 (4:56). Suffers his first MMA submission defeat after Rakhmonov works to the back late in round two. Professional MMA record afterward: 17–7–1.

items.label: LOSS · Joaquin Buckley · UFC 307
items.detail: Lost to Joaquin Buckley by KO (punch) at UFC 307, Round 3 (2:17). Buckley knocks him out in the third round in Salt Lake City. Professional MMA record afterward: 17–8–1.

items.label: LOSS · Gabriel Bonfim · UFC on ESPN 70: Lewis vs. Teixeira
items.detail: Lost to Gabriel Bonfim by Decision (split) at UFC on ESPN 70: Lewis vs. Teixeira, Round 3 (5:00). Loses a closely contested split decision in Nashville. The result marks his third consecutive defeat. Professional MMA record afterward: 17–9–1.

Charles Radtke.name: Charles Radtke
Charles Radtke.subtitle: Career chronology · Wisconsin bison ranch, Cage Fury welterweight title and UFC run

items.label: Born in Illinois
items.detail: Charles William Radtke was born July 9, 1990, in Illinois. He later represented the Chicago area and Salem, Wisconsin, while building his professional MMA career.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · birth date and fighter background

items.label: Grows up working on a Wisconsin bison ranch
items.detail: From around age nine or ten, Radtke worked on his grandfather's Wisconsin bison ranch, eventually becoming a co-owner. Ranch work remained his principal occupation before his full-time transition into MMA.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · 2023 athlete interview about family and ranch

items.label: Builds an 8–1 amateur MMA record
items.detail: Radtke's UFC fighter questionnaire credits him with eight wins and one loss as an amateur before the professional career that began in November 2012. The promotion does not supply the complete amateur bout dates in that profile.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and amateur background

items.label: Competes intermittently while working on the ranch
items.detail: After making his professional debut in November 2012, Radtke did not log a second professional fight until March 2017. During his early fighting years, ranch work continued to be a major commitment.

items.label: Leaves bison ranching to pursue MMA full time
items.detail: Radtke told the UFC he chose to leave the family bison ranch at about age 31, with his grandfather's encouragement, and move to Florida to pursue MMA at a higher level. He later joined Cage Fury Fighting Championships.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · interview on full-time career decision

items.label: Rises through Cage Fury Fighting Championships
items.detail: Consecutive CFFC victories over Jonathan Piersma and Caleb Crump in 2022 help set up an April 2023 championship opportunity against Raheam Forest. His sequence of CFFC wins builds the case for a UFC contract.

items.label: Wins Cage Fury welterweight championship
items.detail: Radtke challenges unbeaten champion Raheam Forest at CFFC 118 in Philadelphia. He survives a difficult start, secures a rear-naked choke at 4:20 of the opening round and leaves with the CFFC welterweight belt.

items.label: Earns Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt
items.detail: In his UFC debut-year questionnaire, Radtke identified himself as a Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt. His exact promotion date was not listed, so this entry is dated only to when the ranking was documented.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A on martial arts ranks

items.label: Apologizes for offensive post-fight remarks at UFC 293
items.detail: Following his UFC debut win over Mike Mathetha, Radtke directed a homophobic slur at the crowd during the broadcast interview. He publicly apologized afterward and said the language did not reflect who he was. This incident is distinct from the bout result.

items.label: Receives UFC Performance of the Night bonus
items.detail: The first-round stoppage of Matthew Semelsberger takes just 51 seconds and earns Radtke a Performance of the Night award, his first reported UFC post-fight performance bonus.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · UFC post-fight bonus and result

items.label: Beats Francisco Prado to extend win streak
items.detail: After submitting Daniel Frunza in November 2025, Radtke controls Francisco Prado for a unanimous decision at UFC 327. The wins put him on a two-fight streak before his next scheduled appearance.

items.label: UFC 334 · Stephen Thompson at Madison Square Garden
items.detail: Radtke is booked to face Stephen Thompson in a welterweight bout at UFC 334 in New York City. The event is being billed as Thompson's planned retirement fight, not Radtke's. No result has been assigned.

items.label: WIN · Jimmy Kim · XFO 46
items.detail: Defeated Jimmy Kim by Submission (triangle choke) at XFO 46, Round 1 (2:07). Wins his professional MMA debut by triangle choke in the first round. Professional record after the bout: 1–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Jeffery Pelton · IT Fight Series 72
items.detail: Defeated Jeffery Pelton by TKO (strikes) at IT Fight Series 72, Round 2 (2:23). Returns to professional MMA after more than four years between recorded bouts and earns his second stoppage win. Professional record after the bout: 2–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: LOSS · Austin Hubbard · Caged Aggression 21
items.detail: Lost to Austin Hubbard by Unanimous decision at Caged Aggression 21, Round 3 (5:00). First professional loss, against a fighter who would later join the UFC. Professional record after the bout: 2–1.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: LOSS · Chris Gonzalez · Bellator 221
items.detail: Lost to Chris Gonzalez by Unanimous decision at Bellator 221, Round 3 (5:00). Makes a Bellator appearance in Rosemont, Illinois, losing a three-round decision and moving to 2–2. Professional record after the bout: 2–2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Geralbert Castillo · XMMA 1
items.detail: Defeated Geralbert Castillo by Unanimous decision at XMMA 1, Round 3 (5:00). Returns to competition after a gap since his Bellator appearance and earns his first professional decision win. Professional record after the bout: 3–2.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: LOSS · Justin Montalvo · Triton Fights 18
items.detail: Lost to Justin Montalvo by TKO (strikes) at Triton Fights 18, Round 2 (4:55). His third professional loss comes late in the second round. Professional record after the bout: 3–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Brandon Lopez · CFFC 100
items.detail: Defeated Brandon Lopez by TKO (punch) at CFFC 100, Round 2 (3:31). Wins his first fight under the Cage Fury banner, starting a four-fight CFFC winning run. Professional record after the bout: 4–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Jonathan Piersma · CFFC 106
items.detail: Defeated Jonathan Piersma by Split decision at CFFC 106, Round 3 (5:00). Edges previously unbeaten Piersma by split decision at CFFC 106. Professional record after the bout: 5–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Caleb Crump · CFFC 110
items.detail: Defeated Caleb Crump by TKO (strikes) at CFFC 110, Round 1 (1:48). Stops Crump in the opening round, extending his winning streak to three. Professional record after the bout: 6–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Raheam Forest · CFFC 118
items.detail: Defeated Raheam Forest by Submission (rear-naked choke) at CFFC 118, Round 1 (4:20). Faces the undefeated reigning Cage Fury welterweight champion in Philadelphia. After adversity early, takes Forest's back and submits him in round one to win the CFFC welterweight championship. Professional record after the bout: 7–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Mike Mathetha · UFC 293
items.detail: Defeated Mike Mathetha by Unanimous decision at UFC 293, Round 3 (5:00). UFC debut in Sydney, Australia against Mike Mathetha, known as Blood Diamond. Uses wrestling and control to secure a decision, with his opponent docked a point for repeated illegal groin strikes. Professional record after the bout: 8–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Gilbert Urbina · UFC Fight Night: Dolidze vs. Imavov
items.detail: Defeated Gilbert Urbina by TKO (left hook) at UFC Fight Night: Dolidze vs. Imavov, Round 1 (4:47). Stops Urbina late in the first round, marking his first UFC win by knockout. Professional record after the bout: 9–3.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: LOSS · Carlos Prates · UFC on ESPN: Cannonier vs. Imavov
items.detail: Lost to Carlos Prates by TKO (knee to the body) at UFC on ESPN: Cannonier vs. Imavov, Round 1 (4:47). Suffers his first UFC defeat when Prates ends the fight with a knee to the body late in round one. Professional record after the bout: 9–4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Matthew Semelsberger · UFC Fight Night: Magny vs. Prates
items.detail: Defeated Matthew Semelsberger by TKO (punches) at UFC Fight Night: Magny vs. Prates, Round 1 (0:51). Scores a 51-second first-round stoppage and earns a UFC Performance of the Night bonus. Professional record after the bout: 10–4.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: LOSS · Mike Malott · UFC 315
items.detail: Lost to Mike Malott by TKO (left hook and ground punches) at UFC 315, Round 2 (0:26). After the first round in Montreal, Malott finishes him with strikes just 26 seconds into the second. Professional record after the bout: 10–5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Daniel Frunza · UFC Fight Night: Garcia vs. Onama
items.detail: Defeated Daniel Frunza by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC Fight Night: Garcia vs. Onama, Round 3 (4:29). Controls large portions of the fight with grappling before locking in a rear-naked choke near the end of round three. Professional record after the bout: 11–5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

items.label: WIN · Francisco Prado · UFC 327
items.detail: Defeated Francisco Prado by Unanimous decision at UFC 327, Round 3 (5:00). Wins three clear rounds in Miami, heavily using takedowns and top control. Moves to 12–5 with his second consecutive win. Professional record after the bout: 12–5.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · complete professional record and result

Drew Dober.name: Drew Dober
Drew Dober.subtitle: Career chronology · National amateur Muay Thai champion and UFC lightweight knockout record holder

items.label: Born in Omaha, Nebraska
items.detail: Andrew Martin Dober was born and grew up in Omaha before becoming associated with Denver, Colorado during his professional career.

items.label: Starts Muay Thai training
items.detail: After watching UFC, Dober started training Muay Thai at age fourteen. The year is estimated from his age, not an exact documented date.

items.label: Becomes two-time national amateur Muay Thai champion
items.detail: Dober won two amateur national Muay Thai titles before turning professional in MMA. Available biographies do not firmly establish their individual dates or events.

items.label: Wrestles for Millard North High School
items.detail: He wrestled during his junior and senior years at Millard North High School in the Omaha area, adding scholastic wrestling to his striking training.

items.label: Records a 9–0 amateur MMA career
items.detail: The UFC credits Dober with a nine-win, undefeated amateur MMA career before his July 2009 professional debut. Amateur contests are not included in his 45 professional bouts.

items.label: Amateur win at Strikeforce: Payback
items.detail: Knocks out Lumumba Sayers in 16 seconds in a fight Sherdog classifies as amateur. UFC biographies also list the bout, but it does not count in his professional record.

items.label: Competes in The Ultimate Fighter 15 elimination phase
items.detail: Dober loses a one-round elimination decision to Daron Cruickshank. This was a professional exhibition bout rather than a fight counting toward his official professional record.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · original TUF 15 elimination results

items.label: Holds Denver PFC lightweight championship
items.detail: Dober lists the Denver Professional Fighting Championships lightweight title among his regional career accomplishments; the exact championship-winning fight is not independently established.

items.label: Develops Denver training base with Elevation and Easton
items.detail: Dober builds his Denver training base through Elevation Fight Team and Easton Training Center, including Brazilian jiu-jitsu under Elliot Marshall. The exact first day of the affiliation is not established.
items.sourceLabel: Drew Dober · gym and team background

items.label: Leandro Silva stoppage officially overturned
items.detail: Brazilian commission CABMMA overturns the premature March 21 referee stoppage to a no contest. Dober had not submitted during Leandro Silva's guillotine attempt.

items.label: Claims UFC lightweight knockout record with nine
items.detail: The first-round finish over Ricky Glenn takes Dober to nine KO/TKO victories at UFC lightweight, breaking the division's existing record and earning Performance of the Night.

items.label: Extends UFC lightweight KO record to eleven
items.detail: Knocks out Michael Johnson at UFC 326, setting the division's knockout record at eleven. His previous fight against Kyle Prepolec in 2025 had moved the mark to ten.

items.label: UFC 334 · lightweight fight vs. Chris Duncan
items.detail: Booked to face Chris Duncan at Madison Square Garden in New York City at UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit. Dober enters 29–15–0 with one no contest and two consecutive victories. This is a future booking; no result assigned.

items.label: WIN · Frank Caraballo · VFC 28: Throwdown
items.detail: Defeated Frank Caraballo at VFC 28: Throwdown. TKO (punches), Round 2 (3:58). Pro MMA debut at Victory Fighting Championship. Professional record afterward: 1–0–0.

items.label: LOSS · Chase Hackett · Fight to Win: Featherweight Grand Prix Final Round
items.detail: Lost to Chase Hackett at Fight to Win: Featherweight Grand Prix Final Round. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). First professional defeat. Professional record afterward: 1–1–0.

items.label: LOSS · Brandon Girtz · VFC 29: The Rising
items.detail: Lost to Brandon Girtz at VFC 29: The Rising. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Regional matchup with future Bellator veteran. Professional record afterward: 1–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Nick Nolte · Bellator 16
items.detail: Defeated Nick Nolte at Bellator 16. Submission (arm-triangle choke), Round 1 (4:45). Debuts in Bellator and earns his first professional submission. Professional record afterward: 2–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Jimmy Seipel · VFC 32: Dober vs. Seipel 2
items.detail: Defeated Jimmy Seipel at VFC 32: Dober vs. Seipel 2. TKO (submission to punches and elbows), Round 2 (3:16). A professional rematch of a previous amateur pairing. Professional record afterward: 3–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Steve Simmons · Fight to Win: The Professionals
items.detail: Defeated Steve Simmons at Fight to Win: The Professionals. TKO (submission to punches), Round 3 (1:37). Finishes after extended ground-and-pound. Professional record afterward: 4–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Kody Frank · VFC 33
items.detail: Defeated Kody Frank at VFC 33. TKO (punches), Round 2 (3:44). Fourth straight professional win. Professional record afterward: 5–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Bobby Cooper · Titan FC 16
items.detail: Defeated Bobby Cooper at Titan FC 16. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Titan FC appearance. Professional record afterward: 6–2–0.

items.label: LOSS · Ramiro Hernandez · VFC 34
items.detail: Lost to Ramiro Hernandez at VFC 34. KO (punches), Round 1 (2:29). First professional knockout loss. Professional record afterward: 6–3–0.

items.label: WIN · Sam Jackson · VFC 35
items.detail: Defeated Sam Jackson at VFC 35. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Rebounds with a decision victory. Professional record afterward: 7–3–0.

items.label: WIN · Jordan Johnson · Disorderly Conduct 4: Turf War
items.detail: Defeated Jordan Johnson at Disorderly Conduct 4: Turf War. TKO (submission to punches), Round 2 (0:30). Ground strikes force the stoppage. Professional record afterward: 8–3–0.

items.label: WIN · Ted Worthington · VFC 37
items.detail: Defeated Ted Worthington at VFC 37. TKO (retirement), Round 3 (1:36). Opponent cannot continue in the third round. Professional record afterward: 9–3–0.

items.label: LOSS · Will Brooks · Disorderly Conduct 10
items.detail: Lost to Will Brooks at Disorderly Conduct 10. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Defeated by future Bellator lightweight champion Will Brooks. Professional record afterward: 9–4–0.

items.label: WIN · Robert Rojas Jr. · VFC 38
items.detail: Defeated Robert Rojas Jr. at VFC 38. Submission (rear-naked choke), Round 1 (3:29). Begins five-fight professional winning streak. Professional record afterward: 10–4–0.

items.label: WIN · Sean Wilson · Disorderly Conduct 15: Resolution
items.detail: Defeated Sean Wilson at Disorderly Conduct 15: Resolution. Submission (rear-naked choke), Round 1 (4:58). Choke finish near the end of the first round. Professional record afterward: 11–4–0.

items.label: WIN · Aaron Derrow · Centurion Fights 1
items.detail: Defeated Aaron Derrow at Centurion Fights 1. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Completes three rounds in St. Joseph, Missouri. Professional record afterward: 12–4–0.

items.label: WIN · T.J. O'Brien · VFC 40
items.detail: Defeated T.J. O'Brien at VFC 40. Submission (rear-naked choke), Round 2 (3:57). Fourth consecutive victory heading toward the UFC. Professional record afterward: 13–4–0.

items.label: WIN · Tony Sims · Fight to Win: Prize FC 4
items.detail: Defeated Tony Sims at Fight to Win: Prize FC 4. Decision (split), Round 3 (5:00). Completes a 14–4 pre-UFC professional record. Professional record afterward: 14–4–0.

items.label: LOSS · Sean Spencer · The Ultimate Fighter 18 Finale
items.detail: Lost to Sean Spencer at The Ultimate Fighter 18 Finale. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). UFC debut at welterweight. Professional record afterward: 14–5–0.

items.label: LOSS · Nick Hein · UFC Fight Night 41: Muñoz vs. Mousasi
items.detail: Lost to Nick Hein at UFC Fight Night 41: Muñoz vs. Mousasi. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Loses on the UFC's Berlin card. Professional record afterward: 14–6–0.

items.label: WIN · Jamie Varner · UFC on Fox 13: dos Santos vs. Miocic
items.detail: Defeated Jamie Varner at UFC on Fox 13: dos Santos vs. Miocic. Submission (rear-naked choke), Round 1 (1:52). Submits former WEC lightweight champion for first UFC victory. Professional record afterward: 15–6–0.

items.label: NO CONTEST · Leandro Silva · UFC Fight Night 62: Maia vs. LaFlare
items.detail: Faced Leandro Silva at UFC Fight Night 62: Maia vs. LaFlare. No contest (overturned stoppage), Round 2 (2:45).
