Referee initially awarded Silva a guillotine submission; Brazil's commission overturned the premature stoppage to a no contest on March 26, 2015. Professional record afterward: 15–6–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Efrain Escudero · UFC 188: Velasquez vs. Werdum
items.detail: Lost to Efrain Escudero at UFC 188: Velasquez vs. Werdum. Submission (guillotine choke), Round 1 (0:54). Loses to former Ultimate Fighter winner. Professional record afterward: 15–7–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Scott Holtzman · UFC 195: Lawler vs. Condit
items.detail: Defeated Scott Holtzman at UFC 195: Lawler vs. Condit. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Returns to winning form. Professional record afterward: 16–7–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Jason Gonzalez · UFC 203: Miocic vs. Overeem
items.detail: Defeated Jason Gonzalez at UFC 203: Miocic vs. Overeem. KO (punches), Round 1 (1:45). First UFC lightweight knockout victory. Professional record afterward: 17–7–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Olivier Aubin-Mercier · UFC 206: Holloway vs. Pettis
items.detail: Lost to Olivier Aubin-Mercier at UFC 206: Holloway vs. Pettis. Submission (rear-naked choke), Round 2 (2:57). Submitted in the second round in Toronto. Professional record afterward: 17–8–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Joshua Burkman · UFC 214: Cormier vs. Jones 2
items.detail: Defeated Joshua Burkman at UFC 214: Cormier vs. Jones 2. KO (punch), Round 1 (3:04). Starts a three-fight UFC winning streak. Professional record afterward: 18–8–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Frank Camacho · UFC on Fox 27: Jacaré vs. Brunson 2
items.detail: Defeated Frank Camacho at UFC on Fox 27: Jacaré vs. Brunson 2. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). High-volume contest earns Fight of the Night. Professional record afterward: 19–8–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Jon Tuck · UFC Fight Night 135: Gaethje vs. Vick
items.detail: Defeated Jon Tuck at UFC Fight Night 135: Gaethje vs. Vick. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Latest victory by judges' decision through October 2026. Professional record afterward: 20–8–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Beneil Dariush · UFC Fight Night 146: Lewis vs. dos Santos
items.detail: Lost to Beneil Dariush at UFC Fight Night 146: Lewis vs. dos Santos. Submission (armbar), Round 2 (4:41). Hurts Dariush early but is caught by a submission. Professional record afterward: 20–9–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Marco Polo Reyes · UFC on ESPN 3: Ngannou vs. dos Santos
items.detail: Defeated Marco Polo Reyes at UFC on ESPN 3: Ngannou vs. dos Santos. TKO (punches), Round 1 (1:07). 67-second stoppage starts a three-fight knockout streak. Professional record afterward: 21–9–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Nasrat Haqparast · UFC 246: McGregor vs. Cerrone
items.detail: Defeated Nasrat Haqparast at UFC 246: McGregor vs. Cerrone. KO (punches), Round 1 (1:10). 70-second finish and Performance of the Night award. Professional record afterward: 22–9–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Alexander Hernandez · UFC Fight Night 171: Smith vs. Teixeira
items.detail: Defeated Alexander Hernandez at UFC Fight Night 171: Smith vs. Teixeira. TKO (punches), Round 2 (4:25). Earns Performance of the Night for late second-round stoppage. Professional record afterward: 23–9–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Islam Makhachev · UFC 259: Błachowicz vs. Adesanya
items.detail: Lost to Islam Makhachev at UFC 259: Błachowicz vs. Adesanya. Submission (arm-triangle choke), Round 3 (1:37). Makhachev's grappling control leads to the third-round submission. Professional record afterward: 23–10–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Brad Riddell · UFC 263: Adesanya vs. Vettori 2
items.detail: Lost to Brad Riddell at UFC 263: Adesanya vs. Vettori 2. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Competitive striking contest earns Fight of the Night. Professional record afterward: 23–11–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Terrance McKinney · UFC Fight Night 203: Santos vs. Ankalaev
items.detail: Defeated Terrance McKinney at UFC Fight Night 203: Santos vs. Ankalaev. TKO (knee and punches), Round 1 (3:17). Survives an early knockdown and turns the fight around for a first-round stoppage. Professional record afterward: 24–11–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Rafael Alves · UFC 277: Peña vs. Nunes 2
items.detail: Defeated Rafael Alves at UFC 277: Peña vs. Nunes 2. KO (body punch), Round 3 (1:30). Third-round body-punch knockout earns Performance of the Night. Professional record afterward: 25–11–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Bobby Green · UFC Fight Night 216: Cannonier vs. Strickland
items.detail: Defeated Bobby Green at UFC Fight Night 216: Cannonier vs. Strickland. KO (punch), Round 2 (2:45). Recovers from a difficult opening round and scores a comeback knockout; wins Fight of the Night. Professional record afterward: 26–11–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Matt Frevola · UFC 288: Sterling vs. Cejudo
items.detail: Lost to Matt Frevola at UFC 288: Sterling vs. Cejudo. TKO (punches), Round 1 (4:08). First-round stoppage defeat. Professional record afterward: 26–12–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Ricky Glenn · UFC Fight Night 229: Dawson vs. Green
items.detail: Defeated Ricky Glenn at UFC Fight Night 229: Dawson vs. Green. TKO (punches), Round 1 (2:36). Sets UFC lightweight knockout record at nine and earns Performance of the Night. Professional record afterward: 27–12–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Renato Carneiro · UFC Fight Night 235: Dolidze vs. Imavov
items.detail: Lost to Renato Carneiro at UFC Fight Night 235: Dolidze vs. Imavov. Decision (unanimous), Round 3 (5:00). Carneiro's positional grappling leads to a three-round decision. Professional record afterward: 27–13–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Jean Silva · UFC on ESPN 59: Namajunas vs. Cortez
items.detail: Lost to Jean Silva at UFC on ESPN 59: Namajunas vs. Cortez. TKO (doctor stoppage), Round 3 (1:28). Cut near the eye prompts a doctor's stoppage in the third round; bout earns Fight of the Night. Professional record afterward: 27–14–0 (1 NC).

items.label: LOSS · Manuel Torres · UFC on ESPN 64: Moreno vs. Erceg
items.detail: Lost to Manuel Torres at UFC on ESPN 64: Moreno vs. Erceg. TKO (punches), Round 1 (1:45). Loses in Mexico City by first-round stoppage. Professional record afterward: 27–15–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Kyle Prepolec · UFC Fight Night 262: de Ridder vs. Allen
items.detail: Defeated Kyle Prepolec at UFC Fight Night 262: de Ridder vs. Allen. TKO (knees and punches), Round 3 (1:16). Ends three-fight losing streak in Vancouver; wins Fight of the Night. Professional record afterward: 28–15–0 (1 NC).

items.label: WIN · Michael Johnson · UFC 326: Holloway vs. Oliveira 2
items.detail: Defeated Michael Johnson at UFC 326: Holloway vs. Oliveira 2. KO (punch), Round 2 (1:53). Extends UFC lightweight knockout record to 11 and earns Performance of the Night. Professional record afterward: 29–15–0 (1 NC).

Chris Duncan.name: Chris Duncan
Chris Duncan.subtitle: Career chronology · Scottish amateur titles, Bellator, UFL championship and UFC lightweight run

items.label: Born in Glasgow, Scotland
items.detail: Chris Duncan was born in Glasgow, Scotland, and grew up with ties to the Stirlingshire and Highland communities. He later represented Scotland throughout his MMA career.

items.label: Earns an HNC in agriculture and works as a shepherd
items.detail: Before pursuing fighting, Duncan earned a Higher National Certificate in agriculture and worked for roughly four years as a shepherd in the Scottish Highlands, including Glen Lyon in Perthshire. He described the isolated work as an experience that taught self-sufficiency and discipline.

items.label: Begins MMA training and amateur competition
items.detail: Duncan began MMA in 2014. During preparation for his first amateur appearance, his mother Elaine died; he continued with the bout and later described her death as a major reason he took his fighting ambitions seriously.
items.sourceLabel: BBC Sport · first amateur fight and family background

items.label: Builds a 10–2 amateur record and wins regional belts
items.detail: His UFC athlete biography credits him with a 10–2 amateur MMA record and championship honors under the On Top, Forza and Headhunters banners. Those amateur contests are separate from his 18 professional fights.

items.label: Leaves shepherding behind for full-time combat sports
items.detail: After four years as a shepherd, Duncan moved into part-time construction work and gym work before concentrating on training and coaching. His first documented professional MMA bout followed on April 7, 2018.

items.label: Becomes inaugural Ultimate Fight League lightweight champion
items.detail: Duncan's head-kick knockout of Leandro Souza at UFL 3 earned the inaugural lightweight title in Musselburgh. Souza entered on a seven-fight winning streak; the knockout was the first loss of his career in more than five years.

items.label: Completes undefeated 7–0 start with three Bellator wins
items.detail: Victories over Sam Slater, Mateusz Piskorz and Iamik Furtado made Duncan 3–0 in Bellator and 7–0 as a professional. This streak led toward his first Dana White's Contender Series opportunity in 2021.

items.label: Regroups after first Contender Series defeat
items.detail: After Viacheslav Borshchev knocked him out in October 2021, Duncan returned to regional competition and beat Jonathan Carlos in February 2022. Seven months later, he knocked out Charlie Campbell at his second Contender Series appearance and earned his UFC contract.

items.label: Moves his training to American Top Team in Florida
items.detail: Duncan shifted his training base from Scotland to American Top Team in Coconut Creek, Florida. He credited Scottish UFC veteran Robert Whiteford for helping connect him with the gym and its coaching and sparring structure. The exact relocation date is not firmly established.

items.label: Wins first UFC performance bonus
items.detail: His first-round guillotine of Bolaji Oki in Paris earned Performance of the Night. The finish was his first UFC submission win.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official fight results and bonuses

items.label: Fight of the Night against Mateusz Rębecki
items.detail: Duncan and Rębecki traded heavy shots through all three rounds in Las Vegas. Duncan won a unanimous decision, and both fighters collected Fight of the Night bonuses.

items.label: Reaches four straight UFC victories
items.detail: The submission of Terrance McKinney at UFC 323 concluded a four-fight run over Bolaji Oki, Jordan Vucenic, Mateusz Rębecki and McKinney, placing Duncan at 6–1 inside the UFC heading into his first main event.

items.label: Makes first UFC main-event appearance
items.detail: Duncan headlined a UFC Fight Night against Renato Moicano at the Meta Apex in Las Vegas. Moicano submitted him in the second round, ending the four-fight winning streak.

items.label: UFC 334 · lightweight matchup vs. Drew Dober
items.detail: Duncan is scheduled to face Drew Dober at Madison Square Garden in New York City on November 14, 2026. His most recent completed result is the April defeat to Renato Moicano; he enters the booking with a 15–3 professional record and a 6–2 UFC record. This is a future bout, not a result.

items.label: WIN · Pietro Colonna · Unity Fighting Championship
items.detail: Defeated Pietro Colonna by Submission (guillotine choke) at Unity Fighting Championship, Round 2 (4:47). Professional MMA debut after competing on Scotland's amateur circuit. Professional MMA record after the fight: 1–0.

items.label: WIN · Steven Moore · On Top: Showdown
items.detail: Defeated Steven Moore by TKO (punches) at On Top: Showdown, Round 3 (exact stoppage time unconfirmed). Second professional victory. The database reports the finish at the start of round three without a reliable stoppage time. Professional MMA record after the fight: 2–0.

items.label: WIN · Niall Smith · On Top 21
items.detail: Defeated Niall Smith by TKO at On Top 21, Round 1 (exact stoppage time unconfirmed). Third consecutive professional victory; the exact stoppage time is not confirmed in the available record. Professional MMA record after the fight: 3–0.

items.label: WIN · Sam Slater · Bellator 217: Gallagher vs. Graham
items.detail: Defeated Sam Slater by TKO (punches) at Bellator 217: Gallagher vs. Graham, Round 1 (3:00). First Bellator appearance; earns a first-round stoppage against Slater. Professional MMA record after the fight: 4–0.

items.label: WIN · Leandro Souza · UFL 3: Ultimate Fight League 3
items.detail: Defeated Leandro Souza by TKO (head kick and punches) at UFL 3: Ultimate Fight League 3, Round 1 (4:03). Wins the inaugural Ultimate Fight League lightweight championship in Musselburgh, Scotland. A head kick floors Souza and punches close the fight. Professional MMA record after the fight: 5–0.

items.label: WIN · Mateusz Piskorz · Bellator 240: McCourt vs. Ruis
items.detail: Defeated Mateusz Piskorz by TKO (punches) at Bellator 240: McCourt vs. Ruis, Round 2 (2:43). Stops Piskorz in the second round at Bellator's Dublin event. Professional MMA record after the fight: 6–0.

items.label: WIN · Iamik Furtado · Bellator 247: Jackson vs. Kielholtz
items.detail: Defeated Iamik Furtado by TKO (punches) at Bellator 247: Jackson vs. Kielholtz, Round 2 (3:58). Stops Furtado in Milan, improving to 7–0 and completing his third Bellator win. Professional MMA record after the fight: 7–0.

Jim Miller.name: Jim Miller
Jim Miller.subtitle: Career chronology · East Coast regional titles, UFC record holder and 59 professional MMA bouts

items.label: Born in Sparta Township, New Jersey
items.detail: James Andrew Miller was born on August 30, 1983, and grew up in Sparta Township, New Jersey. He is the younger brother of former UFC middleweight Dan Miller.

items.label: Starts wrestling as a child
items.detail: Miller began wrestling at around age four. He later competed for Sparta High School and spent one year wrestling at Virginia Tech; the exact childhood start year is approximate.

items.label: Attends Virginia Tech and works in construction
items.detail: Miller studied at Virginia Tech but did not complete his degree. Before entering MMA, he worked in construction with his father and brother.

items.label: Begins mixed martial arts training
items.detail: Miller has said he began training MMA in May 2005 because he wanted to compete again after wrestling and was dissatisfied with a routine of work and home. His first professional bout followed in November.

items.label: Wins regional titles across multiple East Coast promotions
items.detail: Prior to his October 2008 UFC debut, Miller built an 11–1 professional record, competing with Reality Fighting, Cage Fury Fighting Championships, Ring of Combat, Battle Cage Xtreme and the IFL. The UFC credits him with five East Coast regional titles, without naming each sanctioned championship date.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · athlete Q&A and pre-UFC career

items.label: First loss comes against Frankie Edgar
items.detail: Miller loses his first professional fight at Reality Fighting 14 to unbeaten Frankie Edgar, a future UFC lightweight champion. He responds with six consecutive victories before joining the UFC.

items.label: Makes UFC debut against David Baron
items.detail: After going 11–1 on the regional circuit, Miller submits David Baron by rear-naked choke in round three at UFC 89, beginning what becomes a record-setting run in the promotion.

items.label: First landmark-numbered UFC appearance
items.detail: Miller defeats Mac Danzig by unanimous decision at UFC 100. Fifteen years later he becomes the only athlete to have competed at UFC 100, UFC 200 and UFC 300.

items.label: Wins seven consecutive fights inside the UFC
items.detail: After losing to Gray Maynard in March 2009, Miller beats Mac Danzig, Steve Lopez, Duane Ludwig, Mark Bocek, Gleison Tibau, Charles Oliveira and Kamal Shalorus before Benson Henderson ends the streak in August 2011.

items.label: Pat Healy bout overturned after positive drug test
items.detail: The New Jersey State Athletic Control Board changes the result of the UFC 159 fight from a submission loss to a no contest after Healy tests positive for marijuana metabolites. The result remains a no contest in Miller's career total.

items.label: Experiences undiagnosed Lyme disease symptoms
items.detail: Miller later said he believed he contracted Lyme disease around 2013 and suffered fatigue and other persistent symptoms while continuing to fight. This period is described retrospectively rather than treated as a precisely dated diagnosis.

items.label: Receives Lyme disease diagnosis and starts treatment
items.detail: Miller has said he learned he likely had Lyme disease just before his UFC 196 fight with Diego Sanchez. He received treatment and later explained he had been close to considering retirement from MMA.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · interview about March 2016 diagnosis

items.label: Competes at UFC 200 and defeats Takanori Gomi
items.detail: Stops Takanori Gomi in the first round at UFC 200. After starting Lyme disease treatment, Miller goes on to win three consecutive bouts in 2016, against Gomi, Joe Lauzon and Thiago Alves.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · milestones and second landmark card

items.label: Becomes the only UFC 100, 200 and 300 competitor
items.detail: Miller competes against King Green at UFC 300, becoming the only fighter to appear at UFC 100, UFC 200 and UFC 300. He loses a unanimous decision but establishes a unique longevity milestone.

items.label: Sets UFC records for total bouts and victories
items.detail: Miller holds the all-time UFC records for most appearances and most wins. His longevity, submission activity and finishes at lightweight also place him among the division's major record holders; these numbers continue changing as he competes.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · all-time records and fight history

items.label: Deals with serious pelvis-area injury
items.detail: Miller later disclosed that he injured the muscles attached to his pelvis and the pubic symphysis area before UFC 314. He fought Chase Hooper, then had an extended break to recover.

items.label: Steps away from competition amid son's cancer treatment
items.detail: During his own injury recovery, Miller focused on his family as his eldest son Wyatt underwent treatment for a rare childhood cancer. In April 2026, Miller reported that his son had been told there was no evidence of disease.

items.label: Earns 28th UFC win in 47th UFC bout
items.detail: Returns from a 13-month layoff to submit Jared Gordon with a first-round guillotine at UFC 328 in Newark, New Jersey. The victory extends his UFC records for wins and total appearances; it is his 18th lightweight finish.

items.label: UFC 334 · lightweight fight against Terrance McKinney
items.detail: Scheduled to face Terrance McKinney at Madison Square Garden, New York City, on November 14, 2026. Entering this future fight, Miller's completed professional record is 39–19–0 with one no contest. No result is assigned.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · official UFC 334 fight-card announcement

Terrance McKinney.name: Terrance McKinney
Terrance McKinney.subtitle: Career chronology · Washington wrestling titles, regional MMA, seven-second UFC debut and 27 professional bouts

items.label: Born in Chicago, Illinois
items.detail: Terrance Kitarius McKinney was born in Chicago and grew up in the Spokane, Washington, area. His mother helped support his wrestling development as a teenager.

items.label: Becomes two-time Washington state wrestling champion
items.detail: McKinney wrestled at Shadle Park High School in Spokane, won two Class 3A Washington state championships and received national recognition, including Fargo All-American honors. His exact individual title years are not established in the available athletic biography.
items.sourceLabel: Chadron State College · official athlete history

items.label: Wrestles at North Idaho College and Chadron State
items.detail: McKinney went 31–11 in his freshman season at North Idaho College, won the Spokane Open and Southern Oregon Open, and was later listed on Chadron State's 2014–15 roster. He also attended Notre Dame College during his collegiate wrestling years.

items.label: Survives drug-related medical emergency
items.detail: McKinney has publicly discussed a 2015 incident involving drug use in which he required emergency resuscitation. He later described recovery from that period as central to rebuilding his life and moving into MMA. This is a documented personal history, not a diagnosis or fight result.

items.label: Starts training in mixed martial arts
items.detail: After his collegiate wrestling career, McKinney began training MMA. He has said Michael Chiesa's success on The Ultimate Fighter was one of the motivations for pursuing the sport.

items.label: Wins early amateur MMA bout
items.detail: Knocks out Cadence Ross at King of the Cage: No Remorse in just fifteen seconds. This was an amateur fight and is not included in the professional record.

items.label: Begins professional run in CageSport
items.detail: Four consecutive submission victories on the CageSport circuit establish McKinney as a fast-starting featherweight prospect. His first professional loss comes through an injury in a rematch with Tyrone Henderson in July 2018.

items.label: Records first seven-second professional knockout
items.detail: McKinney stops Jeff Coleman in seven seconds at Conquest of the Cage. Two years later his UFC debut against Matt Frevola ends at precisely the same 0:07 mark.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · Conquest of the Cage result

items.label: First Contender Series opportunity ends in defeat
items.detail: After reaching 7–1, McKinney faces Sean Woodson on Dana White's Contender Series. A flying-knee stoppage in the second round prevents him from earning a UFC contract at that appearance.

items.label: Regroups before rapid 2021 knockout run
items.detail: Following losses to Sean Woodson and Darrick Minner in 2019, McKinney has no recorded professional bout in 2020. He returns with consecutive early stoppages against Dedrek Sanders, Luiz Antonio Lobo Gavinho and Michael Irizarry in 2021.

items.label: Sets fastest knockout record in UFC lightweight history
items.detail: Eight days after winning at LFA 109, McKinney accepts a short-notice UFC 263 bout with Matt Frevola. He wins in seven seconds, establishing the UFC lightweight division's fastest knockout record.

items.label: Hurts knee during post-fight celebration
items.detail: After beating Matt Frevola at UFC 263, McKinney jumps onto the cage and lands awkwardly during his celebration, hurting his knee. The incident occurs after the fight and does not affect the result.

items.label: Fares Ziam booking postponed
items.detail: A scheduled UFC Fight Night bout with Fares Ziam is withdrawn after a member of McKinney's corner tests positive for COVID-19. The matchup is rescheduled and McKinney wins it in February 2022.

items.label: Alternating finishes and setbacks in the UFC
items.detail: Following the seven-second debut, McKinney alternates short, often explosive wins with stoppage defeats. Results include victories over Fares Ziam, Erick Gonzalez, Mike Breeden and Brendon Marotte, and losses to Drew Dober, Ismael Bonfim, Nazim Sadykhov and Esteban Ribovics.

items.label: Moves training base to Florida
items.detail: McKinney relocated to the Orlando area and trained with Fusion Xcel Performance, speaking publicly about improving his consistency and approach to fighting. The exact relocation day is not verified.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · June 2025 training and career interview

items.label: All 18 professional victories came by stoppage
items.detail: As of October 27, 2026, his 18 victories comprise nine KO/TKOs and nine submissions, with no decision wins. His career record stands at 18–9 with eight UFC wins and six UFC defeats.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · updated professional finish breakdown

items.label: UFC 334 · lightweight bout against Jim Miller
items.detail: McKinney is scheduled to fight Jim Miller at Madison Square Garden in New York City on November 14, 2026, on the UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit card. He enters at 18–9 professionally after a July defeat to King Green. The future bout has no result assigned.

items.label: LOSS · Sean Woodson · Dana White's Contender Series 2019, Week 5
items.detail: Lost to Sean Woodson by TKO (flying knee) at Dana White's Contender Series 2019, Week 5, Round 2 (1:49). In his first Contender Series appearance, is stopped by Woodson's flying knee in the second round; does not receive a UFC contract. Professional record afterward: 7–2–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Darrick Minner · Midwest Championship Fighting 18
items.detail: Lost to Darrick Minner by Submission (triangle choke) at Midwest Championship Fighting 18, Round 1 (0:57). Falls by first-round triangle choke, leaving his record at 7–3. Professional record afterward: 7–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Dedrek Sanders · Strike Hard Productions 59
items.detail: Defeated Dedrek Sanders by TKO (strikes) at Strike Hard Productions 59, Round 1 (0:16). Returns after an extended period without a recorded professional bout and scores a 16-second stoppage. Professional record afterward: 8–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Luiz Antonio Lobo Gavinho · LFA 106: Silveira vs. Viana
items.detail: Defeated Luiz Antonio Lobo Gavinho by KO (head kick) at LFA 106: Silveira vs. Viana, Round 1 (0:17). Scores a 17-second head-kick knockout during his first LFA appearance. Professional record afterward: 9–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Michael Irizarry · LFA 109: McKinney vs. Irizarry
items.detail: Defeated Michael Irizarry by TKO (punches) at LFA 109: McKinney vs. Irizarry, Round 1 (1:12). Wins the LFA headliner by first-round punches, just eight days before his short-notice UFC debut. Professional record afterward: 10–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Matt Frevola · UFC 263: Adesanya vs. Vettori 2
items.detail: Defeated Matt Frevola by TKO (cross and ground strikes) at UFC 263: Adesanya vs. Vettori 2, Round 1 (0:07). Makes his short-notice UFC debut and stops Frevola in seven seconds, the fastest knockout in UFC lightweight history. Injures his knee during the celebration afterward. Professional record afterward: 11–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: MMA Fighting · UFC 263 seven-second debut report

items.label: WIN · Fares Ziam · UFC Fight Night 202: Makhachev vs. Green
items.detail: Defeated Fares Ziam by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC Fight Night 202: Makhachev vs. Green, Round 1 (2:11). Submits Ziam in the opening round after their original November 2021 booking was postponed. Professional record afterward: 12–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Drew Dober · UFC Fight Night 203: Santos vs. Ankalaev
items.detail: Lost to Drew Dober by TKO (knee and ground strikes) at UFC Fight Night 203: Santos vs. Ankalaev, Round 1 (3:17). Drops and pressures Dober early, but Dober recovers and finishes him with a knee and follow-up punches. Professional record afterward: 12–4–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Erick Gonzalez · UFC on ESPN 40: Santos vs. Hill
items.detail: Defeated Erick Gonzalez by Submission (standing rear-naked choke) at UFC on ESPN 40: Santos vs. Hill, Round 1 (2:17). Returns from the Dober loss with a standing rear-naked-choke finish. Professional record afterward: 13–4–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Ismael Bonfim · UFC 283: Teixeira vs. Hill
items.detail: Lost to Ismael Bonfim by TKO (flying knee) at UFC 283: Teixeira vs. Hill, Round 2 (2:17). Is knocked out by a flying knee in round two in Rio de Janeiro. Professional record afterward: 13–5–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Nazim Sadykhov · UFC on ESPN 49: Holm vs. Bueno Silva
items.detail: Lost to Nazim Sadykhov by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC on ESPN 49: Holm vs. Bueno Silva, Round 2 (1:07). Sadykhov wins by rear-naked choke in the second round; McKinney suffers consecutive defeats. Professional record afterward: 13–6–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Mike Breeden · UFC on ESPN 51: Luque vs. dos Anjos
items.detail: Defeated Mike Breeden by TKO (punches) at UFC on ESPN 51: Luque vs. dos Anjos, Round 1 (1:25). Stops Breeden in round one to end his two-fight losing streak. Professional record afterward: 14–6–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Brendon Marotte · UFC Fight Night 230: Yusuff vs. Barboza
items.detail: Defeated Brendon Marotte by TKO (knee and ground strikes) at UFC Fight Night 230: Yusuff vs. Barboza, Round 1 (0:20). Finishes Marotte in 20 seconds for his second consecutive first-round stoppage. Professional record afterward: 15–6–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Esteban Ribovics · UFC on ESPN 56: Lewis vs. Nascimento
items.detail: Lost to Esteban Ribovics by TKO (head kick) at UFC on ESPN 56: Lewis vs. Nascimento, Round 1 (0:37). Suffers a head-kick knockout loss in St. Louis. The 0:37 time is listed by Tapology and Verdict. Professional record afterward: 15–7–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Damir Hadžović · UFC Fight Night 250: Adesanya vs. Imavov
items.detail: Defeated Damir Hadžović by TKO (punches from back mount) at UFC Fight Night 250: Adesanya vs. Imavov, Round 1 (2:01). Opens 2025 with first-round ground strikes leading to a stoppage. Professional record afterward: 16–7–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Viacheslav Borshchev · UFC 317: Topuria vs. Oliveira
items.detail: Defeated Viacheslav Borshchev by Submission (mounted guillotine choke) at UFC 317: Topuria vs. Oliveira, Round 1 (0:55). Secures a mounted guillotine inside a minute for his second win of 2025. Professional record afterward: 17–7–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · Chris Duncan · UFC 323: Dvalishvili vs. Yan 2
items.detail: Lost to Chris Duncan by Submission (anaconda choke) at UFC 323: Dvalishvili vs. Yan 2, Round 1 (2:30). Duncan catches him in a first-round anaconda choke, ending his two-fight winning streak. Professional record afterward: 17–8–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: WIN · Kyle Nelson · UFC Fight Night 271: Adesanya vs. Pyfer
items.detail: Defeated Kyle Nelson by TKO (head kick and hammerfists) at UFC Fight Night 271: Adesanya vs. Pyfer, Round 1 (0:24). Stops Nelson in 24 seconds in Seattle, returning to winning form. Professional record afterward: 18–8–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

items.label: LOSS · King Green · UFC 329: McGregor vs. Holloway 2
items.detail: Lost to King Green by TKO (body shot and ground strikes) at UFC 329: McGregor vs. Holloway 2, Round 1 (4:59). Controls much of the opening round before Green hurts him with a late body shot and forces the stoppage with one second remaining. Professional record afterward: 18–9–0.
items.sourceLabel: Verdict MMA · opponent, promotion, method, round and time

Macy Chiasson.name: Macy Chiasson
Macy Chiasson.subtitle: Career chronology · New Orleans roots, TUF 28 featherweight champion and UFC bantamweight career

items.label: Born in New Orleans, Louisiana
items.detail: Macy Michelle Chiasson was born on July 27, 1991, and grew up in New Orleans, Louisiana, where she later began her martial arts training.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · date of birth and hometown

items.label: Starts Krav Maga training
items.detail: While studying at the University of New Orleans, Chiasson discovered a Krav Maga self-defense gym and began training. She later began following MMA and Invicta FC and decided to pursue fighting seriously.

items.label: Graduates from University of New Orleans and teaches Krav Maga
items.detail: Chiasson earned a bachelor's degree in biological sciences and undertook civil engineering studies at the University of New Orleans. She worked as an instructor at Triumph Krav Maga during and after college. Her exact graduation year is not stated in the UFC biography.

items.label: Wins Louisiana amateur MMA championship
items.detail: Before her professional debut, Chiasson won the Renaissance MMA Louisiana amateur title at 155 pounds, and has described an unbeaten amateur boxing and kickboxing record. Specific dates for those amateur championships are not documented in her UFC Q&A.

items.label: Faces Felicia Spencer in amateur MMA
items.detail: Chiasson loses a three-round amateur decision to future UFC featherweight Felicia Spencer at Renaissance MMA 31. This is an amateur contest and does not affect her professional record.

items.label: Moves to Dallas and trains at Fortis MMA
items.detail: Chiasson leaves New Orleans to train with a deeper professional fight team at Fortis MMA in Dallas, working to improve her full MMA game. The exact date of her move is not established in the available interview.

items.label: TUF 28 quarterfinal · finishes Larissa Pacheco
items.detail: On Team Kelvin Gastelum, Chiasson defeats experienced Brazilian Larissa Pacheco by first-round TKO (punches) at 3:48 during The Ultimate Fighter 28. This house bout is officially an exhibition, not a professional fight.

items.label: TUF 28 semifinal · finishes Leah Letson
items.detail: Chiasson stops Leah Letson with a body knee in Round 1 at 3:04, advancing to the featherweight final against Pannie Kianzad. This house bout is categorized as an exhibition.

items.label: Wins The Ultimate Fighter 28 women's featherweight tournament
items.detail: Submits Pannie Kianzad by rear-naked choke in the second round to win the TUF 28 featherweight tournament. Unlike the two filmed house fights, this finale contest counts toward her official professional MMA record.

items.label: Drops from featherweight to bantamweight
items.detail: After winning the TUF featherweight tournament, Chiasson moves to the 135-pound bantamweight division for her UFC 235 bout with Gina Mazany. She stops Mazany in the first round.

items.label: Suffers rare upkick-to-body knockout
items.detail: Chiasson loses to Irene Aldana at UFC 279 when Aldana lands an upkick to the liver from the bottom position. The official stoppage is Round 3 at 2:21; it is a KO defeat, not a submission or injury-related no contest.
items.sourceLabel: Sherdog · UFC 279 official result and play-by-play

items.label: Misses all of 2023 and returns after 18 months
items.detail: Following UFC 279, Chiasson does not compete professionally during 2023. She returns in March 2024 against Pannie Kianzad, whom she also faced in the 2018 TUF final. No specific unverified reason is assigned to the entire layoff.

items.label: Wins Performance of the Night in Kianzad rematch
items.detail: Chiasson submits Pannie Kianzad by rear-naked choke in Round 1 at UFC Fight Night: Tuivasa vs. Tybura and receives Performance of the Night. This starts a two-fight finishing streak.

items.label: Stops former title challenger Mayra Bueno Silva
items.detail: A grounded elbow cuts former UFC bantamweight title challenger Mayra Bueno Silva over the eye and prompts a second-round doctor stoppage at UFC 303. Chiasson receives another Performance of the Night bonus.

items.label: Vieira fight moved to featherweight after opponent's weight issue
items.detail: Ketlen Vieira weighs 146 pounds before their scheduled bantamweight fight while Chiasson weighs 144. The bout proceeds at featherweight, with Vieira forfeiting 25 percent of her purse. They compete the following day.

items.label: Misses bantamweight limit before Yana Santos bout
items.detail: Chiasson weighs 137.5 pounds, 1.5 over the 136-pound non-title bantamweight limit. She forfeits 25 percent of her purse and the UFC 320 fight proceeds at a catchweight the following day.

items.label: Third successive decision loss
items.detail: After decisions against Ketlen Vieira and Yana Santos during 2025, Chiasson loses to Ailín Pérez at UFC Fight Night: Moreno vs. Kavanagh. Her record stands at 10–6 entering the scheduled UFC 334 fight.

items.label: UFC 334 · women's bantamweight fight vs. Bia Mesquita
items.detail: Scheduled to face undefeated Brazilian jiu-jitsu specialist Bia Mesquita at Madison Square Garden, New York, on UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit. As of October 27, 2026 this is a future fight and no result has been assigned.

items.label: WIN · Miranda Dearing · In Ya Face: Caged Warrior Championship 16
items.detail: Defeated Miranda Dearing by Submission (armbar) at In Ya Face: Caged Warrior Championship 16, Round 3 (1:38). Makes her professional MMA debut at featherweight, finishing Dearing with an armbar in the third round. Professional record afterward: 1–0–0.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · regional and Invicta professional record

items.label: WIN · Allison Schmidt · Invicta FC 29: Kaufman vs. Lehner
items.detail: Defeated Allison Schmidt by Decision (unanimous) at Invicta FC 29: Kaufman vs. Lehner, Round 3 (5:00). Wins her Invicta FC debut by decision and improves to 2–0 before entering The Ultimate Fighter. Professional record afterward: 2–0–0.
items.sourceLabel: Tapology · regional and Invicta professional record

items.label: WIN · Pannie Kianzad · The Ultimate Fighter 28 Finale
items.detail: Defeated Pannie Kianzad by Submission (rear-naked choke) at The Ultimate Fighter 28 Finale, Round 2 (2:11). Wins the season's women's featherweight tournament final, earning the TUF 28 championship. The two preliminary house bouts were exhibitions and are not part of her professional record. Professional record afterward: 3–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Gina Mazany · UFC 235: Jones vs. Smith
items.detail: Defeated Gina Mazany by TKO (strikes) at UFC 235: Jones vs. Smith, Round 1 (1:49). Drops from featherweight to bantamweight and earns a first-round stoppage in her first UFC bout at 135 pounds. Professional record afterward: 4–0–0.

items.label: WIN · Sarah Moras · UFC Fight Night: Iaquinta vs. Cowboy
items.detail: Defeated Sarah Moras by TKO (strikes) at UFC Fight Night: Iaquinta vs. Cowboy, Round 2 (2:22). Stops Moras in the second round to extend her professional unbeaten streak to five. Professional record afterward: 5–0–0.

items.label: LOSS · Lina Länsberg · UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Cannonier
items.detail: Lost to Lina Länsberg by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night: Hermansson vs. Cannonier, Round 3 (5:00). Suffers her first professional defeat after Länsberg wins a three-round decision in Copenhagen. Professional record afterward: 5–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Shanna Young · UFC Fight Night: Anderson vs. Błachowicz 2
items.detail: Defeated Shanna Young by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night: Anderson vs. Błachowicz 2, Round 3 (5:00). Returns from her first loss with a decision over short-notice opponent Young in Rio Rancho. Professional record afterward: 6–1–0.

items.label: WIN · Marion Reneau · UFC on ESPN: Brunson vs. Holland
items.detail: Defeated Marion Reneau by Decision (unanimous) at UFC on ESPN: Brunson vs. Holland, Round 3 (5:00). Defeats the veteran Reneau by unanimous decision for a second consecutive win. Professional record afterward: 7–1–0.

items.label: LOSS · Raquel Pennington · UFC Fight Night: Lewis vs. Daukaus
items.detail: Lost to Raquel Pennington by Submission (guillotine choke) at UFC Fight Night: Lewis vs. Daukaus, Round 2 (3:07). Pennington catches a guillotine during the second round and hands Chiasson her first professional submission loss. Professional record afterward: 7–2–0.

items.label: WIN · Norma Dumont · UFC 274: Oliveira vs. Gaethje
items.detail: Defeated Norma Dumont by Decision (split) at UFC 274: Oliveira vs. Gaethje, Round 3 (5:00). Wins a closely contested split decision over Dumont in a women's featherweight bout. Professional record afterward: 8–2–0.

items.label: LOSS · Irene Aldana · UFC 279: Diaz vs. Ferguson
items.detail: Lost to Irene Aldana by KO (upkick to body) at UFC 279: Diaz vs. Ferguson, Round 3 (2:21). Aldana lands an upkick to the liver from her back, producing an unusual third-round body-shot knockout. Professional record afterward: 8–3–0.

items.label: WIN · Pannie Kianzad · UFC Fight Night: Tuivasa vs. Tybura
items.detail: Defeated Pannie Kianzad by Submission (rear-naked choke) at UFC Fight Night: Tuivasa vs. Tybura, Round 1 (3:54). Returns after approximately 18 months away from UFC competition and submits the opponent she had beaten in the 2018 TUF final. Earns Performance of the Night. Professional record afterward: 9–3–0.

items.label: WIN · Mayra Bueno Silva · UFC 303: Pereira vs. Procházka 2
items.detail: Defeated Mayra Bueno Silva by TKO (doctor stoppage) at UFC 303: Pereira vs. Procházka 2, Round 2 (1:58). Opens a deep cut over Silva's right eye with a ground elbow; a ringside doctor advises stopping the bout. Earns Performance of the Night. Professional record afterward: 10–3–0.
items.sourceLabel: UFC · official UFC 303 result and doctor stoppage

items.label: LOSS · Ketlen Vieira · UFC Fight Night: Gamrot vs. Klein
items.detail: Lost to Ketlen Vieira by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night: Gamrot vs. Klein, Round 3 (5:00). Originally a bantamweight matchup, the contest moves to featherweight after Vieira's weight-management issue; Vieira wins by decision in Las Vegas. Professional record afterward: 10–4–0.

items.label: LOSS · Yana Santos · UFC 320: Ankalaev vs. Pereira 2
items.detail: Lost to Yana Santos by Decision (unanimous) at UFC 320: Ankalaev vs. Pereira 2, Round 3 (5:00). Loses a decision after missing the bantamweight limit by 1.5 pounds and forfeiting a portion of her purse. Professional record afterward: 10–5–0.

items.label: LOSS · Ailín Pérez · UFC Fight Night: Moreno vs. Kavanagh
items.detail: Lost to Ailín Pérez by Decision (unanimous) at UFC Fight Night: Moreno vs. Kavanagh, Round 3 (5:00). Drops a decision in Mexico City, extending her losing streak to three entering her next scheduled appearance. Professional record afterward: 10–6–0.
